questions.e: Sum of roots = −b/a = −(−6)/3 = 2. The value 2/3 is c/a, the product of the roots, not the sum.

questions.s: The roots of 4x² − 12x + 9 = 0 are
questions.e: Discriminant = (−12)² − 4(4)(9) = 144 − 144 = 0, so the roots are real and equal; indeed 4x² − 12x + 9 = (2x − 3)², giving x = 3/2 twice. Distinct roots would need a positive discriminant.

questions.s: The quadratic equation whose roots are 2 + √3 and 2 − √3 is
questions.e: Sum of roots = 4 and product = (2 + √3)(2 − √3) = 4 − 3 = 1, so the equation is x² − (sum)x + product = x² − 4x + 1 = 0. The option with +7 adds 3 instead of subtracting it in the product, and x² + 4x + 1 = 0 has the wrong sign for the sum.

questions.s: If α and β are the roots of x² − 3x + 1 = 0, then α² + β² equals
questions.e: α + β = 3 and αβ = 1, so α² + β² = (α + β)² − 2αβ = 9 − 2 = 7. The value 11 comes from adding 2αβ instead of subtracting it.

questions.s: The solution set of x⁴ − 5x² + 4 = 0 is
questions.e: Put y = x²: y² − 5y + 4 = 0 gives y = 1 or 4, so x² = 1 or x² = 4 and x = ±1, ±2. The set {1, 4} gives the values of x², not of x, and {1, 2} misses the negative roots.

questions.s: If 2ˣ⁺¹ = 32, then x equals
questions.e: 32 = 2⁵, so x + 1 = 5 and x = 4. Choosing 5 forgets to subtract 1 from the exponent.

questions.s: The solution set of √(x + 7) = x − 5 is
questions.e: Squaring gives x + 7 = x² − 10x + 25, so x² − 11x + 18 = 0 and x = 2 or 9. Check: x = 9 gives √16 = 4 = 9 − 5, true; x = 2 gives √9 = 3 but 2 − 5 = −3, so 2 is extraneous. Keeping both values ignores the check that squaring makes necessary.

questions.s: The remainder when x³ − 2x² + 4x − 5 is divided by x − 2 is
questions.e: By the remainder theorem the remainder is P(2) = 8 − 8 + 8 − 5 = 3. The value −29 is P(−2), which would be the remainder on division by x + 2.

questions.s: If x + 2 is a factor of x³ + kx² + x − 6, then k equals
questions.e: By the factor theorem P(−2) = 0: −8 + 4k − 2 − 6 = 0, so 4k = 16 and k = 4. Substituting x = 2 instead gives 8 + 4k + 2 − 6 = 0, i.e. k = −1, which is the condition for x − 2 to be a factor.

questions.s: When 2x³ − 3x² + 5 is divided by x − 1 using synthetic division, the quotient and remainder are
questions.e: Write the coefficients 2, −3, 0, 5 (the missing x term needs a 0) and use 1: 2; −3 + 2 = −1; 0 − 1 = −1; 5 − 1 = 4. So the quotient is 2x² − x − 1 and the remainder 4. Using −1 instead of 1 gives 2x² − 5x + 5 with remainder 0, which is division by x + 1.
5x + 1 = A(x + 2) + B(x − 1). Put x = 1: 6 = 3A, so A = 2. Put x = −2: −9 = −3B, so B = 3. Swapping the values (A = 3, B = 2) still gives A + B = 5 but fails the check at x = 1.

questions.s: If (x² + 1)/(x(x − 1)²) = A/x + B/(x − 1) + C/(x − 1)², then
questions.e: x² + 1 = A(x − 1)² + Bx(x − 1) + Cx. Put x = 0: A = 1. Put x = 1: C = 2. Comparing x² coefficients: 1 = A + B, so B = 0. Taking B = 1 comes from equating B to the x² coefficient alone and forgetting A also contributes x².

questions.s: The partial fractions of 1/(x(x² + 1)) are
questions.e: Write 1 = A(x² + 1) + (Bx + C)x. Put x = 0: A = 1. The x² coefficient gives 0 = A + B, so B = −1, and the x coefficient gives C = 0. Hence 1/x − x/(x² + 1); the plus sign would give (2x² + 1)/(x(x² + 1)) on recombining.

questions.s: For ax² + bx + c = 0 with a, b, c rational, the roots are real, unequal and irrational when the discriminant is
o: positive but not a perfect square
questions.e: A positive discriminant gives two real unequal roots; they are irrational only when √(b² − 4ac) is irrational, i.e. the discriminant is not a perfect square. A positive perfect square gives rational roots.

questions.s: If α and β are the roots of x² − 4x + 2 = 0, then α³ + β³ equals
questions.e: α + β = 4 and αβ = 2. α³ + β³ = (α + β)³ − 3αβ(α + β) = 64 − 3(2)(4) = 64 − 24 = 40. The value 88 adds 24 instead of subtracting it, and 56 drops the factor 3.

questions.s: The roots of x² + kx + 9 = 0 are equal when k equals
questions.e: Equal roots need b² − 4ac = 0: k² − 36 = 0, so k = ±6. Choosing 6 only forgets that k = −6 also works, giving (x − 3)² = 0.

questions.s: The solution set of 4ˣ − 3·2ˣ⁺¹ + 8 = 0 is
questions.e: Let y = 2ˣ; then 4ˣ = y² and 3·2ˣ⁺¹ = 6y, so y² − 6y + 8 = 0 and y = 2 or 4. Then 2ˣ = 2 gives x = 1 and 2ˣ = 4 gives x = 2. The set {2, 4} gives the values of 2ˣ, not of x.

questions.s: The product of the roots of 5x² + 7x − 10 = 0 is
questions.e: Product of roots = c/a = −10/5 = −2. The value −7/5 is −b/a, which is the sum of the roots.

questions.s: The roots of x² − 2x − 4 = 0 are
questions.e: x = [2 ± √(4 + 16)]/2 = [2 ± √20]/2 = [2 ± 2√5]/2 = 1 ± √5. The pair −1 ± √5 uses +b instead of −b in the quadratic formula.

questions.s: If the discriminant of a quadratic equation with real coefficients is negative, its roots are
questions.e: With b² − 4ac < 0 the square root in the formula is imaginary, giving roots p ± iq, a conjugate pair. A real quadratic can never have exactly one real and one complex root, because complex roots occur in conjugate pairs.

questions.s: If one root of x² − 7x + k = 0 is 3, then k equals
questions.e: The sum of the roots is 7, so the other root is 7 − 3 = 4, and k = product = 3 × 4 = 12. Check: 9 − 21 + 12 = 0. The value 21 multiplies the known root by the sum instead of by the other root.

questions.s: If α and β are the roots of x² − 5x + 3 = 0, the equation whose roots are 2α and 2β is
questions.e: New sum = 2(α + β) = 10 and new product = 4αβ = 12, so the equation is x² − 10x + 12 = 0. Doubling the product instead of multiplying it by 4 gives the wrong constant 6.

questions.s: If α and β are the roots of x² − 6x + 4 = 0, then 1/α + 1/β equals
questions.e: 1/α + 1/β = (α + β)/(αβ) = 6/4 = 3/2. The value 2/3 inverts the fraction, giving αβ/(α + β).

questions.s: The solution set of (x² + x)² − 8(x² + x) + 12 = 0 is
questions.e: Let y = x² + x: y² − 8y + 12 = 0, so y = 2 or 6. Then x² + x − 2 = 0 gives x = 1, −2, and x² + x − 6 = 0 gives x = 2, −3. The set {2, 6} lists the values of y, not of x.

questions.s: If 3²ˣ⁻¹ = 27, then x equals
questions.e: 27 = 3³, so 2x − 1 = 3 and x = 2. The value 3/2 comes from dropping the −1 and solving 2x = 3.

questions.s: The solution set of √(2x + 1) + 1 = x is
questions.e: √(2x + 1) = x − 1; squaring gives 2x + 1 = x² − 2x + 1, so x² − 4x = 0 and x = 0 or 4. Check: x = 4 gives 3 + 1 = 4, true; x = 0 gives 1 + 1 = 2 ≠ 0, so 0 is extraneous. The set {0, 4} skips this check.

questions.s: The remainder when x⁴ + 3x − 1 is divided by x + 1 is
questions.e: Remainder = P(−1) = 1 − 3 − 1 = −3. Using x = 1 instead gives 1 + 3 − 1 = 3, which is the remainder on division by x − 1.

questions.s: If x − 1 and x + 2 are both factors of x³ + ax² + bx − 6, then
questions.e: P(1) = 0 gives 1 + a + b − 6 = 0, so a + b = 5. P(−2) = 0 gives −8 + 4a − 2b − 6 = 0, so 2a − b = 7. Adding, 3a = 12, a = 4 and b = 1; indeed x³ + 4x² + x − 6 = (x − 1)(x + 2)(x + 3). The pair a = 1, b = 4 also has a + b = 5 but fails P(−2) = 0.

questions.s: Synthetic division of x³ − 7x + 6 by x + 3 gives the quotient
questions.e: Use −3 with coefficients 1, 0, −7, 6: 1; 0 − 3 = −3; −7 + 9 = 2; 6 − 6 = 0. The quotient is x² − 3x + 2 with remainder 0. Using +3 gives x² + 3x + 2 with remainder 12, and leaving out the 0 for the missing x² term gives the wrong-degree quotient x − 10.

questions.s: The correct form of partial fractions for (3x + 2)/((x − 1)(x² + 4)) is
questions.e: A linear factor takes a constant numerator and an irreducible quadratic factor x² + 4 takes a linear numerator Bx + C. A constant B alone over x² + 4 cannot match every numerator, so A/(x − 1) + B/(x² + 4) is incomplete.

questions.s: In the partial fractions of 1/((x − 1)(x − 2)(x − 3)), the coefficient of 1/(x − 2) is
questions.e: Cover up x − 2 and put x = 2 in the rest: 1/((2 − 1)(2 − 3)) = 1/(1 × −1) = −1. The value 1/2 is the coefficient of 1/(x − 1) (and of 1/(x − 3)), not of 1/(x − 2).

questions.s: (x² + 1)/(x² − 1) resolved into partial fractions is
questions.e: The fraction is improper, so divide first: (x² + 1)/(x² − 1) = 1 + 2/(x² − 1). Then 2/((x − 1)(x + 1)) = 1/(x − 1) − 1/(x + 1). Leaving out the 1 from the division gives 1/(x − 1) − 1/(x + 1), which equals only 2/(x² − 1).

questions.s: The equation x² − 4x + k = 0 has real roots if and only if
questions.e: Real roots need b² − 4ac ≥ 0: 16 − 4k ≥ 0, so k ≤ 4. The condition k < 4 gives only real distinct roots and wrongly excludes k = 4, where the roots are equal (x = 2, 2).

questions.s: The quadratic equation whose roots are −3 and 5 is
questions.e: Sum = 2 and product = −15, so x² − (sum)x + product = x² − 2x − 15 = 0. The option x² + 2x − 15 = 0 has the roots 3 and −5, because it uses +sum for the x coefficient.

questions.s: If α and β are the roots of 2x² − 5x + 1 = 0, then α/β + β/α equals
questions.e: α + β = 5/2 and αβ = 1/2. α² + β² = 25/4 − 2(1/2) = 21/4, so α/β + β/α = (α² + β²)/(αβ) = (21/4) ÷ (1/2) = 21/2. The value 21/4 forgets to divide by αβ.

questions.s: If 2ˣ · 4ˣ = 64, then x equals
questions.e: 2ˣ · 4ˣ = 2ˣ · 2²ˣ = 2³ˣ and 64 = 2⁶, so 3x = 6 and x = 2. The value 3 treats 2ˣ · 4ˣ as 8ˣ correctly but then wrongly takes 8³ = 64; in fact 8² = 64.

questions.s: When x³ + ax − 4 is divided by x − 2 the remainder is 10. The value of a is
questions.e: By the remainder theorem P(2) = 8 + 2a − 4 = 10, so 2a = 6 and a = 3. Dropping the constant −4 gives 8 + 2a = 10 and the wrong value a = 1.

questions.s: The solution of √(x + 5) + √x = 5 is
questions.e: Write √(x + 5) = 5 − √x and square: x + 5 = 25 − 10√x + x, so 10√x = 20, √x = 2 and x = 4. Check: √9 + √4 = 3 + 2 = 5. x = 16 would give √21 + 4, which is not 5.

questions.s: The roots of x² + px + q = 0 are equal in magnitude but opposite in sign when
questions.e: Roots r and −r have sum 0, and the sum is −p, so p = 0 (with q < 0 for real roots). The condition q = 0 instead makes one root zero.

questions.s: If the roots of 2x² − 5x + k = 0 are reciprocals of each other, then k equals
questions.e: Reciprocal roots α and 1/α have product 1, and the product is k/2, so k = 2. Choosing k = 1 sets c = 1 without dividing by a = 2.

questions.s: If one root of x² − 6x + k = 0 is double the other, then k equals
questions.e: Let the roots be a and 2a. Then 3a = 6, so a = 2, the roots are 2 and 4, and k = 2 × 4 = 8. The value 9 gives equal roots 3 and 3, not one double the other.

questions.s: By completing the square, x² − 6x + 2 = 0 can be written as
questions.e: x² − 6x = −2; add (6/2)² = 9 to both sides: x² − 6x + 9 = 7, so (x − 3)² = 7. The form (x − 3)² = 11 moves the constant across without changing its sign (x² − 6x = 2), and (x + 3)² has the wrong sign inside the bracket.

questions.s: The product of two consecutive positive integers is 132. The smaller integer is
questions.e: n(n + 1) = 132 gives n² + n − 132 = 0 = (n + 12)(n − 11), so n = 11 (the positive root) and the integers are 11 and 12. The value 12 is the larger integer.

questions.s: The equation x² − 2(k + 1)x + k² = 0 has equal roots when k equals
questions.e: Equal roots need b² − 4ac = 4(k + 1)² − 4k² = 0, i.e. 2k + 1 = 0, so k = −1/2. Writing (k + 1)² as k² + 1 makes the k² terms cancel wrongly and loses the 2k term.

questions.s: The solution set of x + 1/x = 5/2 (x ≠ 0) is
questions.e: Multiply by 2x: 2x² + 2 = 5x, so 2x² − 5x + 2 = 0 = (2x − 1)(x − 2) and x = 2 or 1/2. The negatives −2 and −1/2 satisfy x + 1/x = −5/2, not +5/2.

questions.s: The solution set of 9ˣ − 4·3ˣ + 3 = 0 is
questions.e: Let y = 3ˣ so 9ˣ = y²: y² − 4y + 3 = 0 gives y = 1 or 3. Then 3ˣ = 1 gives x = 0 and 3ˣ = 3 gives x = 1. The set {1, 3} lists the values of 3ˣ, not of x.

questions.s: The solution set of 2ˣ + 2²⁻ˣ = 5 is
questions.e: 2²⁻ˣ = 4/2ˣ. With y = 2ˣ: y + 4/y = 5, so y² − 5y + 4 = 0 and y = 1 or 4. Hence 2ˣ = 1 gives x = 0 and 2ˣ = 4 gives x = 2. The set {1, 4} stops at the values of y.

questions.s: The number of real solutions of √(3x − 2) = x − 2 is
questions.e: Squaring: 3x − 2 = x² − 4x + 4, so x² − 7x + 6 = 0 and x = 1 or 6. x = 6 gives √16 = 4 = 6 − 2, true; x = 1 gives √1 = 1 but 1 − 2 = −1, so it is extraneous. Only one solution remains; answering 2 counts the extraneous root.

questions.s: The solution set of √(x² + 9) = 5 is
questions.e: Squaring gives x² + 9 = 25, so x² = 16 and x = ±4; both check, since (−4)² + 9 = 25 too. Rejecting −4 is a mistake: the right side 5 is positive whatever the sign of x.

questions.s: The remainder when 4x³ − 2x² + 3x − 1 is divided by 2x − 1 is
questions.e: 2x − 1 = 0 gives x = 1/2, so the remainder is P(1/2) = 4(1/8) − 2(1/4) + 3(1/2) − 1 = 1/2 − 1/2 + 3/2 − 1 = 1/2. The value 4 is P(1), obtained by treating the divisor as x − 1.

questions.s: Which of the following is a factor of x³ − 6x² + 11x − 6?
questions.e: P(3) = 27 − 54 + 33 − 6 = 0, so x − 3 is a factor; in fact the polynomial is (x − 1)(x − 2)(x − 3). For x + 1, P(−1) = −1 − 6 − 11 − 6 = −24 ≠ 0.

questions.s: Synthetic division of x⁴ − 3x³ + 2x − 5 by x − 2 gives the quotient
questions.e: Coefficients 1, −3, 0, 2, −5 (0 for the missing x²) with 2: 1; −3 + 2 = −1; 0 − 2 = −2; 2 − 4 = −2; −5 − 4 = −9. Quotient x³ − x² − 2x − 2, remainder −9. Using −2 instead gives x³ − 5x² + 10x − 18, and omitting the 0 gives a quotient of the wrong degree.

questions.s: (3x − 1)/(x² − x) expressed in partial fractions is
questions.e: x² − x = x(x − 1), and 3x − 1 = A(x − 1) + Bx. Put x = 0: −1 = −A, so A = 1. Put x = 1: 2 = B. Taking A = −1 forgets that the factor (x − 1) is also −1 at x = 0.

questions.s: If (x + 5)/((x − 1)(x + 1)²) = A/(x − 1) + B/(x + 1) + C/(x + 1)², then B equals
questions.e: x + 5 = A(x + 1)² + B(x − 1)(x + 1) + C(x − 1). Put x = 1: 6 = 4A, A = 3/2. Put x = −1: 4 = −2C, C = −2. The x² coefficients give 0 = A + B, so B = −3/2. The value −2 is C, the coefficient of the squared factor.

questions.s: (2x² + x + 3)/((x + 1)(x² + 1)) expressed in partial fractions is
questions.e: 2x² + x + 3 = A(x² + 1) + (Bx + C)(x + 1). Put x = −1: 4 = 2A, A = 2. x² terms: 2 = A + B, so B = 0; constants: 3 = A + C, so C = 1. Hence 2/(x + 1) + 1/(x² + 1); the option with x/(x² + 1) wrongly assumes the quadratic part must contain x.

questions.s: A rational fraction P(x)/Q(x) is called proper when
o: degree of P(x) ≥ degree of Q(x)
P(x) and Q(x) have a common factor
degree of P(x) < degree of Q(x)
questions.e: A proper fraction has a numerator of lower degree than the denominator, e.g. (x + 1)/(x² + 3). When the degree of P(x) is greater than or equal to that of Q(x) the fraction is improper and must be divided out before resolving into partial fractions.

questions.s: If α and β are the roots of x² − 5x + 3 = 0, then (α − β)² equals
questions.e: (α − β)² = (α + β)² − 4αβ = 25 − 12 = 13. Using 2αβ instead of 4αβ gives 19, which is α² + β².

questions.s: The equations x² + 2x − 3 = 0 and x² + kx + 3 = 0 have a common root. The possible values of k are
questions.e: The first equation has roots 1 and −3. If x = 1 is common: 1 + k + 3 = 0, so k = −4. If x = −3 is common: 9 − 3k + 3 = 0, so k = 4. Answering −4 only checks just one of the two roots.

questions.s: The roots of 3x² − 5x − 2 = 0 are
questions.e: Split −5x using the product 3 × (−2) = −6: 3x² − 6x + x − 2 = (3x + 1)(x − 2), so x = 2 or −1/3. The pair −2 and 1/3 has both signs reversed; those are the roots of 3x² + 5x − 2 = 0.

questions.s: The equation kx² + 4x + 1 = 0 has equal roots when k equals
questions.e: Equal roots need b² − 4ac = 16 − 4k = 0, so k = 4, giving 4x² + 4x + 1 = (2x + 1)². Taking k = 16 comes from writing the condition as b² = k, forgetting the factor 4.

questions.s: The roots of x² − 6x + 7 = 0 are
questions.e: Discriminant = 36 − 28 = 8, which is positive but not a perfect square, so the roots 3 ± √2 are real, unequal and irrational. Rational roots would need a perfect-square discriminant such as 4 or 9.

questions.s: The equation x² + (k − 3)x + k = 0 has equal roots when k equals
questions.e: Equal roots: (k − 3)² − 4k = 0, i.e. k² − 10k + 9 = 0 = (k − 1)(k − 9), so k = 1 or 9. Check k = 1: x² − 2x + 1 = (x − 1)². The pair −1 or −9 comes from a sign slip when factorising.

questions.s: If α and β are the roots of x² − 4x + 2 = 0, the equation whose roots are α² and β² is
questions.e: α + β = 4 and αβ = 2. New sum α² + β² = 16 − 2(2) = 12; new product α²β² = 4. So x² − 12x + 4 = 0. Using (α + β)² = 16 as the new sum forgets to subtract 2αβ.

questions.s: If α and β are the roots of 2x² + 3x − 4 = 0, the equation whose roots are α + 1 and β + 1 is
questions.e: If y = x + 1 then x = y − 1: 2(y − 1)² + 3(y − 1) − 4 = 2y² − y − 5 = 0. Check: new sum = −3/2 + 2 = 1/2 and new product = αβ + (α + β) + 1 = −2 − 3/2 + 1 = −5/2. Substituting x + 1 instead of x − 1 gives 2x² + 7x + 1 = 0, whose roots are α − 1 and β − 1.

questions.s: If α and β are the roots of 2x² − 6x + 3 = 0, then α²β + αβ² equals
questions.e: α²β + αβ² = αβ(α + β) = (3/2)(3) = 9/2. Taking the sum as −3 (forgetting the minus in −b/a) gives −9/2.

questions.s: The real solutions of (x + 1)(x + 2)(x + 3)(x + 4) = 24 are
questions.e: Pair the factors: (x² + 5x + 4)(x² + 5x + 6) = 24. With y = x² + 5x: (y + 4)(y + 6) = 24, so y² + 10y = 0 and y = 0 or −10. x² + 5x = 0 gives x = 0, −5; x² + 5x + 10 = 0 has discriminant 25 − 40 < 0, so no real roots. The set {0, −10} lists values of y, not of x.

questions.s: The solution set of 5ˣ⁺¹ + 5¹⁻ˣ = 26 is
questions.e: Let y = 5ˣ: 5y + 5/y = 26, so 5y² − 26y + 5 = 0 = (5y − 1)(y − 5), giving y = 5 or 1/5. Then 5ˣ = 5 gives x = 1 and 5ˣ = 1/5 gives x = −1. The set {5, 1/5} gives the values of 5ˣ, not of x.

questions.s: The solution of x − √x − 2 = 0 is
questions.e: Let y = √x ≥ 0: y² − y − 2 = 0 = (y − 2)(y + 1), so y = 2 (y = −1 is rejected because √x cannot be negative). Then x = 4; check: 4 − 2 − 2 = 0. Accepting y = −1 gives x = 1, but 1 − 1 − 2 = −2 ≠ 0.

questions.s: P(x) = x³ + ax + b leaves remainder 3 when divided by x − 1 and remainder 5 when divided by x + 1. Then
questions.e: P(1) = 1 + a + b = 3 gives a + b = 2; P(−1) = −1 − a + b = 5 gives b − a = 6. Adding, 2b = 8 so b = 4 and a = −2. Check: P(1) = 1 − 2 + 4 = 3 and P(−1) = −1 + 2 + 4 = 5. Taking a = 2 gives P(1) = 7, not 3.

questions.s: x + a is a factor of xⁿ + aⁿ when the positive integer n is
questions.e: By the factor theorem put x = −a: (−a)ⁿ + aⁿ is 0 exactly when (−a)ⁿ = −aⁿ, i.e. n is odd. For even n it equals 2aⁿ ≠ 0 (a ≠ 0), e.g. x² + a² has no real linear factor.

questions.s: In the synthetic division of 3x³ + 2x² − 7x + 2 by x − 1, the bottom row of numbers is
questions.e: Bring down 3; 3 × 1 + 2 = 5; 5 × 1 − 7 = −2; −2 × 1 + 2 = 0. So the row is 3, 5, −2, 0: quotient 3x² + 5x − 2 and remainder 0, so x − 1 is a factor. The row 3, −1, −6, 8 uses −1, i.e. divides by x + 1.

questions.s: (x + 7)/(x² − x − 6) expressed in partial fractions is
questions.e: x² − x − 6 = (x − 3)(x + 2). x + 7 = A(x + 2) + B(x − 3); x = 3 gives 10 = 5A, A = 2; x = −2 gives 5 = −5B, B = −1. The last option uses (x + 3)(x − 2) = x² + x − 6, the wrong factorisation.

questions.s: 4x/(x − 1)² expressed in partial fractions is
questions.e: Write 4x = 4(x − 1) + 4, so 4x/(x − 1)² = 4/(x − 1) + 4/(x − 1)². With the minus sign the numerator would be 4(x − 1) − 4 = 4x − 8, not 4x.

questions.s: 1/(x²(x + 1)) expressed in partial fractions is
questions.e: 1 = Ax(x + 1) + B(x + 1) + Cx². x = 0 gives B = 1; x = −1 gives C = 1; the x² terms give 0 = A + C, so A = −1. Dropping the A/x term, as in 1/x² + 1/(x + 1), leaves a numerator x² + x + 1 instead of 1.

questions.s: (x² + 2)/(x(x² + 1)) expressed in partial fractions is
questions.e: x² + 2 = A(x² + 1) + (Bx + C)x. x = 0 gives A = 2; x² terms give 1 = A + B, so B = −1; x terms give C = 0. Hence 2/x − x/(x² + 1). The plus sign would recombine to (3x² + 2)/(x(x² + 1)).

questions.s: The number of unknown constants needed to resolve 1/((x − 1)³(x + 2)) into partial fractions is
questions.e: The form is A/(x − 1) + B/(x − 1)² + C/(x − 1)³ + D/(x + 2): three for the repeated factor (x − 1)³ and one for x + 2, four in all. Writing only 2 forgets that a repeated factor needs one term for each power.

questions.s: Ayesha's rectangular garden in Lahore is 3 m longer than it is wide and has an area of 40 m². Its width is
questions.e: w(w + 3) = 40 gives w² + 3w − 40 = 0 = (w + 8)(w − 5), so w = 5 m (the width cannot be −8). The value 8 m is the length, not the width.

questions.s: The sum of the roots of x² − (k + 2)x + 2k = 0 is 5. The product of its roots is
questions.e: Sum = k + 2 = 5 gives k = 3, so the product is 2k = 6; the equation is x² − 5x + 6 = 0 with roots 2 and 3. Answering 3 gives the value of k, not the product.

questions.s: Which of the following is a quadratic equation in x?
questions.e: (x − 1)(x + 1) = 2x gives x² − 2x − 1 = 0, of degree 2. In (x + 2)² = x² + 4 and x(x − 1) = x² + 5 the x² terms cancel, leaving linear equations, and x² + 1/x = 3 is not a polynomial equation.

questions.s: The roots of x² − px + 12 = 0 differ by 1 and p is positive. Then p equals
questions.e: Let the roots be r and r + 1 with r(r + 1) = 12, so r = 3 and the roots are 3 and 4. Then p = sum = 7. Using (α − β)² = p² − 48 = 1 also gives p² = 49, p = 7; the value 13 adds 12 and 1 instead.

questions.s: The equation whose roots are the reciprocals of the roots of 3x² − 5x + 2 = 0 is
questions.e: Replace x by 1/x and multiply by x²: 3 − 5x + 2x² = 0, i.e. 2x² − 5x + 3 = 0, whose roots 1 and 3/2 are the reciprocals of 1 and 2/3. Changing the sign of the middle term instead gives the equation with roots −α and −β.

questions.s: If α and β are the roots of 2x² + 3x − 7 = 0, the equation whose roots are −α and −β is
questions.e: Replace x by −x: 2x² − 3x − 7 = 0. The sum changes sign (from −3/2 to 3/2) but the product (−α)(−β) = αβ = −7/2 stays the same, so the constant must not change sign. Reversing the coefficients gives the equation for reciprocal roots instead.

questions.s: If α and β are the roots of x² − 2x − 1 = 0, then α⁴ + β⁴ equals
questions.e: α + β = 2, αβ = −1. α² + β² = 4 − 2(−1) = 6, and α⁴ + β⁴ = (α² + β²)² − 2(αβ)² = 36 − 2 = 34. The value 38 adds 2(αβ)² instead of subtracting it.

questions.s: If a and c have opposite signs in ax² + bx + c = 0 (a, b, c real), then the roots are always
questions.e: If ac < 0 then −4ac > 0, so b² − 4ac > 0 whatever b is, and the roots are real and unequal (with product c/a negative, one positive and one negative). They need not be rational: x² − 2 = 0 has roots ±√2.

questions.s: The product of all the roots of x⁴ − 13x² + 36 = 0 is
questions.e: With y = x²: y² − 13y + 36 = 0 gives y = 4 or 9, so x = ±2, ±3. The product is (2)(−2)(3)(−3) = (−4)(−9) = 36. The value 0 is the sum of the roots, not the product.

questions.s: The solution set of (∛x)² − 5∛x + 4 = 0 is
questions.e: Let y = ∛x: y² − 5y + 4 = 0, so y = 1 or 4. Then x = y³ = 1 or 64. The set {1, 16} squares y instead of cubing it, and {1, 4} stops at the values of y.

questions.s: The solution set of 2²ˣ⁺¹ − 9·2ˣ + 4 = 0 is
questions.e: 2²ˣ⁺¹ = 2·(2ˣ)². With y = 2ˣ: 2y² − 9y + 4 = 0 = (2y − 1)(y − 4), so y = 4 or 1/2. Then 2ˣ = 4 gives x = 2 and 2ˣ = 1/2 gives x = −1. The set {4, 1/2} gives the values of y.

questions.s: If 3ˣ⁺² − 3ˣ = 72, then x equals
questions.e: Take 3ˣ common: 3ˣ(3² − 1) = 8·3ˣ = 72, so 3ˣ = 9 and x = 2. Reading 3ˣ = 9 as x = 9/3 = 3 divides instead of finding the power: 3² = 9.

questions.s: The solution of √(x + 4) − √(x − 4) = 2 is
The solution set of √x + 6/√x = 5 is
questions.e: Let y = √x: y + 6/y = 5, so y² − 5y + 6 = 0 and y = 2 or 3. Then x = 4 or 9, and both check (2 + 3 = 5 and 3 + 2 = 5). The set {2, 3} gives the values of √x, not of x.

questions.s: The remainder when 3x⁵ − 2x³ + 7 is divided by x is
questions.e: Dividing by x − 0, the remainder is P(0) = 7, the constant term. The value 8 is P(1) = 3 − 2 + 7, the remainder on division by x − 1.

questions.s: If x − 3 is a factor of 2x³ − 5x² + kx − 3, then k equals
questions.e: P(3) = 0: 54 − 45 + 3k − 3 = 0, so 6 + 3k = 0 and k = −2. Dropping the constant −3 gives 9 + 3k = 0 and the wrong value k = −3; a sign slip gives k = 2.

questions.s: x − 2 is a factor of P(x) = 2x³ + ax² + bx − 2, and P(x) leaves remainder −3 when divided by x + 1. Then
questions.e: P(2) = 16 + 4a + 2b − 2 = 0 gives 2a + b = −7. P(−1) = −2 + a − b − 2 = −3 gives a − b = 1. Adding, 3a = −6, so a = −2 and b = −3. Check: P(2) = 16 − 8 − 6 − 2 = 0. Swapping the values (a = −3, b = −2) still gives a sum of −5 but P(2) = −4 ≠ 0.

questions.s: Dividing 2x³ + 3x² − x + 5 by x + 2 by synthetic division gives
questions.e: Use −2 with 2, 3, −1, 5: 2; 3 − 4 = −1; −1 + 2 = 1; 5 − 2 = 3. So the quotient is 2x² − x + 1 and the remainder 3 (check P(−2) = −16 + 12 + 2 + 5 = 3). Using +2 gives quotient 2x² + 7x + 13 and remainder 31, which is division by x − 2.

questions.s: If (5x + 4)/((x + 2)(x − 1)) = A/(x + 2) + B/(x − 1), then A + B equals
questions.e: 5x + 4 = A(x − 1) + B(x + 2). x = −2 gives −6 = −3A, A = 2; x = 1 gives 9 = 3B, B = 3. So A + B = 5, which also follows at once from comparing x coefficients. The values 2 and 3 are A and B separately.

questions.s: x²/((x − 1)(x² + 1)) expressed in partial fractions is
questions.e: x² = A(x² + 1) + (Bx + C)(x − 1). x = 1 gives A = 1/2; x² terms: 1 = A + B, B = 1/2; constants: 0 = A − C, C = 1/2. Hence 1/(2(x − 1)) + (x + 1)/(2(x² + 1)). Writing C = −1/2 makes the constant terms add to 1, not 0.

questions.s: To resolve (x³ + 1)/(x² − 4) into partial fractions, the first step is to
questions.e: The numerator has higher degree than the denominator, so the fraction is improper: divide first to get x + (4x + 1)/(x² − 4), then split the proper part. Writing A/(x − 2) + B/(x + 2) directly cannot produce the polynomial part x.

questions.s: x³/(x² − 1) expressed in partial fractions is
questions.e: Divide: x³ = x(x² − 1) + x, so x³/(x² − 1) = x + x/(x² − 1). Then x = A(x + 1) + B(x − 1): x = 1 gives A = 1/2, x = −1 gives B = 1/2. Dropping the quotient x, as in the third option, leaves only x/(x² − 1).

questions.s: The quadratic formula gives the roots of ax² + bx + c = 0 (a ≠ 0) as
questions.e: Completing the square on ax² + bx + c = 0 gives (x + b/(2a))² = (b² − 4ac)/(4a²), so x = (−b ± √(b² − 4ac))/(2a). Dividing by a instead of 2a doubles both roots.

questions.s: The solution set of x² = 7x is
questions.e: x² − 7x = 0 gives x(x − 7) = 0, so x = 0 or 7. Dividing both sides by x loses the root x = 0, which is why {7} alone is wrong.

questions.s: A positive number exceeds its reciprocal by 3/2. The number is
questions.e: x − 1/x = 3/2 gives 2x² − 3x − 2 = 0 = (2x + 1)(x − 2), so x = 2 (x = −1/2 is not positive). Check: 2 − 1/2 = 3/2. The value 1/2 is the reciprocal, which is less than 2, not greater.

questions.s: Bilal drives 120 km. If his speed were 10 km/h more, the trip would take 1 hour less. His speed is
questions.e: 120/v − 120/(v + 10) = 1 gives 1200 = v(v + 10), so v² + 10v − 1200 = 0 = (v + 40)(v − 30) and v = 30 km/h. Check: 120/30 = 4 h and 120/40 = 3 h. The value 40 km/h is the increased speed.

questions.s: The equation x² + 2x + k = 0 has complex (non-real) roots when
questions.e: Non-real roots need b² − 4ac < 0: 4 − 4k < 0, so k > 1. The condition k < 1 makes the discriminant positive, giving real distinct roots, and k = 1 gives equal roots.

questions.s: For all real a, b and k, the roots of (x − a)(x − b) = k² are
questions.e: Expand: x² − (a + b)x + ab − k² = 0. Discriminant = (a + b)² − 4ab + 4k² = (a − b)² + 4k² ≥ 0, so the roots are always real. They are equal only when a = b and k = 0, and need not be rational (a = b = 0, k = 1 gives x = ±1, but k = √2 gives ±√2).

questions.s: For 2x² + kx + 8 = 0, the sum of the roots equals their product. Then k equals
questions.e: Sum = −k/2 and product = 8/2 = 4, so −k/2 = 4 and k = −8. Forgetting the minus sign in −b/a gives k = 8.

questions.s: If α and β are the roots of x² − 3x + 5 = 0, the equation whose roots are α + 1/β and β + 1/α is
questions.e: Sum = (α + β) + (α + β)/(αβ) = 3 + 3/5 = 18/5. Product = αβ + 1 + 1 + 1/(αβ) = 5 + 2 + 1/5 = 36/5. So x² − (18/5)x + 36/5 = 0, i.e. 5x² − 18x + 36 = 0. Forgetting the two middle terms (1 + 1) of the product gives 26/5.

questions.s: If α and β are the roots of x² + 3x − 4 = 0, then (α + 2)(β + 2) equals
questions.e: (α + 2)(β + 2) = αβ + 2(α + β) + 4 = −4 + 2(−3) + 4 = −6. (Check with the roots 1 and −4: 3 × (−2) = −6.) Taking the sum as +3 gives 6.

questions.s: The real solutions of x⁴ − 3x² − 4 = 0 are
questions.e: With y = x²: y² − 3y − 4 = 0 gives y = 4 or −1. x² = 4 gives x = ±2, while x² = −1 has no real solution. Including ±1 wrongly treats x² = −1 as x² = 1.

questions.s: The solution set of (x² − 2x)² − 2(x² − 2x) − 3 = 0 is
questions.e: Let y = x² − 2x: y² − 2y − 3 = 0 gives y = 3 or −1. x² − 2x − 3 = 0 gives x = 3, −1; x² − 2x + 1 = 0 gives x = 1. So the set is {−1, 1, 3}. The set {3, −1} gives the values of y and also misses x = 1.

questions.s: If 4ˣ = 8, then x equals
questions.e: Write both sides as powers of 2: 2²ˣ = 2³, so 2x = 3 and x = 3/2. The value 2/3 inverts the ratio of the exponents.

questions.s: If 2ˣ⁺ʸ = 8 and 3ˣ⁻ʸ = 3, then
questions.e: 8 = 2³ gives x + y = 3 and 3 = 3¹ gives x − y = 1. Adding, 2x = 4, so x = 2 and y = 1. The pair x = 1, y = 2 satisfies x + y = 3 but gives x − y = −1.

questions.s: The solution set of √(5x + 6) = x is
questions.e: Squaring gives x² − 5x − 6 = 0 = (x − 6)(x + 1), so x = 6 or −1. x = 6 checks (√36 = 6), but x = −1 gives √1 = 1 ≠ −1, so it is extraneous. A square root is never negative, so the right side x must be ≥ 0.

questions.s: A value obtained after squaring both sides of a radical equation that does not satisfy the original equation is called
questions.e: Squaring can introduce values that satisfy the squared equation but not the original one; these are extraneous roots and must be rejected after checking. A repeated root is a genuine root that occurs twice.

questions.s: The remainder when x¹⁰⁰ + 1 is divided by x + 1 is
questions.e: P(−1) = (−1)¹⁰⁰ + 1 = 1 + 1 = 2, since an even power of −1 is 1. Answering 0 treats (−1)¹⁰⁰ as −1, which would be true only for an odd power.

questions.s: Which pair of values makes x² − 1 a factor of x³ + ax² − x + b?
questions.e: x² − 1 = (x − 1)(x + 1), so P(1) = 0 and P(−1) = 0. P(1) = 1 + a − 1 + b = a + b and P(−1) = −1 + a + 1 + b = a + b, so we need b = −a; only a = 2, b = −2 fits, giving (x + 2)(x² − 1). The pair a = b = 2 gives P(1) = 4 ≠ 0.

questions.s: Synthetic division of x³ − 8 by x − 2 gives the quotient
questions.e: Coefficients 1, 0, 0, −8 with 2: 1; 0 + 2 = 2; 0 + 4 = 4; −8 + 8 = 0. So the quotient is x² + 2x + 4 with remainder 0, matching x³ − 8 = (x − 2)(x² + 2x + 4). The quotient x² − 2x + 4 belongs to x³ + 8 divided by x + 2.

questions.s: (x + 1)/(x² + 3x + 2) expressed in its simplest partial-fraction form is
questions.e: x² + 3x + 2 = (x + 1)(x + 2), and the factor x + 1 cancels, leaving 1/(x + 2), which is already a single partial fraction. 1/(x + 1) − 1/(x + 2) recombines to 1/((x + 1)(x + 2)), which has numerator 1, not x + 1.

questions.s: (2x² + 3)/(x − 1)³ expressed in partial fractions is
questions.e: Put t = x − 1: 2x² + 3 = 2(t + 1)² + 3 = 2t² + 4t + 5. Dividing by t³ gives 2/t + 4/t² + 5/t³. Keeping the constant 3 forgets that the 2x² term also contributes 2 to the constant when rewritten in powers of x − 1.

questions.s: The sum of the roots of x² − 9 = 0 is
questions.e: The roots are 3 and −3, so their sum is 0; equivalently −b/a = 0 because there is no x term. The value −9 is the product of the roots, c/a.

questions.s: The roots of x² + x + 1 = 0 are
questions.e: Discriminant = 1 − 4 = −3 < 0, so the roots (−1 ± i√3)/2 are non-real and conjugate to each other. Real roots would need a discriminant of at least 0.

questions.s: If x = 2 is a root of x² + bx − 8 = 0, then b equals
questions.e: Substitute x = 2: 4 + 2b − 8 = 0, so 2b = 4 and b = 2; the equation is x² + 2x − 8 = (x − 2)(x + 4). A sign slip with the −8 gives b = −2.

questions.s: The quadratic equation whose roots are 0 and 4 is
questions.e: Sum = 4 and product = 0, so x² − 4x + 0 = 0, i.e. x(x − 4) = 0. The equation x² − 4 = 0 has roots ±2, and x² − 4x + 4 = 0 has the double root 2.

questions.s: If 5ˣ = 1/25, then x equals
questions.e: 1/25 = 5⁻², so x = −2. Choosing 2 ignores that a reciprocal needs a negative exponent.

questions.s: By the remainder theorem, when a polynomial P(x) is divided by x − a, the remainder is
questions.e: P(x) = (x − a)Q(x) + R; putting x = a makes the first term zero, so R = P(a). P(−a) is the remainder on division by x + a.

questions.s: To divide x⁴ + 2x − 1 by x − 3 by synthetic division, the numbers written in the top row are
questions.e: All powers from x⁴ down to the constant need a place, so the missing x³ and x² terms take 0: 1, 0, 0, 2, −1. Leaving out the zeros (1, 2, −1) shifts every coefficient into the wrong place.

questions.s: 1/(x(x + 1)) expressed in partial fractions is
questions.e: 1 = A(x + 1) + Bx; x = 0 gives A = 1 and x = −1 gives B = −1. So 1/(x(x + 1)) = 1/x − 1/(x + 1). With a plus sign the numerator would be 2x + 1, not 1.

questions.s: Putting y = 3ˣ in 9ˣ − 10·3ˣ + 9 = 0 gives the equation
questions.e: 9ˣ = (3²)ˣ = (3ˣ)² = y², so the equation becomes y² − 10y + 9 = 0 (then y = 1 or 9 and x = 0 or 2). Writing 9ˣ as 3y treats the power as a product.

questions.s: If √(x − 3) = 4, then x equals
questions.e: Squaring gives x − 3 = 16, so x = 19; check √16 = 4. The value 7 adds 3 to 4 without squaring first.

questions.s: For any real m, the roots of x² − (m + 1)x + m = 0 are
questions.e: The roots have sum m + 1 and product m, which fits 1 and m; indeed x² − (m + 1)x + m = (x − 1)(x − m). The pair −1 and −m has sum −(m + 1), the wrong sign.

questions.s: The roots of 3x² + 7x + 2 = 0 are
questions.e: Discriminant = 49 − 24 = 25 = 5², a perfect square, so the roots are rational and unequal: x = (−7 ± 5)/6 = −1/3 or −2. Irrational roots need a positive discriminant that is not a perfect square.

questions.s: If α and β are the roots of x² − 4x + 1 = 0, then 1/α² + 1/β² equals
questions.e: 1/α² + 1/β² = (α² + β²)/(αβ)². α² + β² = 16 − 2 = 14 and (αβ)² = 1, so the value is 14. Using (α + β)² = 16 without subtracting 2αβ gives 16.

questions.s: If α and β are the roots of x² − 2x − 5 = 0, the equation whose roots are 3α and 3β is
questions.e: New sum = 3 × 2 = 6 and new product = 9 × (−5) = −45, giving x² − 6x − 45 = 0 (equivalently, replace x by x/3). Multiplying the product by 3 instead of 9 gives −15.

questions.s: The quadratic equation with real coefficients whose roots are 1 + 2i and 1 − 2i is
questions.e: Sum = 2 and product = (1 + 2i)(1 − 2i) = 1 − 4i² = 1 + 4 = 5, so x² − 2x + 5 = 0. Taking i² = 1 gives the product 1 − 4 = −3 and the wrong equation x² − 2x − 3 = 0.

questions.s: If α and β are the roots of x² + 2x − 2 = 0, then α³β + αβ³ equals
questions.e: α³β + αβ³ = αβ(α² + β²). α + β = −2 and αβ = −2, so α² + β² = 4 − 2(−2) = 8 and the value is −2 × 8 = −16. Forgetting the sign of αβ gives 16.

questions.s: The number of real roots of 2x⁴ − 5x² + 2 = 0 is
questions.e: With y = x²: 2y² − 5y + 2 = 0 gives y = 2 or 1/2, both positive. So x = ±√2 and x = ±1/√2, four real roots. Answering 2 counts the values of y instead of x.

questions.s: If 2 raised to the power (x² − 3x) equals 1/4, then x belongs to
questions.e: 1/4 = 2⁻², so x² − 3x = −2, i.e. x² − 3x + 2 = 0 = (x − 1)(x − 2) and x = 1 or 2. The set {0, 3} solves x² − 3x = 0, as if 1/4 were 2⁰.

questions.s: The solution set of √(x + 1) = x − 1 is
questions.e: Squaring: x + 1 = x² − 2x + 1, so x² − 3x = 0 and x = 0 or 3. x = 3 checks (√4 = 2 = 3 − 1); x = 0 gives √1 = 1 but 0 − 1 = −1, so it is extraneous. Keeping {0, 3} skips the check.

questions.s: P(x) = x³ − 3x² + kx + 5 leaves remainder 7 when divided by x − 2. The value of k is
questions.e: P(2) = 8 − 12 + 2k + 5 = 2k + 1 = 7, so k = 3. Setting P(2) = 0 instead, as if x − 2 were a factor, gives k = −1/2, and a sign slip with −12 gives other wrong values such as −3.

questions.s: The roots of x² + 6x + c = 0 differ by 4. The value of c is
questions.e: (α − β)² = (α + β)² − 4αβ = 36 − 4c = 16, so c = 5; the roots are −1 and −5. The value 20 is 36 − 16 without dividing by 4, and c = 9 would make the roots equal.

questions.s: If one root of 2x² + 7x + k = 0 is −4, the other root is
questions.e: Sum of roots = −7/2, so the other root is −7/2 − (−4) = 1/2. (Then k = 2 × product = 2(−4)(1/2) = −4; check 32 − 28 − 4 = 0.) The value −15/2 adds −4 instead of subtracting it.

questions.s: The equation x² + kx + k + 3 = 0 has equal roots when k equals
questions.e: Equal roots: k² − 4(k + 3) = 0, so k² − 4k − 12 = 0 = (k − 6)(k + 2) and k = 6 or −2. Check k = −2: x² − 2x + 1 = (x − 1)². The pair −6 or 2 reverses both signs when factorising.

questions.s: If α and β (α > β) are the roots of x² − 5x + 2 = 0, then α − β equals
questions.e: (α − β)² = (α + β)² − 4αβ = 25 − 8 = 17, and α > β, so α − β = √17. Adding 4αβ instead of subtracting gives √33, and 17 forgets the square root.

questions.s: If α and β are the roots of 2x² − 3x − 4 = 0, the equation whose roots are α/β and β/α is
questions.e: α + β = 3/2 and αβ = −2, so α² + β² = 9/4 + 4 = 25/4. New sum = (α² + β²)/(αβ) = (25/4)/(−2) = −25/8 and new product = 1. So x² + (25/8)x + 1 = 0, i.e. 8x² + 25x + 8 = 0. Using α² + β² = 9/4 − 4 (wrong sign of αβ) leads to the options with 7x.

questions.s: Dividing x⁴ − 5x³ + 8x² − 5x + 1 = 0 by x² and putting y = x + 1/x gives
questions.e: Dividing by x²: (x² + 1/x²) − 5(x + 1/x) + 8 = 0. Since x² + 1/x² = y² − 2, this is y² − 2 − 5y + 8 = 0, i.e. y² − 5y + 6 = 0. Forgetting the −2 gives y² − 5y + 8 = 0, and using +2 gives y² − 5y + 10 = 0.

questions.s: The number of real solutions of 4ˣ − 4·2ˣ + 4 = 0 is
questions.e: With y = 2ˣ: y² − 4y + 4 = (y − 2)² = 0, so y = 2 only and x = 1. A repeated value of y gives only one value of x, so answering 2 counts the double root twice.

questions.s: If 2ˣ⁺¹ + 2ˣ⁻¹ = 20, then x equals
questions.e: Take 2ˣ common: 2ˣ(2 + 1/2) = (5/2)·2ˣ = 20, so 2ˣ = 8 and x = 3. Taking 2ˣ common as 2ˣ(2 + 2) = 20 (writing 2⁻¹ as 2) gives 2ˣ = 5, which has no integer solution.

questions.s: The solution set of √(2x + 3) = √(x + 1) + 1 is
questions.e: Squaring: 2x + 3 = x + 2 + 2√(x + 1), so x + 1 = 2√(x + 1). With u = √(x + 1): u² = 2u gives u = 0 or 2, so x = −1 or 3. Both check: x = −1 gives 1 = 0 + 1 and x = 3 gives 3 = 2 + 1. Dividing by u loses the root x = −1.

questions.s: The solution of √(x² + x + 4) = x + 2 is
questions.e: Squaring: x² + x + 4 = x² + 4x + 4, so 3x = 0 and x = 0. Check: √4 = 2 = 0 + 2. x = −2 makes the right side 0 while the left side is √6.

questions.s: Which of the following polynomials has x − 1 as a factor?
questions.e: x − 1 is a factor exactly when P(1) = 0, i.e. the coefficients add up to 0: 2 − 3 + 1 = 0. The others give P(1) = 1, 2 and 2 respectively.

questions.s: If x + 1 is a factor of x⁴ + kx³ − x + 3, then k equals
questions.e: P(−1) = 1 − k + 1 + 3 = 5 − k = 0, so k = 5. Taking (−1)³ as +1 gives 5 + k = 0 and the wrong value −5.

questions.s: The remainder when x⁵ − 3x⁴ + 2 is divided by x − 3 is
questions.e: P(3) = 3⁵ − 3·3⁴ + 2 = 243 − 243 + 2 = 2. The value −484 is P(−3), the remainder on division by x + 3.

questions.s: When 2x³ + x² − 4x + 3 is divided by 2x − 1, the quotient is
questions.e: Synthetic division by x − 1/2 on 2, 1, −4, 3: 2; 1 + 1 = 2; −4 + 1 = −3; 3 − 3/2 = 3/2. So P(x) = (x − 1/2)(2x² + 2x − 3) + 3/2 = (2x − 1)(x² + x − 3/2) + 3/2. The quotient 2x² + 2x − 3 belongs to the divisor x − 1/2; for 2x − 1 it must be halved.

questions.s: (x² + x + 2)/(x(x − 1)(x + 1)) expressed in partial fractions is
questions.e: Cover-up rule: at x = 0, 2/((−1)(1)) = −2; at x = 1, 4/((1)(2)) = 2; at x = −1, 2/((−1)(−2)) = 1. The coefficients must add up to 1 (the x² coefficient), which −2 + 2 + 1 does; −2 + 2 − 1 = −1 fails that check.

questions.s: (x³ + 2x)/(x² + 1)² expressed in partial fractions is
questions.e: Divide the numerator by x² + 1: x³ + 2x = x(x² + 1) + x. Hence (x³ + 2x)/(x² + 1)² = x/(x² + 1) + x/(x² + 1)². Taking 2x as the second numerator forgets that x(x² + 1) already supplies one x.

questions.s: In (3x² + 2)/((x − 2)(x² + 1)) = A/(x − 2) + (Bx + C)/(x² + 1), the value of A is
questions.e: Multiply through and put x = 2: 3(4) + 2 = A(4 + 1), so 14 = 5A and A = 14/5. Using x² − 1 = 3 instead of x² + 1 = 5 gives 14/3.

questions.s: 3/(x² − 9) expressed in partial fractions is
questions.e: 3 = A(x + 3) + B(x − 3); x = 3 gives A = 1/2 and x = −3 gives B = −1/2. Then 1/(x − 3) − 1/(x + 3) = 6/(x² − 9), twice the given fraction, so the halves are needed.

questions.s: The ages of Zainab and Sana add up to 15 years and their product is 56. The difference of their ages is
questions.e: The ages are the roots of x² − 15x + 56 = 0 = (x − 7)(x − 8), i.e. 7 and 8 years, so the difference is 1 year. (Also (α − β)² = 225 − 224 = 1.) The value 7 is one of the ages.

questions.s: Exactly one root of ax² + bx + c = 0 (a ≠ 0) is zero when
questions.e: x = 0 is a root when c = 0; the equation is then x(ax + b) = 0, whose other root −b/a is non-zero only if b ≠ 0. If b = c = 0 both roots are zero, and b = 0 alone gives roots equal in magnitude and opposite in sign.

questions.s: The roots of x² + x − 12 = 0 are
questions.e: Two numbers with product −12 and sum 1 are 4 and −3, so x² + x − 12 = (x + 4)(x − 3) and x = 3 or −4. The pair −3 and 4 solves x² − x − 12 = 0, with the sign of the middle term reversed.

questions.s: The discriminant of x² − 4x − 5 = 0 is
questions.e: b² − 4ac = 16 − 4(1)(−5) = 16 + 20 = 36. The value 6 is √36, which appears in the formula but is not the discriminant itself; −4 forgets that −4ac is positive here.

questions.s: If α and β are the roots of 4x² + 12x − 7 = 0, then α + β equals
questions.e: Sum = −b/a = −12/4 = −3. The value −7/4 is c/a, the product, and 3 drops the minus sign.

questions.s: If α and β are the roots of x² − 7x + 3 = 0, then α² + β² equals
questions.e: α² + β² = (α + β)² − 2αβ = 49 − 6 = 43. The value 55 adds 2αβ, and 49 forgets to subtract it.

questions.s: The quadratic equation whose roots are 4 and −1 is
questions.e: Sum = 3 and product = −4, so x² − 3x − 4 = 0 = (x − 4)(x + 1). The equation x² + 3x − 4 = 0 has the roots −4 and 1.

questions.s: The roots of 9x² + kx + 4 = 0 are equal when k equals
questions.e: Equal roots: k² − 4(9)(4) = 0, so k² = 144 and k = ±12, giving (3x ± 2)². Writing 12 only misses k = −12.

questions.s: The largest root of x⁴ − 10x² + 9 = 0 is
questions.e: With y = x²: y² − 10y + 9 = 0 gives y = 1 or 9, so x = ±1, ±3 and the largest root is 3. The value 9 is a value of x², not of x.

questions.s: If 7ˣ⁻² = 1, then x equals
questions.e: Any non-zero number to the power 0 is 1, so x − 2 = 0 and x = 2. Answering 0 confuses the exponent x − 2 with x.

questions.s: The solution set of √(x + 6) = x is
questions.e: Squaring: x² − x − 6 = 0 = (x − 3)(x + 2), so x = 3 or −2. x = 3 checks (√9 = 3), but x = −2 gives √4 = 2 ≠ −2, so it is extraneous and the set is {3}.

questions.s: The remainder when 2x³ − x + 4 is divided by x − 1 is
questions.e: P(1) = 2 − 1 + 4 = 5. The value 3 is P(−1) = −2 + 1 + 4, the remainder on division by x + 1.

questions.s: If x − 2 is a factor of x³ − 3x² + kx + 2, then k equals
questions.e: P(2) = 8 − 12 + 2k + 2 = 2k − 2 = 0, so k = 1. Forgetting the constant 2 gives 2k − 4 = 0 and the wrong value k = 2.

questions.s: Synthetic division of x³ + 2x² − 5x − 6 by x − 2 gives the quotient
questions.e: Use 2 with 1, 2, −5, −6: 1; 2 + 2 = 4; −5 + 8 = 3; −6 + 6 = 0. The quotient is x² + 4x + 3 and the remainder 0. Using −2 gives 1, 0, −5 and the quotient x² − 5 with remainder 4, which is division by x + 2.

questions.s: (x + 5)/((x − 1)(x + 2)) expressed in partial fractions is
questions.e: x + 5 = A(x + 2) + B(x − 1). x = 1 gives 6 = 3A, A = 2; x = −2 gives 3 = −3B, B = −1. With B = +1 the numerator would be 3x + 3, not x + 5.

questions.s: (x + 2)/(x + 1)² expressed in partial fractions is
questions.e: Write x + 2 = (x + 1) + 1, so (x + 2)/(x + 1)² = 1/(x + 1) + 1/(x + 1)². Taking 2 as the second numerator ignores that the first term already supplies 1 to the constant.

questions.s: (x + 1)/(x(x² + 1)) expressed in partial fractions is
questions.e: x + 1 = A(x² + 1) + (Bx + C)x. x = 0 gives A = 1; x² terms: 0 = A + B, so B = −1; x terms: C = 1. Hence 1/x + (1 − x)/(x² + 1). Dropping B, as in 1/x + 1/(x² + 1), leaves an extra x² in the numerator.

questions.s: The roots of x² − 2x + 5 = 0 are
questions.e: Discriminant = 4 − 20 = −16 < 0, so the roots 1 ± 2i are non-real complex conjugates. A real pair would need a discriminant of 0 or more.

questions.s: If α and β are the roots of x² + x + 3 = 0, then α³ + β³ equals
questions.e: α + β = −1 and αβ = 3. α³ + β³ = (α + β)³ − 3αβ(α + β) = −1 − 3(3)(−1) = −1 + 9 = 8. Taking −3αβ(α + β) as −9 gives −10.

questions.s: The solution set of 4ˣ⁺¹ − 17·2ˣ + 4 = 0 is
questions.e: 4ˣ⁺¹ = 4(2ˣ)². With y = 2ˣ: 4y² − 17y + 4 = 0 = (4y − 1)(y − 4), so y = 4 or 1/4, giving x = 2 or −2. The set {4, 1/4} lists the values of 2ˣ.

questions.s: The solution of √(x + 3) + √(x + 8) = 5 is
questions.e: √(x + 8) = 5 − √(x + 3); squaring gives x + 8 = 25 − 10√(x + 3) + x + 3, so 10√(x + 3) = 20 and x + 3 = 4, x = 1. Check: √4 + √9 = 2 + 3 = 5. x = 6 gives 3 + √14, which is more than 5.

questions.s: If α and β are the roots of x² − 5x + 6 = 0, the equation whose roots are α + β and αβ is
questions.e: α + β = 5 and αβ = 6 are the new roots, so their sum is 11 and product 30: x² − 11x + 30 = 0. Swapping sum and product in the equation gives x² − 30x + 11 = 0.

questions.s: Synthetic division, in its basic form, is used to divide a polynomial by a divisor of the form
questions.e: Synthetic division works with the root a of a linear divisor x − a (a divisor such as 2x − 1 is first written as 2(x − 1/2)). Quadratic divisors need long division.

questions.s: The solution set of (x − 1)/x + x/(x − 1) = 5/2 is
questions.e: Let y = (x − 1)/x: y + 1/y = 5/2 gives y = 2 or 1/2. (x − 1)/x = 2 gives x = −1, and (x − 1)/x = 1/2 gives x = 2. The set {2, 1/2} lists the values of y, not of x.

questions.s: x² + ax + b leaves remainder 2 when divided by x − 1 and remainder 6 when divided by x + 1. Then
questions.e: P(1) = 1 + a + b = 2 and P(−1) = 1 − a + b = 6. Adding gives 2 + 2b = 8, so b = 3, and then a = −2. With a = 2 the first condition gives P(1) = 6, not 2.

questions.s: The correct form of partial fractions for (3x + 1)/(x + 2)² is
questions.e: A repeated linear factor (x + 2)² needs one term for each power: A/(x + 2) + B/(x + 2)². Here 3x + 1 = 3(x + 2) − 5 gives A = 3 and B = −5. A single term A/(x + 2)² cannot produce the x in the numerator.

questions.s: Usman says that the sum of a positive number and its square is 42. The number is
questions.e: x + x² = 42 gives x² + x − 42 = 0 = (x + 7)(x − 6), so x = 6 (−7 is rejected as not positive). Check: 6 + 36 = 42. The value 7 takes the wrong sign from the factor x + 7.

questions.s: The 15th term of the arithmetic progression 7, 11, 15, … is
questions.e: Here a = 7 and d = 4, so T₁₅ = a + 14d = 7 + 56 = 63. Writing a + 15d gives 67, which is the 16th term; the nth term uses (n − 1) steps of d.

questions.s: Which term of the AP 5, 8, 11, … is 92?
questions.e: Tₙ = 5 + 3(n − 1) = 92 gives 3(n − 1) = 87, so n − 1 = 29 and n = 30. Stopping at n − 1 = 29 gives the tempting wrong choice 29th.

questions.s: In an arithmetic progression the 4th term is 17 and the 9th term is 37. The common difference is
questions.e: T₉ − T₄ = (a + 8d) − (a + 3d) = 5d = 37 − 17 = 20, so d = 4. The value 20 is the difference of the two terms, not of consecutive terms.

questions.s: The sum of the first 20 terms of the AP 3, 7, 11, … is
questions.e: S₂₀ = (20/2)[2(3) + 19(4)] = 10(6 + 76) = 820. Using 20d instead of 19d gives 10(86) = 860, and forgetting the factor n/2 gives 1640.

questions.s: The arithmetic mean between 13 and 27 is
questions.e: A = (13 + 27)/2 = 40/2 = 20, and 13, 20, 27 is indeed an AP with d = 7. The value 40 is the sum, not the mean, and 7 is the common difference.

questions.s: Four arithmetic means are inserted between 3 and 23. The third of these means is
questions.e: With 4 means there are 6 terms in all, so 23 = 3 + 5d and d = 4. The means are 7, 11, 15, 19, so the third is 15. Taking d = 20/4 = 5 (counting only 5 terms) gives 18.

questions.s: The nth term of a sequence is 5n − 2. The sum of its first 10 terms is
questions.e: T₁ = 3 and T₁₀ = 48, so S₁₀ = (10/2)(3 + 48) = 5(51) = 255. Using 5Σn alone gives 275, which forgets to subtract 2 from each of the 10 terms; 48 is only the 10th term.

questions.s: The sum of all two-digit natural numbers that are multiples of 7 is
questions.e: The multiples are 14, 21, …, 98, an AP with d = 7 and n = (98 − 14)/7 + 1 = 13 terms. S = (13/2)(14 + 98) = 13 × 56 = 728. Counting 14 terms gives 7 × 112 = 784.

questions.s: If the sum of the first n terms of a sequence is Sₙ = 3n² + 2n, then its nth term is
questions.e: Tₙ = Sₙ − Sₙ₋₁ = 3[n² − (n − 1)²] + 2 = 3(2n − 1) + 2 = 6n − 1. Check: T₁ = 5 = S₁. The form 6n + 1 comes from an expansion sign slip and gives T₁ = 7 ≠ S₁.

questions.s: The general term of the sequence 2, 5, 8, 11, … is
questions.e: a = 2 and d = 3, so Tₙ = 2 + 3(n − 1) = 3n − 1; n = 1 gives 2 as required. The form 3n + 2 uses a + nd and gives 5 as the first term.

questions.s: Three numbers in AP have sum 27 and product 504. The largest of the three numbers is
questions.e: Take the numbers as a − d, a, a + d. Their sum 3a = 27 gives a = 9, and 9(81 − d²) = 504 gives d² = 25, d = ±5. The numbers are 4, 9, 14, so the largest is 14.

questions.s: If x + 1, 3x and 4x + 2 are consecutive terms of an arithmetic progression, then x =
questions.e: For consecutive AP terms the middle one is the mean: 2(3x) = (x + 1) + (4x + 2), so 6x = 5x + 3 and x = 3. The terms are 4, 9, 14 with d = 5. Moving 3 to the wrong side gives −3.

questions.s: If a, b and c are in arithmetic progression, then
questions.e: In an AP, b − a = c − b, which gives 2b = a + c, so b is the arithmetic mean of a and c. b² = ac is the condition for a GP, and b = 2ac/(a + c) is the condition for an HP.

questions.s: How many terms of the AP 24, 20, 16, … must be taken so that their sum is 72?
questions.e: Sₙ = (n/2)[48 − 4(n − 1)] = n(26 − 2n) = 72 gives n² − 13n + 36 = 0, so n = 4 or n = 9. Both work: terms 5 to 9 are 8, 4, 0, −4, −8, which add to 0. Rejecting 9 overlooks these cancelling terms.

questions.s: The 7th term of an AP is 12 and its 12th term is 7. Its 19th term is
questions.e: 5d = 7 − 12 = −5 gives d = −1, and a = 12 − 6d = 18. So T₁₉ = 18 + 18(−1) = 0. Taking d = +1 by mistake gives a much larger value instead.

questions.s: For an arithmetic progression, S₁₀ = 120 and S₂₀ = 440, where Sₙ is the sum of the first n terms. Then S₃₀ =
questions.e: 5(2a + 9d) = 120 and 10(2a + 19d) = 440 give 2a + 9d = 24 and 2a + 19d = 44, so d = 2 and a = 3. S₃₀ = 15(6 + 58) = 960, which also equals 3(S₂₀ − S₁₀). Adding S₂₀ − S₁₀ = 320 to S₂₀ gives 760, forgetting that each block of 10 terms grows.

questions.s: The sum of the first 50 odd natural numbers is
questions.e: 1 + 3 + … + 99 is an AP with 50 terms, so S = (50/2)(1 + 99) = 2500 = 50². The value 2550 is the sum of the first 50 even numbers, which is n(n + 1).

questions.s: The 3rd term of an AP is 16 and its 7th term exceeds its 5th term by 12. The 10th term of the AP is
questions.e: T₇ − T₅ = 2d = 12, so d = 6, and a = 16 − 2(6) = 4. Then T₁₀ = 4 + 9(6) = 58. Using 10d gives 64.

questions.s: The 10th term of the AP −4, −1, 2, … is
questions.e: a = −4 and d = 3, so T₁₀ = −4 + 9(3) = 23. Taking 10 steps of d gives 26, which is the 11th term.

questions.s: The sum of all natural numbers from 1 to 200 that are divisible by 5 is
questions.e: The numbers are 5, 10, …, 200: 40 terms. S = (40/2)(5 + 200) = 20 × 205 = 4100. The value 20100 is the sum of all numbers from 1 to 200.

questions.s: In an AP the 3rd term is 1/5 and the 5th term is 1/3. The 15th term is
questions.e: 2d = 1/3 − 1/5 = 2/15, so d = 1/15 and a = 1/5 − 2/15 = 1/15. T₁₅ = 1/15 + 14(1/15) = 15/15 = 1. The value 14/15 forgets to add the first term.

questions.s: The sum of the first n terms of an AP is n² + 4n. The common difference of the AP is
questions.e: T₁ = S₁ = 5 and S₂ = 12, so T₂ = 7 and d = 7 − 5 = 2. In general, if Sₙ = pn² + qn then d = 2p. The value 4 is the coefficient of n, not related to d.

questions.s: What is the least number of terms of the AP 3, 7, 11, … whose sum exceeds 300?
questions.e: Sₙ = (n/2)[6 + 4(n − 1)] = n(2n + 1). S₁₂ = 12 × 25 = 300, which only equals 300, while S₁₃ = 13 × 27 = 351 exceeds it. So 13 terms are needed; 12 is the trap because the sum must exceed, not equal, 300.

questions.s: The arithmetic mean of the first n natural numbers is
questions.e: Their sum is n(n + 1)/2, and dividing by the n numbers gives (n + 1)/2, the mean of the first and last terms 1 and n. The expression n(n + 1)/2 is the sum itself, not the mean.

questions.s: If 5, x and 19 are in arithmetic progression, then x =
questions.e: x is the arithmetic mean: x = (5 + 19)/2 = 12, giving the AP 5, 12, 19 with d = 7. √95 is the geometric mean, which would make the numbers a GP.

questions.s: The 8th term of the geometric progression 3, 6, 12, … is
questions.e: a = 3 and r = 2, so T₈ = ar⁷ = 3 × 128 = 384. Using r⁸ gives 768, which is the 9th term.

questions.s: The common ratio of the geometric progression 81, −27, 9, … is
questions.e: r = (−27)/81 = −1/3, and 9/(−27) = −1/3 confirms it. Dividing the first term by the second gives −3, which is the reciprocal of the ratio.

questions.s: The positive geometric mean between 4 and 25 is
questions.e: G = √(4 × 25) = √100 = 10, and 4, 10, 25 is a GP with ratio 5/2. The value 14.5 is the arithmetic mean (4 + 25)/2.

questions.s: If x, 12 and 48 are consecutive terms of a geometric progression, then x =
questions.e: 12² = 48x gives x = 144/48 = 3, and 3, 12, 48 has ratio 4. The value −24 treats the terms as an AP (2 × 12 − 48).

questions.s: The sum of the first 6 terms of the GP 2, 6, 18, … is
questions.e: S₆ = a(r⁶ − 1)/(r − 1) = 2(729 − 1)/2 = 728. The value 486 is only the 6th term 2 × 3⁵, and 364 forgets to multiply by a = 2.

questions.s: Which term of the GP 2, 4, 8, … is 512?
questions.e: Tₙ = 2 × 2ⁿ⁻¹ = 2ⁿ, and 2ⁿ = 512 = 2⁹ gives n = 9. Solving 2ⁿ⁻¹ = 512 without the first term gives 10th.

questions.s: The 3rd term of a GP is 12 and its 6th term is 96. The first term is
questions.e: T₆/T₃ = r³ = 96/12 = 8, so r = 2 and a = 12/r² = 12/4 = 3. Dividing 12 by r only once gives 6, which is the 2nd term.

questions.s: The sum of the infinite geometric series 6 + 2 + 2/3 + … is
questions.e: a = 6 and r = 1/3, so S∞ = a/(1 − r) = 6/(2/3) = 9. Dividing by r instead of 1 − r gives 18.

questions.s: The sum of an infinite geometric series is 20 and its first term is 5. The common ratio is
questions.e: 5/(1 − r) = 20 gives 1 − r = 1/4, so r = 3/4. The value 1/4 is 1 − r, not r, and 4/3 is not allowed since |r| < 1 for a convergent series.

questions.s: The recurring decimal 0.454545… written as a fraction in lowest terms is
questions.e: 0.4545… = 0.45 + 0.0045 + … is an infinite GP with a = 45/100 and r = 1/100, so it equals (45/100)/(99/100) = 45/99 = 5/11. The fraction 9/20 = 0.45 is only the first term.

questions.s: The infinite geometric series a + ar + ar² + … (a ≠ 0) has a finite sum if and only if
questions.e: rⁿ → 0 exactly when |r| < 1, and then S∞ = a/(1 − r). The condition r < 1 is not enough: r = −2 is less than 1 but the terms grow without bound.

questions.s: The recurring decimal 0.2777… (only the 7 repeats) as a fraction in lowest terms is
Three numbers in GP have product 216 and sum 21. The largest of the numbers is
questions.e: Write them as a/r, a, ar: a³ = 216 gives a = 6. Then 6/r + 6 + 6r = 21 gives 2r² − 5r + 2 = 0, so r = 2 or 1/2. Either way the numbers are 3, 6, 12, and the largest is 12.

questions.s: Two geometric means are inserted between 2 and 54. The sum of these two means is
questions.e: The 4 terms are 2, 2r, 2r², 2r³ = 54, so r³ = 27 and r = 3. The means are 6 and 18, with sum 24. The value 56 is the sum of the two given numbers.

questions.s: How many terms of the GP 1, 3, 9, … must be added to give a sum of 364?
questions.e: Sₙ = (3ⁿ − 1)/(3 − 1) = 364 gives 3ⁿ − 1 = 728, so 3ⁿ = 729 = 3⁶ and n = 6. Check: 1 + 3 + 9 + 27 + 81 + 243 = 364. Forgetting to divide by r − 1 = 2 leads to 3ⁿ = 365, which has no whole-number solution.

questions.s: The 3rd term of a geometric progression is 4. The product of its first five terms is
questions.e: The first five terms are 4/r², 4/r, 4, 4r, 4r², and the powers of r cancel, leaving 4⁵ = 1024. The value 20 is 5 × 4, a sum-type slip, and 256 = 4⁴ drops one factor.

questions.s: The nth term of the geometric progression 5, 10, 20, … is
questions.e: a = 5 and r = 2, so Tₙ = arⁿ⁻¹ = 5 × 2ⁿ⁻¹; n = 1 gives 5. The form 5 × 2ⁿ gives 10 as the first term, one step too far.

questions.s: The 4th term of a GP is 1/8 and its 7th term is 1/64. The sum of the GP to infinity is
questions.e: r³ = (1/64)/(1/8) = 1/8, so r = 1/2, and a = (1/8)/r³ = 1. Then S∞ = 1/(1 − 1/2) = 2. The value 1 is the first term, not the sum.

questions.s: In an infinite GP of positive terms, every term is 3 times the sum of all the terms that follow it. The common ratio is
questions.e: For the term a, the terms after it sum to ar/(1 − r). So a = 3ar/(1 − r), which gives 1 − r = 3r and r = 1/4. Taking r = 1/3 confuses the factor 3 with the ratio itself.

questions.s: The sum of the infinite series 1 − 1/3 + 1/9 − 1/27 + … is
questions.e: a = 1 and r = −1/3, so S∞ = 1/(1 + 1/3) = 3/4. Ignoring the alternating sign (r = +1/3) gives 3/2.

questions.s: If k, k + 3 and k + 9 are consecutive terms of a geometric progression, then k =
questions.e: (k + 3)² = k(k + 9) gives k² + 6k + 9 = k² + 9k, so 3k = 9 and k = 3. The terms are 3, 6, 12 with ratio 2.

questions.s: The sum of the first n terms of the series 1 + 2 + 4 + 8 + … is
questions.e: a = 1, r = 2, so Sₙ = (2ⁿ − 1)/(2 − 1) = 2ⁿ − 1; for n = 3, 1 + 2 + 4 = 7 = 2³ − 1. The form 2ⁿ⁺¹ − 1 is the sum of n + 1 terms.

questions.s: In a geometric progression of positive terms, every term equals the sum of the next two terms. The common ratio is
questions.e: a = ar + ar² gives r² + r − 1 = 0, so r = (−1 ± √5)/2. Positive terms need r > 0, so r = (√5 − 1)/2. The value (√5 + 1)/2 solves r² − r − 1 = 0, a sign slip.

questions.s: A ball is dropped from a height of 12 m. After each bounce it rises to 2/3 of the height from which it fell. The total distance it travels before coming to rest is
questions.e: Down 12 m first, then each rebound height is covered twice (up and down): 12 + 2(8 + 16/3 + …) = 12 + 2 × 8/(1 − 2/3) = 12 + 48 = 60 m. The value 36 m = 12/(1/3) counts every height only once.

questions.s: The 5th term of the GP 2, −6, 18, … is
questions.e: a = 2 and r = −3, so T₅ = 2(−3)⁴ = 2 × 81 = 162; an even power makes it positive. The value 486 is 2 × 3⁵, the size of the 6th term.

questions.s: A sequence of non-zero numbers is called a harmonic progression if
o: the reciprocals of its terms are in AP
the squares of its terms are in AP
the reciprocals of its terms are in GP
questions.e: By definition, a₁, a₂, a₃, … is an HP when 1/a₁, 1/a₂, 1/a₃, … form an AP; for example 1, 1/2, 1/3, … is an HP because 1, 2, 3, … is an AP. Reciprocals of a GP form another GP, not an HP.

questions.s: The harmonic mean between 3 and 6 is
questions.e: H = 2ab/(a + b) = 2(3)(6)/9 = 36/9 = 4. Check: 1/3, 1/4, 1/6 form an AP with difference −1/12. The value 4.5 is the arithmetic mean and 3√2 the geometric mean.

questions.s: The 10th term of the harmonic progression 1/2, 1/5, 1/8, … is
questions.e: The reciprocals 2, 5, 8, … form an AP with d = 3, whose 10th term is 2 + 9(3) = 29. So the 10th term of the HP is 1/29. The value 29 forgets to take the reciprocal back.

questions.s: The nth term of the harmonic progression 1, 1/3, 1/5, 1/7, … is
questions.e: The reciprocals 1, 3, 5, 7, … have nth term 2n − 1, so the HP has nth term 1/(2n − 1). The form 1/(2n + 1) gives 1/3 for n = 1, which is the second term.

questions.s: The harmonic mean between 1/4 and 1/6 is
questions.e: The reciprocals are 4 and 6, whose arithmetic mean is 5, so the harmonic mean is 1/5. Equivalently 2ab/(a + b) = (2/24)/(5/12) = 1/5. The value 5/24 is the arithmetic mean of 1/4 and 1/6.

questions.s: Two harmonic means are inserted between 1/3 and 1/12. They are
questions.e: The reciprocals 3, x, y, 12 form an AP with 3d = 9, so d = 3 and the AP is 3, 6, 9, 12. The harmonic means are therefore 1/6 and 1/9.

questions.s: If a, b and c (all non-zero) are in harmonic progression, then b =
questions.e: 1/a, 1/b, 1/c are in AP, so 2/b = 1/a + 1/c = (a + c)/ac, giving b = 2ac/(a + c). The expression (a + c)/(2ac) is 1/b, the reciprocal of the required value.

questions.s: The 4th term of a harmonic progression is 1/10 and its 9th term is 1/20. Its 14th term is
questions.e: For the AP of reciprocals, T₄ = 10 and T₉ = 20, so 5d = 10, d = 2 and a = 4. Its 14th term is 4 + 13(2) = 30, so the HP term is 1/30. The value 30 forgets to invert.

questions.s: If 2, x and 3 are in harmonic progression, then x =
questions.e: x = 2ab/(a + b) = 2(2)(3)/5 = 12/5. Check: 1/2, 5/12, 1/3 have common difference −1/12. The value 5/2 is the arithmetic mean and 5/12 is 1/x.

questions.s: If a, b and c are in harmonic progression, then (a − b)/(b − c) equals
questions.e: 1/b − 1/a = 1/c − 1/b gives (a − b)/(ab) = (b − c)/(bc). Multiplying by b gives (a − b)/a = (b − c)/c, so (a − b)/(b − c) = a/c. The value 1 holds for an AP, where a − b = b − c.

questions.s: If 1/3, 1/x and 1/11 are consecutive terms of a harmonic progression, then x =
questions.e: The reciprocals 3, x, 11 must be in AP, so x = (3 + 11)/2 = 7. The value 14 is the sum 3 + 11 without halving.

questions.s: The first term of a harmonic progression is 1/2 and its fifth term is 1/14. Its third term is
questions.e: The reciprocal AP has first term 2 and fifth term 14, so 4d = 12 and d = 3. Its third term is 2 + 6 = 8, so the HP's third term is 1/8. The value 8 is the term of the reciprocal AP; the HP term is its reciprocal.

questions.s: The harmonic mean of the roots of x² − 6x + 4 = 0 is
questions.e: For the roots α, β: α + β = 6 and αβ = 4. HM = 2αβ/(α + β) = 8/6 = 4/3. The value 3 is the arithmetic mean (α + β)/2 and 2 is the geometric mean √(αβ).

questions.s: For two unequal positive numbers with arithmetic mean A, geometric mean G and harmonic mean H, which is correct?
questions.e: For unequal positive numbers A > G > H always holds; for example 1 and 4 give A = 2.5, G = 2, H = 1.6. Equality A = G = H happens only when the two numbers are equal.

questions.s: For two positive numbers with arithmetic mean A, geometric mean G and harmonic mean H, the correct relation is
questions.e: A = (a + b)/2 and H = 2ab/(a + b), so AH = ab = G². This means G is the geometric mean of A and H. For 1 and 4: A·H = 2.5 × 1.6 = 4 = G².

questions.s: The arithmetic and geometric means of two positive numbers are 10 and 8. Their harmonic mean is
questions.e: G² = AH gives H = 64/10 = 32/5. The numbers are 4 and 16, and 2(64)/20 = 32/5 confirms it. The value 6 continues the pattern 10, 8, 6 as if A, G, H were in AP.

questions.s: The arithmetic mean of two positive numbers is 5 and their geometric mean is 4. The numbers are
questions.e: The numbers have sum 10 and product 16, so they are the roots of x² − 10x + 16 = 0, which are 2 and 8. The pairs 4 and 6, 3 and 7, 1 and 9 also add to 10 but their products are 24, 21 and 9.

questions.s: The harmonic mean of 2 and 18 is
questions.e: H = 2ab/(a + b) = 2(36)/20 = 18/5. Check with G² = AH: 6² = 10 × 18/5 = 36. The values 10 and 6 are the arithmetic and geometric means.

questions.s: The arithmetic mean and harmonic mean of two positive numbers are 13/2 and 72/13. Their geometric mean is
questions.e: G² = AH = (13/2)(72/13) = 36, so G = 6 (the numbers are 4 and 9). The value 36 is G², not G.

questions.s: The least value of x + 9/x for x > 0 is
questions.e: By A ≥ G for x and 9/x: (x + 9/x)/2 ≥ √9 = 3, so x + 9/x ≥ 6, with equality at x = 3. The value 3 is the geometric mean, half the minimum.

questions.s: Two positive numbers x and y have x + y = 20. The greatest possible value of xy is
questions.e: A ≥ G gives √(xy) ≤ (x + y)/2 = 10, so xy ≤ 100, reached at x = y = 10. The value 400 is (x + y)², which forgets to halve before squaring.

questions.s: The arithmetic mean of two positive numbers equals their geometric mean if and only if
o: one number is double the other
the sum of the numbers is 1
questions.e: A − G = (a + b)/2 − √(ab) = (√a − √b)²/2, which is zero only when a = b. Reciprocals such as 2 and 1/2 give G = 1 but A = 5/4.

questions.s: The ratio of the arithmetic mean to the harmonic mean of two positive numbers is 25 : 16. The ratio of the larger number to the smaller is
questions.e: A/H = (a + b)²/(4ab) = 25/16. With t = a/b this is (t + 1)² = (25/4)t, i.e. 4t² − 17t + 4 = 0, so t = 4 or 1/4. Check 4 and 1: A = 5/2, H = 8/5 and A/H = 25/16. The ratio 5 : 4 is A : G, not the numbers.

questions.s: The geometric mean and harmonic mean of two positive numbers are 12 and 48/5. Their arithmetic mean is
questions.e: A = G²/H = 144/(48/5) = 144 × 5/48 = 15; the numbers are 6 and 24. The value 10 is below G, which is impossible since A ≥ G.

questions.s: The harmonic mean of the three numbers 1, 3 and 9 is
questions.e: H = 3/(1/1 + 1/3 + 1/9) = 3/(13/9) = 27/13. As expected A = 13/3 > G = 3 > H = 27/13. The value 13/27 is 1/H, the mean of the reciprocals.

questions.s: The sum 1 + 2 + 3 + … + 50 equals
questions.e: Σk = n(n + 1)/2 = 50 × 51/2 = 1275. Forgetting to divide by 2 gives 2550, and 50²/2 = 1250 uses n² instead of n(n + 1).

questions.s: The value of 1² + 2² + 3² + … + 10² is
questions.e: Σk² = n(n + 1)(2n + 1)/6 = 10 × 11 × 21/6 = 385. The value 55 is 1 + 2 + … + 10, and 3025 is the sum of the cubes.

questions.s: The value of 1³ + 2³ + 3³ + 4³ + 5³ is
questions.e: Σk³ = [n(n + 1)/2]² = (15)² = 225; directly 1 + 8 + 27 + 64 + 125 = 225. The value 15 is 1 + 2 + … + 5 before squaring, and 55 is the sum of squares.

questions.s: The sum of the squares of the first n natural numbers, 1² + 2² + … + n², is
questions.e: Σk² = n(n + 1)(2n + 1)/6; for n = 2 it gives 2 × 3 × 5/6 = 5 = 1 + 4. The form [n(n + 1)/2]² is the sum of cubes, and n(n + 1)/2 is the sum of the numbers themselves.

questions.s: The sum 1³ + 2³ + 3³ + … + n³ is equal to
questions.e: The sum of the first n cubes is the square of the sum of the first n numbers: [n(n + 1)/2]² = n²(n + 1)²/4. For n = 2: 1 + 8 = 9 = 3². The form n²(n + 1)²/2 has the wrong denominator and gives 18 for n = 2.

questions.s: The value of 11² + 12² + 13² + … + 20² is
questions.e: Σ(1 to 20) k² = 20 × 21 × 41/6 = 2870 and Σ(1 to 10) k² = 385, so the required sum is 2870 − 385 = 2485. Subtracting the squares up to 11² instead gives 2364, which also drops 11².
Σk(k + 1) = Σk² + Σk = 385 + 55 = 440, which also equals n(n + 1)(n + 2)/3 = 10 × 11 × 12/3. The value 385 includes only the squares.

questions.s: The value of 2² + 4² + 6² + … + 20² is
questions.e: Each term is (2k)² = 4k² for k = 1 to 10, so the sum is 4 × 385 = 1540. Taking 2 × 385 = 770 forgets that the factor 2 is squared.

questions.s: The value of 1² + 3² + 5² + … + 19² is
questions.e: All squares up to 20² add to 2870 and the even squares 2² + 4² + … + 20² add to 4 × 385 = 1540. The odd squares therefore add to 2870 − 1540 = 1330. The value 1540 is the even part, not the odd part.

questions.s: The sum of the first n terms of the series whose nth term is 3n² + n is

questions.e: n(n + 1)/2 = 78 gives n(n + 1) = 156 = 12 × 13, so n = 12. The value 39 comes from 78/2, which ignores the formula.

questions.s: If 1³ + 2³ + 3³ + … + n³ = 441, then n =
questions.e: [n(n + 1)/2]² = 441 gives n(n + 1)/2 = 21, so n(n + 1) = 42 and n = 6. The value 21 is √441, which is the sum 1 + 2 + … + n, not n.

questions.s: The value of 6³ + 7³ + 8³ + 9³ + 10³ is
questions.e: Σ(1 to 10) k³ = 55² = 3025 and Σ(1 to 5) k³ = 15² = 225, so the sum is 3025 − 225 = 2800. Subtracting the cubes up to 6³ gives 2584, which wrongly removes 6³ as well.

questions.s: The sum of the first n terms of the series 1 + (1 + 2) + (1 + 2 + 3) + … is
questions.e: The kth term is k(k + 1)/2, so the sum is ½[Σk² + Σk] = ½ × n(n + 1)(n + 2)/3 = n(n + 1)(n + 2)/6. Check n = 2: 1 + 3 = 4 = 2 × 3 × 4/6. The form with /3 forgets the factor ½ in each term.

questions.s: The sum Σ (2k + 3), taken from k = 1 to k = n, equals
questions.e: Σ(2k + 3) = 2 × n(n + 1)/2 + 3n = n² + n + 3n = n² + 4n. Check n = 1: 5 = 1 + 4. The form n² + n + 3 adds 3 only once instead of n times.

questions.s: The sum of the first 10 terms of the series 1·3 + 2·4 + 3·5 + … is
questions.e: The kth term is k(k + 2) = k² + 2k, so the sum is 385 + 2(55) = 495. Adding Σk only once gives 440.

questions.s: The value of (1³ + 2³ + … + 10³)/(1 + 2 + … + 10) is
questions.e: The numerator is (55)² = 3025 and the denominator is 55, so the ratio is 55. In general the ratio equals n(n + 1)/2. The value 385 is the sum of the squares, a different series.
The ratio is [n(n + 1)(2n + 1)/6]/[n(n + 1)/2] = (2n + 1)/3 = 7, so 2n + 1 = 21 and n = 10. The value 21 is 2n + 1, not n.

questions.s: The value of 1² − 2² + 3² − 4² + … + 19² − 20² is
questions.e: Each pair (2k − 1)² − (2k)² = −(4k − 1), so the sum is −Σ(4k − 1) for k = 1 to 10 = −(220 − 10) = −210. This equals −(1 + 2 + … + 20). The positive value 210 ignores that every even square is larger than the odd square before it.

questions.s: The sum of all natural numbers from 1 to 100 that are not divisible by 3 is
questions.e: 1 + 2 + … + 100 = 5050. The multiples of 3 are 3, 6, …, 99, i.e. 33 terms with sum 3 × 33 × 34/2 = 1683. So the required sum is 5050 − 1683 = 3367. Counting 34 multiples gives 3265, and 1683 is the excluded part.

questions.s: The value of Σ (2k + 1) from k = 1 to k = 5 is
questions.e: The terms are 3, 5, 7, 9, 11, with sum 35; by formula 2(15) + 5 = 35. The value 30 forgets the +1 in each term, and 36 starts the odd numbers from 1.

questions.s: If 1² + 2² + 3² + … + n² = 204, then n =
questions.e: n(n + 1)(2n + 1)/6 = 204 gives n(n + 1)(2n + 1) = 1224 = 8 × 9 × 17, so n = 8. For n = 9 the sum is already 285.

questions.s: The nth term of the sequence 2, 6, 12, 20, 30, … is
questions.e: The differences 4, 6, 8, 10 rise by 2, so the nth term is quadratic; 1·2, 2·3, 3·4, … gives Tₙ = n(n + 1) = n² + n. The form 4n − 2 fits only the first two terms.
These are the squares 1² to 20², so the sum is 20 × 21 × 41/6 = 2870. Dividing 20 × 21 × 41 by 2 instead of 6 gives 8610, and dividing by 3 gives 5740.

questions.s: The sum of the first 100 natural numbers is
questions.e: n(n + 1)/2 = 100 × 101/2 = 5050. The value 10100 forgets to halve, and 5000 uses n²/2.

questions.s: Ali saves Rs 100 in the first week and each week he saves Rs 50 more than in the week before. How much does he save in the 10th week?
questions.e: Weekly savings form an AP with a = 100 and d = 50, so T₁₀ = 100 + 9(50) = Rs 550. Using 10 steps of Rs 50 gives Rs 600, the amount for the 11th week.

questions.s: Ayesha saves Rs 200 in the first month and increases her saving by Rs 20 every month. Her total saving in the first year is
A hall in Lahore has 25 rows of seats. The first row has 20 seats and each row has 2 more seats than the row in front of it. The total number of seats is
questions.e: The last row has 20 + 24(2) = 68 seats, so the total is (25/2)(20 + 68) = 25 × 44 = 1100. Taking the last row as 20 + 25(2) = 70 gives 1125, and using 25d in the sum formula gives 1150.

questions.s: A culture starts with 500 bacteria and the number doubles every hour. The number of bacteria after 6 hours is
questions.e: After n hours the count is 500 × 2ⁿ, so after 6 hours it is 500 × 64 = 32000. The value 16000 = 500 × 2⁵ counts only 5 doublings, and 3000 adds 500 each hour.

questions.s: A car bought for Rs 1 600 000 loses 25% of its value every year, each loss being 25% of its value at the start of that year. Its value after 2 years is
questions.e: Each year the value is multiplied by 3/4, so after 2 years it is 1 600 000 × 9/16 = Rs 900 000. Subtracting 25% of the original price twice gives Rs 800 000, which treats the loss as an AP.

questions.s: Hamza runs 2 km on the first day and increases the distance by 0.5 km each day. On which day does he first run 8 km?
questions.e: 2 + 0.5(n − 1) = 8 gives n − 1 = 12, so n = 13. The answer 12th forgets that the first day has no increase yet.

questions.s: Logs are stacked in rows: 21 logs in the bottom row, 20 in the next, 19 in the next, and so on. If there are 165 logs in all, how many logs are in the top row?
questions.e: (n/2)[42 − (n − 1)] = 165 gives n² − 43n + 330 = 0, so n = 10 or 33. n = 33 would need negative rows, so there are 10 rows and the top row has 21 − 9 = 12 logs. The value 10 is the number of rows, not the logs in the top row.

questions.s: A clock strikes once at 1 o'clock, twice at 2 o'clock, and so on up to 12 times at 12 o'clock. How many times does it strike in a full day of 24 hours?
questions.e: In 12 hours it strikes 1 + 2 + … + 12 = 78 times, and the cycle repeats, so a full day gives 2 × 78 = 156. The value 300 = 1 + 2 + … + 24 wrongly assumes it strikes up to 24 times.

questions.s: Rs 10 000 is invested at 10% per annum compound interest. The amount after 3 years is
questions.e: The amounts form a GP with ratio 1.1, so after 3 years A = 10 000 × 1.1³ = 10 000 × 1.331 = Rs 13 310. Rs 13 000 is simple interest (an AP), and Rs 14 641 is the amount after 4 years.

questions.s: Zainab starts a job with a salary of Rs 40 000 per month, and her monthly salary rises by Rs 2000 at the start of each new year. Her total earnings in the first 10 years are
questions.e: The monthly salaries for the 10 years form an AP 40 000, 42 000, …, 58 000 with sum (10/2)(40 000 + 58 000) = 490 000. Each salary is paid for 12 months, so the total is 12 × 490 000 = Rs 5 880 000. Rs 490 000 forgets the 12 months.

questions.s: The four angles of a quadrilateral are in arithmetic progression with common difference 10°. The smallest angle is
questions.e: The angles a, a + 10°, a + 20°, a + 30° add to 360°, so 4a + 60° = 360° and a = 75°. The angles are 75°, 85°, 95°, 105°. The value 85° is the second angle.

questions.s: The sides of a right-angled triangle are in arithmetic progression. The ratio of its sides is
questions.e: Take the sides as a − d, a, a + d. Pythagoras gives (a − d)² + a² = (a + d)², so a² = 4ad and a = 4d. The sides are 3d, 4d, 5d. The triple 5, 12, 13 is right-angled but not in AP.

questions.s: A sheet of paper 0.1 mm thick is folded in half 10 times. The thickness of the folded paper is
questions.e: Each fold doubles the thickness, so after 10 folds it is 0.1 × 2¹⁰ = 0.1 × 1024 = 102.4 mm. The value 51.2 mm uses only 9 doublings, and 1 mm adds 0.1 mm per fold.

questions.s: A pendulum swings through an arc of 60 cm and each later swing is 4/5 of the one before. The total distance it covers before it comes to rest is
questions.e: The swings form an infinite GP with a = 60 and r = 4/5, so S∞ = 60/(1 − 4/5) = 60 × 5 = 300 cm. Dividing 60 by 4/5 gives 75 cm, which is not a sum.

questions.s: A loan of Rs 3250 is repaid in monthly instalments: Rs 20 in the first month, and each instalment is Rs 15 more than the one before. How many months does it take to repay the loan?
Sana reads 10 pages on the first day, 12 pages on the second day, 14 pages on the third day, and so on. How many pages does she read on the 15th day?
questions.e: a = 10 and d = 2, so T₁₅ = 10 + 14(2) = 38. Using 15 steps gives 40, which belongs to the 16th day.

questions.s: A tank holds 1000 litres of water. Each day one tenth of the water present is lost. The amount left after 3 days is
questions.e: Each day the amount is multiplied by 9/10, so after 3 days 1000 × (0.9)³ = 729 L remain. Losing 100 L each day gives 700 L, which wrongly takes one tenth of the original amount every time.

questions.s: How many natural numbers between 100 and 500 are divisible by 7?
questions.e: The first such number is 105 and the last is 497, forming an AP with d = 7. So n = (497 − 105)/7 + 1 = 56 + 1 = 57. The value 56 forgets the +1 for the first term.

questions.s: Three numbers in GP have sum 26 and the sum of their squares is 364. The largest of the numbers is
questions.e: Write the numbers as a/r, a, ar. Since 1/r² + 1 + r² = (1/r + 1 + r)(1/r − 1 + r), dividing 364 by 26 gives a(1/r − 1 + r) = 14. Subtracting this from a(1/r + 1 + r) = 26 gives 2a = 12, so a = 6 and r + 1/r = 10/3, r = 3. The numbers are 2, 6, 18, and 4 + 36 + 324 = 364.

questions.s: Every term of an arithmetic progression with common difference d is multiplied by 3. The new sequence is
o: an AP with common difference d + 3
an AP with common difference d
questions.e: If Tₙ = a + (n − 1)d, then 3Tₙ = 3a + (n − 1)(3d), an AP with first term 3a and difference 3d. Adding 3 to each term, not multiplying, would keep the difference d.

questions.s: Every term of a geometric progression with common ratio r is squared. The new sequence is
o: a GP with common ratio r²
an AP with common difference r²
questions.e: (arⁿ⁻¹)² = a²(r²)ⁿ⁻¹, a GP with first term a² and ratio r². For example 1, 3, 9, … becomes 1, 9, 81, … with ratio 9 = 3², not 2r = 6.

questions.s: Three non-zero numbers a, b, c are in arithmetic progression and also in geometric progression. Then
questions.e: AP gives b = (a + c)/2 and GP gives b² = ac. So (a + c)²/4 = ac, i.e. (a − c)² = 0, giving a = c and then b = a. A constant sequence is both an AP (d = 0) and a GP (r = 1).

questions.s: The first, second and fifth terms of an AP with non-zero common difference are in geometric progression. The common ratio of this GP is
questions.e: (a + d)² = a(a + 4d) gives a² + 2ad + d² = a² + 4ad, so d² = 2ad and d = 2a. The terms a, 3a, 9a have ratio 3. The value 2 is d/a, not the ratio of the GP.

questions.s: A square has side 8 cm. A second square is drawn by joining the midpoints of its sides, a third by joining the midpoints of the second, and so on without end. The sum of the areas of all the squares is
questions.e: Joining midpoints halves the area, so the areas are 64, 32, 16, … with r = 1/2. The sum is 64/(1 − 1/2) = 128 cm². The side shrinks by the factor 1/√2, but the area by 1/2; taking twice the side-based sum would wrongly give 256 cm².

questions.s: The 6th term of the geometric progression 1/9, 1/3, 1, … is
questions.e: a = 1/9 and r = 3, so T₆ = (1/9) × 3⁵ = 243/9 = 27. The value 81 is the 7th term.

questions.s: The common difference of the arithmetic progression 1/2, 1/3, 1/6, … is
questions.e: d = 1/3 − 1/2 = −1/6, and 1/6 − 1/3 = −1/6 confirms it. The sign matters: the terms decrease, so d = +1/6 is wrong.

questions.s: The sum of the first 10 terms of the geometric progression 1, −1, 1, −1, … is
questions.e: Here r = −1, so Sₙ = (1 − (−1)ⁿ)/2, which is 0 for even n; the terms cancel in pairs. The value 1 would be the sum of an odd number of terms.

questions.s: Which of the following sequences is a geometric progression?
questions.e: In 3, 6, 12, 24 each term is 2 times the one before, so r = 2. The sequence 2, 4, 6, 8 is an AP, 1, 4, 9, 16 are squares, and 1, 1/2, 1/3, 1/4 is an HP.

questions.s: Which of the following sequences is a harmonic progression?
questions.e: The reciprocals of 1/2, 1/4, 1/6, 1/8 are 2, 4, 6, 8, an AP, so the sequence is an HP. The reciprocals of 1, 1/2, 1/4, 1/8 are 1, 2, 4, 8, a GP, so that sequence is a GP, not an HP.

questions.s: The arithmetic mean between x − 3 and x + 5 is
