questions.e: (1 + y)ⁿ ≈ 1 + ny with n = −3 and y = −x gives 1 + (−3)(−x) = 1 + 3x. 1 − 3x forgets that y = −x is also negative.

questions.s: The binomial expansion of (3 + x)^(1/2) in ascending powers of x is valid for
questions.e: Write (3 + x)^(1/2) = √3(1 + x/3)^(1/2). The series needs |x/3| < 1, that is |x| < 3. |x| < 1 forgets to take out the 3, and |x| < 1/3 inverts it.

questions.s: The coefficient of x³ in the expansion of (1 − x)^(1/2) for |x| < 1 is
questions.e: n(n − 1)(n − 2)/3! with n = 1/2 is (1/2)(−1/2)(−3/2)/6 = (3/8)/6 = 1/16, and (−x)³ = −x³ makes it −1/16. 1/16 forgets the sign of (−x)³, and −1/8 is the x² coefficient.

questions.s: Using the binomial series, 1/1.02 correct to four decimal places is
questions.e: (1 + 0.02)⁻¹ = 1 − 0.02 + 0.0004 − 0.000008 + … ≈ 0.98039, which rounds to 0.9804. 0.9800 stops after two terms, and 0.9796 subtracts the x² term although it is positive.

questions.s: If x is so small that x² and higher powers can be neglected, then √((1 + x)/(1 − x)) is approximately
questions.e: (1 + x)^(1/2) ≈ 1 + x/2 and (1 − x)^(−1/2) ≈ 1 + x/2, so the product is about 1 + x/2 + x/2 = 1 + x. 1 + x/2 uses only one of the two factors, and 1 assumes the x terms cancel.

questions.s: For every positive integer n, 1·2 + 2·3 + 3·4 + … + n(n + 1) equals
questions.e: For n = 1 both sides are 2. If the sum up to k is k(k + 1)(k + 2)/3, adding (k + 1)(k + 2) gives (k + 1)(k + 2)(k + 3)/3, which is the formula for k + 1. Dividing by 6 instead of 3 gives 1 for n = 1, not 2.

questions.s: The period of f(x) = sin 3x is
questions.e: For sin(bx) the period is 2π/b, so sin 3x repeats every 2π/3. Writing 6π multiplies by 3 instead of dividing, and 3π/2 inverts the fraction.

questions.s: The period of f(x) = tan(x/2) is
questions.e: tan x has period π, so tan(bx) has period π/b; with b = 1/2 the period is π ÷ (1/2) = 2π. The value 4π comes from using 2π as the basic period of tangent.

questions.s: The period of f(x) = cos²x is
questions.e: cos²x = (1 + cos 2x)/2, and cos 2x has period 2π/2 = π. Squaring removes the sign change, so the period halves from 2π to π; 2π is the period of cos x itself.

questions.s: The period of f(x) = |cos 2x| is
questions.e: cos 2x has period π, and the modulus makes the negative half-wave repeat the positive one, halving the period to π/2. π is the period before taking the modulus.

questions.s: The period of f(x) = sin x + cos x is
questions.e: sin x + cos x = √2 sin(x + π/4), a single sine wave of period 2π. Adding the two functions does not halve the period; π would be the period of sin x cos x.

questions.s: The period of f(x) = sin 2x + cos 3x is
questions.e: sin 2x has period π = 3π/3 and cos 3x has period 2π/3. The period of the sum is the least common multiple: in units of π/3 these are 3 and 2, whose LCM is 6, giving 6 × π/3 = 2π. 6π multiplies the periods instead of taking their LCM.

questions.s: The maximum value of 3 sin x + 4 cos x is
questions.e: a sin x + b cos x = √(a² + b²) sin(x + α), so its maximum is √(9 + 16) = 5. Adding 3 + 4 = 7 assumes sin x and cos x are both 1 at the same x, which never happens.

questions.s: The range of f(x) = 2 − 3 cos x is
questions.e: cos x runs over [−1, 1], so −3 cos x runs over [−3, 3] and 2 − 3 cos x over [−1, 5]. [−3, 3] forgets the vertical shift of 2.

questions.s: The amplitude of y = −4 sin(2x − π/3) is
questions.e: Amplitude is the modulus of the coefficient of the sine, |−4| = 4; the minus sign only reflects the graph in the x-axis. An amplitude is never negative, so −4 is wrong.

questions.s: The period of f(x) = cosec(πx) is
questions.e: cosec x has period 2π, so cosec(bx) has period 2π/b = 2π/π = 2. Writing 2π ignores the factor π inside the function.

questions.s: The period of f(x) = tan 3x + cot 3x is
questions.e: Both tan 3x and cot 3x have period π/3. Also tan 3x + cot 3x = 1/(sin 3x cos 3x) = 2 cosec 6x, whose period is 2π/6 = π/3, so no smaller period exists. π/6 wrongly halves it as if the function were squared.

questions.s: Which of the following functions has period π?
questions.e: tan x repeats every π because tan(x + π) = tan x. sin x and sec x have period 2π, and cos(x/2) has period 4π.

questions.s: On the interval 0 ≤ x ≤ 2π, the graph of y = sin x meets the x-axis at how many points?
questions.e: sin x = 0 at x = 0, π and 2π, which are all in the closed interval, so there are 3 points. Answering 2 forgets that both end points count.

questions.s: The vertical asymptotes of the graph of y = tan x are the lines
questions.e: tan x = sin x/cos x is undefined where cos x = 0, that is at odd multiples of π/2. The lines x = nπ are the asymptotes of cot x, where sin x = 0.

questions.s: The domain of f(x) = cot x is
o: all real x except x = nπ, n ∈ Z
questions.e: cot x = cos x/sin x is undefined where sin x = 0, i.e. at every integer multiple of π. Excluding odd multiples of π/2 gives the domain of tan x instead.

questions.s: The range of f(x) = sec x is
questions.e: sec x = 1/cos x and 0 < |cos x| ≤ 1, so |sec x| ≥ 1. [−1, 1] is the range of cos x, and (−1, 1) is exactly the set of values sec x never takes.

questions.s: The minimum value of sin²x − 4 sin x + 5 is
questions.e: Write it as (sin x − 2)² + 1. Since sin x ≤ 1, sin x − 2 is between −3 and −1, so the square is least (= 1) at sin x = 1, giving 1 + 1 = 2. The value 1 assumes sin x can equal 2.

questions.s: The greatest value of sin x cos x is
questions.e: sin x cos x = ½ sin 2x, and sin 2x ≤ 1, so the greatest value is ½, at x = π/4. The answer 1 treats sin x and cos x as both reaching 1 together.

questions.s: The period of f(x) = sin⁴x + cos⁴x is
questions.e: sin⁴x + cos⁴x = (sin²x + cos²x)² − 2 sin²x cos²x = 1 − ½ sin²2x = 3/4 + ¼ cos 4x. cos 4x has period 2π/4 = π/2. π is the period of sin⁴x alone, but the sum repeats sooner.

questions.s: For 0 ≤ x ≤ π, the greatest value of y = 3 sin 2x + 1 and the value of x where it occurs are
questions.e: sin 2x = 1 when 2x = π/2, i.e. x = π/4, giving y = 3 + 1 = 4. At x = π/2, sin 2x = sin π = 0 so y = 1; −2 at 3π/4 is the least value, not the greatest.

questions.s: The period of f(x) = sin(πx/4) is
questions.e: Period = 2π ÷ (π/4) = 8. The π cancels, so 8π is wrong, and 1/8 comes from dividing the wrong way round.

questions.s: The graph of y = cos x is symmetric about
questions.e: cos(−x) = cos x, so cosine is an even function and its graph is a mirror image in the y-axis. Symmetry about the origin belongs to odd functions such as sin x.

questions.s: The graph of y = sin(x − π/3) is obtained from the graph of y = sin x by a shift of
questions.e: Replacing x by x − π/3 moves every point π/3 to the right, since the new graph reaches each value π/3 later. A vertical shift would need a constant added outside the sine.

questions.s: The period of f(x) = |sin x| + |cos x| is
questions.e: f(x + π/2) = |sin(x + π/2)| + |cos(x + π/2)| = |cos x| + |sin x| = f(x), so π/2 is a period, and f(0) = 1 while f(π/4) = √2 shows no shorter one works. π is the period of each modulus term separately.

questions.s: If f(x) = a sin(bx), where a > 0 and b > 0, has greatest value 3 and period 4π, then ab equals
questions.e: The greatest value gives a = 3 and the period gives 2π/b = 4π, so b = 1/2 and ab = 3/2. Taking b = 4π/2π = 2, i.e. dividing the period by 2π, gives 6.

questions.s: In triangle ABC, a = 3, b = 5 and C = 120°. The side c equals
questions.e: c² = a² + b² − 2ab cos C = 9 + 25 − 30(−½) = 34 + 15 = 49, so c = 7. Taking cos 120° = +½ gives 34 − 15 = 19 and the wrong value √19.

questions.s: In triangle ABC, a = 6 cm, b = 8 cm and C = 30°. The area of the triangle is
questions.e: Area = ½ab sin C = ½ × 6 × 8 × ½ = 12 cm². Using sin 60° instead of sin 30° gives 12√3 cm², and leaving out the ½ gives 24 cm².

questions.s: The circum-radius of a triangle with sides 3 cm, 4 cm and 5 cm is
questions.e: 3² + 4² = 5², so the triangle is right-angled and the hypotenuse is a diameter of the circumcircle: R = 5/2 cm. Check: R = abc/(4Δ) = 60/24 = 5/2. The value 1 cm is the in-radius.

questions.s: The in-radius of a triangle with sides 5, 12 and 13 is
questions.e: The triangle is right-angled, so Δ = ½ × 5 × 12 = 30 and s = (5 + 12 + 13)/2 = 15. Then r = Δ/s = 30/15 = 2. The value 13/2 is the circum-radius, not the in-radius.

questions.s: In triangle ABC, A = 30°, B = 90° and a = 4. The side b equals
questions.e: By the sine rule b = a sin B/sin A = 4 × 1/(½) = 8. The value 4√3 is the third side c, opposite the 60° angle.

questions.s: The sides of a triangle are in the ratio 7 : 8 : 13. Its largest angle is
questions.e: Take sides 7, 8, 13. The largest angle is opposite 13: cos θ = (49 + 64 − 169)/(2 × 7 × 8) = −56/112 = −½, so θ = 120°. A negative cosine rules out 90°.

questions.s: The area of a triangle with sides 13, 14 and 15 is
questions.e: s = 21, so by Hero's formula Δ = √(21 × 8 × 7 × 6) = √7056 = 84. 42 is half the area and 168 is twice it, so check the product 21 × 8 × 7 × 6 = 7056 = 84².

questions.s: A triangle has sides 13 cm, 14 cm and 15 cm. Its in-radius is
questions.e: s = 21 and Δ = √(21 × 8 × 7 × 6) = 84, so r = Δ/s = 84/21 = 4 cm. The value 65/8 cm is the circum-radius abc/(4Δ) = 2730/336.

questions.s: In any triangle ABC with circum-radius R, the ratio a/sin A equals
questions.e: The sine rule in full is a/sin A = b/sin B = c/sin C = 2R. Writing R alone forgets that the chord a subtends 2A at the centre, which gives the factor 2.

questions.s: The in-radius of an equilateral triangle of side 6 cm is
questions.e: Δ = (√3/4) × 36 = 9√3 and s = 9, so r = Δ/s = √3 cm. 2√3 cm is the circum-radius and 3√3 cm is the full height.

questions.s: Which of the following is the law of tangents for triangle ABC?
questions.e: From the sine rule, (a − b)/(a + b) = (sin A − sin B)/(sin A + sin B) = tan((A − B)/2)/tan((A + B)/2) by sum-to-product. Swapping the two tangents inverts the ratio, and replacing tangents by sines does not give an identity.

questions.s: In triangle ABC, a = √3, b = 1 and c = 2. The angle B equals
questions.e: cos B = (a² + c² − b²)/(2ac) = (3 + 4 − 1)/(2 × √3 × 2) = 6/(4√3) = √3/2, so B = 30°. 60° is angle A, opposite the side √3.

questions.s: In triangle ABC, a = 13, b = 14 and c = 15. The value of tan(A/2) is
questions.e: s = 21, Δ = 84 and r = Δ/s = 4. Then tan(A/2) = r/(s − a) = 4/(21 − 13) = 1/2. Using s − b = 7 instead gives 4/7, which is tan(B/2).

questions.s: With s the semi-perimeter of triangle ABC, sin(A/2) equals
questions.e: From cos A = 1 − 2 sin²(A/2) and the cosine rule, sin²(A/2) = (a² − (b − c)²)/(4bc) = (s − b)(s − c)/(bc). √[s(s − a)/(bc)] is cos(A/2) and the third form is tan(A/2).

questions.s: In triangle ABC, A = 45°, B = 60° and a = 2√2. The side b equals
questions.e: b = a sin B/sin A = 2√2 × (√3/2) ÷ (√2/2) = 2√3. Swapping the sines gives 2√2 × (√2/2)/(√3/2) = 4/√3, and √6 comes from multiplying by sin B only.

questions.s: In triangle ABC, A = 30°, b = 8 and a = 5. How many triangles satisfy these data?
questions.e: sin B = b sin A/a = 8 × ½/5 = 4/5 < 1, so B can be acute or its supplement. Since b sin A = 4 < a = 5 < b = 8, both values of B leave room for C, giving two triangles (the ambiguous case).

questions.s: A triangle has sides 6, 8 and 10 and circum-radius 5. Using Δ = abc/(4R), its area is
questions.e: Δ = (6 × 8 × 10)/(4 × 5) = 480/20 = 24, which agrees with ½ × 6 × 8 for this right triangle. Forgetting the 4 in the denominator gives 96.

questions.s: In any triangle ABC, a cos B + b cos A equals
questions.e: Drop the perpendicular from C to AB: the projections of sides a and b on AB are a cos B and b cos A, and together they make up c (projection formula). a + b would be true only if both cosines were 1.

questions.s: In triangle ABC, a² + b² − ab = c². The angle C equals
questions.e: cos C = (a² + b² − c²)/(2ab) = ab/(2ab) = ½, so C = 60°. If the given relation had + ab, the cosine would be −½ and C would be 120°.

questions.s: For a triangle with sides a, b, c and area Δ, the expression abc/(4Δ) equals
questions.e: Δ = ½ab sin C and sin C = c/(2R), so Δ = abc/(4R) and R = abc/(4Δ). The in-radius is r = Δ/s instead.

questions.s: For the triangle with sides a = 5, b = 3 and c = 4, the escribed radius r₁ (of the circle touching side a) is
questions.e: Δ = ½ × 3 × 4 = 6 and s = 6, so r₁ = Δ/(s − a) = 6/(6 − 5) = 6. The value 1 is the in-radius Δ/s, and 2 and 3 are r₂ = 6/3 and r₃ = 6/2.

questions.s: The area of a triangle with sides 5 cm, 5 cm and 6 cm is
questions.e: s = 8, so Δ = √(8 × 3 × 3 × 2) = √144 = 12 cm². Equivalently the height to the base 6 is √(25 − 9) = 4, giving ½ × 6 × 4 = 12. 24 cm² forgets the ½.

questions.s: The angles of a triangle are in the ratio 1 : 2 : 3. The corresponding sides are in the ratio
questions.e: The angles are 30°, 60° and 90°, and by the sine rule the sides are as sin 30° : sin 60° : sin 90° = ½ : √3/2 : 1 = 1 : √3 : 2. Sides are proportional to the sines of the angles, not to the angles, so 1 : 2 : 3 is wrong.

questions.s: In triangle ABC, a = 2b cos C. The triangle must be
questions.e: Substitute cos C = (a² + b² − c²)/(2ab): a = (a² + b² − c²)/a, so a² = a² + b² − c² and b = c. Nothing forces a = b, so the triangle need not be equilateral.

questions.s: A triangle has sides 5, 7 and 8. The angle opposite the side of length 7 is
questions.e: cos θ = (5² + 8² − 7²)/(2 × 5 × 8) = 40/80 = ½, so θ = 60°. Since 5² + 7² ≠ 8², the triangle has no right angle.

questions.s: In triangle ABC, b = 4, c = 6 and A = 60°. The area of the triangle is
questions.e: Area = ½bc sin A = ½ × 4 × 6 × (√3/2) = 6√3. Using sin 30° = ½ gives 6, and dropping the ½ in front gives 12√3.

questions.s: In triangle ABC, a = 6 cm and A = 30°. The circum-radius of the triangle is
questions.e: a/sin A = 2R gives 2R = 6 ÷ ½ = 12, so R = 6 cm. The value 12 cm is the diameter 2R, not the radius.

questions.s: For an equilateral triangle, the ratio of its circum-radius to its in-radius is
questions.e: In an equilateral triangle the circumcentre and incentre coincide with the centroid, which divides each median 2 : 1; so R is two-thirds and r one-third of the height, and R : r = 2 : 1. √3 : 1 is the ratio of side to R.

questions.s: In triangle ABC, b = c, A = 120° and a = 6. The side b equals
questions.e: B = C = (180° − 120°)/2 = 30°, so by the sine rule b = a sin B/sin A = 6 × ½ ÷ (√3/2) = 6/√3 = 2√3. Taking b = a/2 = 3 ignores the sine rule.

questions.s: In triangle ABC, (a + b + c)(a + b − c) = 3ab. The angle C equals
questions.e: The left side is (a + b)² − c² = a² + 2ab + b² − c², so a² + b² − c² = ab and cos C = ab/(2ab) = ½, giving C = 60°. Reading a² + b² − c² = 3ab would give a cosine above 1, which is impossible.

questions.s: A triangle has in-radius 3 cm and semi-perimeter 12 cm. Its area is
questions.e: Δ = rs = 3 × 12 = 36 cm². Using the full perimeter 24 cm instead of s gives 72 cm², and 4 comes from dividing s by r.

questions.s: In triangle ABC, a = 2, b = √6 and c = √3 + 1. The angle A equals
questions.e: b² + c² − a² = 6 + (4 + 2√3) − 4 = 6 + 2√3 = 2√3(√3 + 1), and 2bc = 2√6(√3 + 1). So cos A = 2√3/(2√6) = 1/√2 and A = 45°. 75° is angle C, opposite the longest side √3 + 1.

questions.s: The circumcentre of a right-angled triangle lies
o: at the vertex of the right angle
at the centroid of the triangle
at the midpoint of the shortest side
at the midpoint of the hypotenuse
questions.e: The hypotenuse subtends a right angle at the opposite vertex, so it is a diameter of the circumcircle and the centre is its midpoint; hence R = hypotenuse/2. The centroid is the circumcentre only for an equilateral triangle.

questions.s: In triangle ABC, a = 4, b = 5 and c = 6. The value of cos C is
questions.e: cos C = (a² + b² − c²)/(2ab) = (16 + 25 − 36)/40 = 5/40 = 1/8. The values 3/4 and 9/16 are cos A and cos B, obtained by putting the wrong side on the minus.

questions.s: In triangle ABC, a = 3, b = 1 and C = 60°. By the law of tangents, tan((A − B)/2) equals
questions.e: tan((A − B)/2) = ((a − b)/(a + b)) cot(C/2) = (2/4) × cot 30° = ½ × √3 = √3/2. Using tan 30° instead of cot 30° gives 1/(2√3).

questions.s: The principal value of sin⁻¹(1/2) is
questions.e: sin(π/6) = ½ and π/6 lies in the principal range [−π/2, π/2]. 5π/6 also has sine ½ but lies outside that range; π/3 is cos⁻¹(½).

questions.s: The principal value of cos⁻¹(−1/2) is
questions.e: The principal range of cos⁻¹ is [0, π]; cos(2π/3) = −½, and cos⁻¹(−x) = π − cos⁻¹x = π − π/3. −π/3 has cosine +½ and is outside the range anyway.

questions.s: The principal value of tan⁻¹(−√3) is
questions.e: tan(π/3) = √3 and tan⁻¹ is odd, so tan⁻¹(−√3) = −π/3, which lies in (−π/2, π/2). 2π/3 has the same tangent but is outside the principal range.

questions.s: The range (principal values) of y = sin⁻¹x is
questions.e: sin x is one-to-one on [−π/2, π/2] and takes every value in [−1, 1] there, so sin⁻¹ maps onto this closed interval; sin⁻¹(1) = π/2 is included. [0, π] is the range of cos⁻¹x, and the open interval is the range of tan⁻¹x.

questions.s: The value of sin⁻¹(sin 5π/6) is
questions.e: sin(5π/6) = sin(π − π/6) = ½, and sin⁻¹(½) = π/6. The answer 5π/6 ignores that sin⁻¹ only returns values in [−π/2, π/2].

questions.s: The value of cos⁻¹(cos 4π/3) is
questions.e: cos(4π/3) = −½, and the angle in [0, π] with cosine −½ is 2π/3 (equivalently 2π − 4π/3). 4π/3 is outside the principal range of cos⁻¹.

questions.s: The value of tan⁻¹(1/2) + tan⁻¹(1/3) is
questions.e: tan⁻¹x + tan⁻¹y = tan⁻¹((x + y)/(1 − xy)) when xy < 1: (½ + ⅓)/(1 − 1/6) = (5/6)/(5/6) = 1, and tan⁻¹1 = π/4. π/2 would need xy = 1.

questions.s: The value of sin(cos⁻¹(3/5)) is
questions.e: Let θ = cos⁻¹(3/5), an angle in [0, π] with cos θ = 3/5, so sin θ = +√(1 − 9/25) = 4/5. The value 3/4 is cot θ = cos θ/sin θ, not sin θ.

questions.s: The value of tan(sin⁻¹(5/13)) is
questions.e: Let θ = sin⁻¹(5/13), so sin θ = 5/13 with θ acute; then cos θ = 12/13 and tan θ = 5/12. The value 12/5 is cot θ.

questions.s: For −1 ≤ x ≤ 1, sin⁻¹x + cos⁻¹x equals
questions.e: If sin⁻¹x = θ then x = cos(π/2 − θ) with π/2 − θ in [0, π], so cos⁻¹x = π/2 − θ and the sum is π/2 for every allowed x. The value π is wrong: for x = 1 the sum is π/2 + 0.

questions.s: The value of cos(2 tan⁻¹(1/2)) is
questions.e: With tan θ = ½, cos 2θ = (1 − tan²θ)/(1 + tan²θ) = (3/4)/(5/4) = 3/5. The value 4/5 is sin 2θ = 2 tan θ/(1 + tan²θ), and 2/√5 is cos θ.

questions.s: The domain of f(x) = cos⁻¹(2x − 1) is
questions.e: cos⁻¹ needs −1 ≤ 2x − 1 ≤ 1, so 0 ≤ 2x ≤ 2 and 0 ≤ x ≤ 1. [−1, 1] is the domain of cos⁻¹x itself, before the substitution.

questions.s: The value of 2 tan⁻¹(1/3) + tan⁻¹(1/7) is
questions.e: 2 tan⁻¹(1/3) = tan⁻¹((2/3)/(1 − 1/9)) = tan⁻¹(3/4). Then tan⁻¹(3/4) + tan⁻¹(1/7) = tan⁻¹((3/4 + 1/7)/(1 − 3/28)) = tan⁻¹((25/28)/(25/28)) = tan⁻¹1 = π/4. Doubling 1/3 to 2/3 inside the tan⁻¹ is the usual mistake.

questions.s: The value of sin⁻¹(3/5) + sin⁻¹(4/5) is
questions.e: If sin⁻¹(3/5) = θ (acute), then cos θ = 4/5, so sin⁻¹(4/5) = π/2 − θ and the sum is π/2. Adding the arguments to get sin⁻¹(7/5) is meaningless since 7/5 > 1.

questions.s: For real x, cos(tan⁻¹x) equals
questions.e: Let θ = tan⁻¹x in (−π/2, π/2), where cos θ > 0. Then sec²θ = 1 + x², so cos θ = 1/√(1 + x²). x/√(1 + x²) is sin θ.

questions.s: The principal value of cot⁻¹(−1), with range (0, π), is
questions.e: cot⁻¹(−x) = π − cot⁻¹x, so cot⁻¹(−1) = π − π/4 = 3π/4, and cot(3π/4) = −1. −π/4 also has cotangent −1 but is outside (0, π).

questions.s: The principal value of sec⁻¹(2) is
questions.e: sec⁻¹2 = cos⁻¹(½) = π/3, since sec θ = 2 means cos θ = ½. π/6 is cosec⁻¹2, where sin θ = ½.

questions.s: The principal value of cosec⁻¹(−2), with range [−π/2, π/2] excluding 0, is
questions.e: cosec⁻¹(−2) = sin⁻¹(−½) = −π/6. 7π/6 has sine −½ too, but it lies outside the principal range; −π/3 has sine −√3/2.

questions.s: The value of sin(sin⁻¹(1/3) + cos⁻¹(1/3)) is
questions.e: For any x in [−1, 1], sin⁻¹x + cos⁻¹x = π/2, so the expression is sin(π/2) = 1. Expanding with the compound-angle formula gives the same result, (1/9) + (8/9) = 1, while 2/3 comes from adding the two arguments.

questions.s: If sin⁻¹x = π/5, then cos⁻¹x equals
questions.e: sin⁻¹x + cos⁻¹x = π/2, so cos⁻¹x = π/2 − π/5 = 3π/10. 4π/5 = π − π/5 uses π instead of π/2.

questions.s: The value of tan⁻¹2 + tan⁻¹3 is
questions.e: Here xy = 6 > 1 with x, y > 0, so tan⁻¹2 + tan⁻¹3 = π + tan⁻¹((2 + 3)/(1 − 6)) = π + tan⁻¹(−1) = π − π/4 = 3π/4. The formula without the π gives −π/4, impossible since both angles are positive.

questions.s: Which of the following is true for all x in the domain?
questions.e: cos⁻¹ takes values in [0, π], and cos(π − θ) = −cos θ, so cos⁻¹(−x) = π − cos⁻¹x. sin⁻¹ and tan⁻¹ are odd functions, so for them the correct rule is f(−x) = −f(x); −cos⁻¹x would be negative, outside [0, π].

questions.s: The value of x for which sin⁻¹x = cos⁻¹x is
questions.e: Their sum is π/2, so each equals π/4 and x = sin(π/4) = 1/√2. At x = ½ the values are π/6 and π/3, which are not equal.

questions.s: For x > −1, the solution of tan⁻¹((1 − x)/(1 + x)) = ½ tan⁻¹x is
questions.e: tan⁻¹((1 − x)/(1 + x)) = tan⁻¹1 − tan⁻¹x = π/4 − tan⁻¹x. So π/4 = (3/2) tan⁻¹x, tan⁻¹x = π/6 and x = 1/√3. x = √3 would make tan⁻¹x = π/3 and the left side negative.

questions.s: The value of sin(2 sin⁻¹(3/5)) is
questions.e: With sin θ = 3/5 (θ acute), cos θ = 4/5 and sin 2θ = 2 × 3/5 × 4/5 = 24/25. 6/5 just doubles 3/5, impossible for a sine; 7/25 is cos 2θ.

questions.s: The value of sec(tan⁻¹(3/4)) is
questions.e: With tan θ = 3/4 (θ acute), sec²θ = 1 + 9/16 = 25/16, so sec θ = 5/4. 5/3 is cosec θ and 4/5 is cos θ.

questions.s: cos⁻¹(4/5) + cos⁻¹(12/13) equals
questions.e: Let cos α = 4/5, sin α = 3/5 and cos β = 12/13, sin β = 5/13. Then cos(α + β) = (4/5)(12/13) − (3/5)(5/13) = (48 − 15)/65 = 33/65, and α + β is in [0, π]. 63/65 is cos(α − β), from adding the products.

questions.s: The domain of f(x) = sin⁻¹(x/3) is
questions.e: We need −1 ≤ x/3 ≤ 1, i.e. −3 ≤ x ≤ 3. [−1/3, 1/3] comes from dividing by 3 instead of multiplying.

questions.s: For x > 0, tan⁻¹x + tan⁻¹(1/x) equals
questions.e: tan⁻¹(1/x) = cot⁻¹x for x > 0, and tan⁻¹x + cot⁻¹x = π/2. For x = 1 this is π/4 + π/4 = π/2, which checks; π/4 is only one of the two terms at x = 1.

questions.s: The value of sin⁻¹(sin 10), where 10 is in radians, is
questions.e: 3π ≈ 9.42, so 10 = 3π + 0.58 and sin 10 = sin(3π + 0.58) = −sin 0.58 = sin(3π − 10). Since 3π − 10 ≈ −0.58 lies in [−π/2, π/2], it is the principal value. 10 − 3π has the wrong sign and 10 − 4π ≈ −2.57 is outside the range.

questions.s: The value of tan(½ cos⁻¹(3/5)) is
questions.e: With cos θ = 3/5 (θ acute), tan(θ/2) = √((1 − cos θ)/(1 + cos θ)) = √((2/5)/(8/5)) = √(1/4) = ½. 4/3 is tan θ itself, before halving.

questions.s: The graph of y = tan⁻¹x has horizontal asymptotes
questions.e: As x → ∞, tan⁻¹x → π/2, and as x → −∞ it tends to −π/2, never reaching either. The vertical lines x = ±π/2 are asymptotes of tan x, the reflection of this graph in y = x.

questions.s: The value of sin⁻¹(1) + cos⁻¹(−1) is
questions.e: sin⁻¹1 = π/2 and cos⁻¹(−1) = π, so the sum is 3π/2. Treating cos⁻¹(−1) as 0 (confusing it with cos⁻¹1) gives π/2.

questions.s: If x, y, z > 0 and tan⁻¹x + tan⁻¹y + tan⁻¹z = π, then
questions.e: tan(A + B + C) = (x + y + z − xyz)/(1 − xy − yz − zx), and tan π = 0, so x + y + z = xyz. The condition xy + yz + zx = 1 is the one for a sum of π/2, where the denominator vanishes.

questions.s: If cos⁻¹x + cos⁻¹y = π, then
questions.e: cos⁻¹y = π − cos⁻¹x = cos⁻¹(−x), and cos⁻¹ is one-to-one, so y = −x. The relation x = y would come from cos⁻¹x + cos⁻¹y = 2 cos⁻¹x, which is not given.

questions.s: The general solution of sin x = 0 is
questions.e: sin x = 0 at x = 0, ±π, ±2π, …, i.e. every integer multiple of π. x = 2nπ misses odd multiples such as π, and (2n + 1)π/2 gives the zeros of cos x.

questions.s: The general solution of cos x = 1/2 is
questions.e: cos(π/3) = ½, and cos x = cos α gives x = 2nπ ± α. nπ ± π/3 would include 2π/3, where cosine is −½; the (−1)ⁿ form is the general solution for sine.

questions.s: The general solution of tan 2x = 1 is
questions.e: tan 2x = 1 gives 2x = nπ + π/4, so x = nπ/2 + π/8. Halving only π/4 and not nπ gives nπ + π/8, which loses half the solutions (e.g. x = 5π/8).

questions.s: The number of solutions of 2 sin²x − 1 = 0 in 0 ≤ x < 2π is
questions.e: sin²x = ½ gives sin x = ±1/√2, so x = π/4, 3π/4, 5π/4, 7π/4: four solutions. Taking only the positive root gives 2.

questions.s: The solutions of sin x + cos x = 1 in 0 ≤ x < 2π are
questions.e: sin x + cos x = √2 sin(x + π/4) = 1 gives sin(x + π/4) = 1/√2, so x + π/4 = π/4 or 3π/4, i.e. x = 0 or π/2. At x = π, sin x + cos x = −1, and at π/4 it is √2.

questions.s: The general solution of tan x = √3 is
questions.e: tan(π/3) = √3 and tangent has period π, so x = nπ + π/3. 2nπ + π/3 misses solutions such as 4π/3, and π/6 has tangent 1/√3.

questions.s: The general solution of sin x = −1 is
questions.e: sin x = −1 only at x = 3π/2 in each turn, i.e. at −π/2 + 2nπ. nπ − π/2 would also include π/2, where sin x = +1.

questions.s: The solutions of 2cos²x − cos x − 1 = 0 in 0 ≤ x < 2π are
questions.e: Factorise: (2 cos x + 1)(cos x − 1) = 0, so cos x = 1 (x = 0) or cos x = −½ (x = 2π/3, 4π/3). Using cos x = +½ by a sign slip gives π/3 and 5π/3.

questions.s: The number of solutions of sin 2x = cos x in 0 ≤ x ≤ π is
questions.e: 2 sin x cos x − cos x = cos x(2 sin x − 1) = 0. cos x = 0 gives x = π/2, and sin x = ½ gives x = π/6, 5π/6: three solutions. Dividing by cos x loses π/2 and leaves only 2.

questions.s: The general solution of sin x = √3/2 is
questions.e: sin(π/3) = √3/2, and sin x = sin α gives x = nπ + (−1)ⁿα, i.e. π/3, 2π/3, 7π/3, … The ± form belongs to cosine: it would include −π/3, where sine is negative.

questions.s: The general solution of tan²x = 3 is
questions.e: tan x = ±√3, so x = nπ + π/3 or nπ − π/3, i.e. nπ ± π/3. Keeping only tan x = √3 loses the negative root, and 2nπ wrongly uses the period of sine.

questions.s: The general solution of cos 2x = 0 is
questions.e: cos 2x = 0 gives 2x = (2n + 1)π/2, so x = (2n + 1)π/4 = π/4, 3π/4, 5π/4, … nπ + π/4 misses 3π/4, and (2n + 1)π/2 forgets to halve.

questions.s: The solutions of sin 3x = sin x in 0 < x < π are
questions.e: sin 3x − sin x = 2 cos 2x sin x = 0. In (0, π), sin x ≠ 0, so cos 2x = 0 and 2x = π/2 or 3π/2, giving x = π/4, 3π/4. At x = π/2, sin 3x = −1 while sin x = 1, so π/2 is not a solution.

questions.s: The solutions of √3 tan x − 1 = 0 in 0 ≤ x < 2π are
questions.e: tan x = 1/√3 gives x = π/6, and since tangent has period π the next solution is π/6 + π = 7π/6. At 5π/6 the tangent is negative.

questions.s: The general solution of sec x = −2 is
questions.e: sec x = −2 means cos x = −½ = cos(2π/3), so x = 2nπ ± 2π/3. 2nπ ± π/3 solves cos x = +½, and 2nπ ± 5π/6 would solve cos x = −√3/2.

questions.s: The general solution of √3 cos x + sin x = √2 is
o: x = nπ + π/6 ± π/4, n ∈ Z
questions.e: √3 cos x + sin x = 2(cos x cos π/6 + sin x sin π/6) = 2 cos(x − π/6). So cos(x − π/6) = 1/√2 and x − π/6 = 2nπ ± π/4. Using nπ instead of 2nπ includes values where the cosine is −1/√2.

questions.s: The number of solutions of sin²x − sin x = 0 in 0 ≤ x < 2π is
questions.e: sin x(sin x − 1) = 0: sin x = 0 gives x = 0, π, and sin x = 1 gives x = π/2, so there are 3 solutions. Cancelling sin x loses 0 and π.

questions.s: The solutions of sin 2x = 1/2 in 0 ≤ x ≤ π are
questions.e: With 0 ≤ 2x ≤ 2π, sin 2x = ½ gives 2x = π/6 or 5π/6, so x = π/12 or 5π/12. π/6 and 5π/6 are the values of 2x, not of x.

questions.s: The solutions of tan x + sec x = √3 in 0 ≤ x < 2π are
questions.e: Multiply by cos x: sin x + 1 = √3 cos x, i.e. √3 cos x − sin x = 2 cos(x + π/6) = 1, so x + π/6 = π/3 or 5π/3, giving x = π/6 or 3π/2. At 3π/2, cos x = 0 and tan x, sec x are undefined, so it must be rejected.

questions.s: The solutions of sin x = 1/√2 in 0 ≤ x < 2π are
questions.e: Sine is positive in the first and second quadrants, so x = π/4 and π − π/4 = 3π/4. π/4 and 7π/4 are the solutions of cos x = 1/√2.

questions.s: The general solution of 4 sin²x = 3 is
questions.e: sin²x = 3/4 = sin²(π/3), and sin²x = sin²α gives x = nπ ± α. The (−1)ⁿ form solves only sin x = +√3/2 and misses the negative root.

questions.s: The solutions of 2 sin²x + 3 cos x = 0 in 0 ≤ x < 2π are
questions.e: Replace sin²x by 1 − cos²x: 2cos²x − 3 cos x − 2 = 0, so (2 cos x + 1)(cos x − 2) = 0. cos x = 2 is impossible, and cos x = −½ gives 2π/3 and 4π/3.

questions.s: The general solution of tan x + cot x = 2 is
questions.e: tan x + cot x = 1/(sin x cos x) = 2/sin 2x = 2, so sin 2x = 1, 2x = 2nπ + π/2 and x = nπ + π/4. nπ/2 + π/4 includes 3π/4, where tan x + cot x = −2.

questions.s: The general solution of sin 2x = sin x is
o: x = nπ or x = 2nπ ± π/6, n ∈ Z
x = nπ or x = nπ ± π/3, n ∈ Z
x = nπ or x = 2nπ ± π/3, n ∈ Z
questions.e: sin x(2 cos x − 1) = 0, so sin x = 0 (x = nπ) or cos x = ½ (x = 2nπ ± π/3). Dividing by sin x loses x = nπ, and nπ ± π/3 includes 2π/3, where sin 2x = −√3/2 but sin x = √3/2.

questions.s: Which of the following is a solution of cos 2x = −1?
questions.e: cos 2x = −1 needs 2x = π (+ 2nπ), so x = π/2 works: cos π = −1. At x = π, cos 2π = 1, and at π/4 or 3π/4, cos 2x = 0.

questions.s: The general solution of tan 3x = tan x is
questions.e: tan 3x = tan x gives 3x = nπ + x, so x = nπ/2. For odd n, x = π/2, 3π/2, … where tan x is undefined, so those must be dropped, leaving x = nπ. Stopping at nπ/2 is the trap.

questions.s: The solutions of 2 cos x + √2 = 0 in 0 ≤ x < 2π are
questions.e: cos x = −1/√2, and cosine is negative in the second and third quadrants: x = π − π/4 = 3π/4 and π + π/4 = 5π/4. π/4 and 7π/4 solve cos x = +1/√2.

questions.s: The solution of sin(x + π/6) = 1 in 0 ≤ x < 2π is
questions.e: sin(x + π/6) = 1 needs x + π/6 = π/2 (the next value, 5π/2, gives x outside the interval), so x = π/2 − π/6 = π/3. Adding π/6 instead of subtracting gives 2π/3.

questions.s: The smallest positive value of x satisfying cos 3x = −1 is
questions.e: cos 3x = −1 needs 3x = π, 3π, …; the smallest positive is 3x = π, so x = π/3. x = π is also a solution (3x = 3π) but not the smallest; at π/6 cos 3x = cos(π/2) = 0.

questions.s: The general solution of sin x + √3 cos x = 2 is
questions.e: sin x + √3 cos x = 2 sin(x + π/3), so sin(x + π/3) = 1, x + π/3 = 2nπ + π/2 and x = 2nπ + π/6. Check: sin(π/6) + √3 cos(π/6) = ½ + 3/2 = 2. nπ + π/6 includes 7π/6, where the left side is −2.

questions.s: The number of solutions of cos 2x + cos x + 1 = 0 in 0 ≤ x < 2π is
questions.e: cos 2x = 2cos²x − 1, so the equation becomes 2cos²x + cos x = cos x(2 cos x + 1) = 0. cos x = 0 gives π/2, 3π/2 and cos x = −½ gives 2π/3, 4π/3: four solutions. Dividing by cos x leaves only 2.

questions.s: The number of real solutions of the equation sin x = x is
questions.e: The line y = x touches the curve y = sin x only at the origin: for x > 0, sin x < x, and for x < 0, sin x > x. So x = 0 is the only solution, and the graphs never meet elsewhere.

questions.s: The number of real solutions of cos x = |x| is
questions.e: At x = 0, cos 0 = 1 ≠ 0. For x > 0, g(x) = cos x − x falls steadily (g′ = −sin x − 1 ≤ 0) from 1 to negative values, so it has exactly one zero; by symmetry there is one negative solution too. Counting only the positive root gives 1.

questions.s: The general solution of 2 sin x + 1 = 0 is
questions.e: sin x = −½ = sin(−π/6), so x = nπ + (−1)ⁿ(−π/6) = nπ + (−1)ⁿ⁺¹π/6: this gives −π/6, 7π/6, … The (−1)ⁿπ/6 form solves sin x = +½ instead.

questions.s: The general solution of sin⁴x + cos⁴x = 1/2 is
questions.e: sin⁴x + cos⁴x = 1 − 2 sin²x cos²x = 1 − ½ sin²2x, so sin²2x = 1 and 2x = nπ + π/2, giving x = nπ/2 + π/4. nπ + π/4 misses 3π/4, where sin 2x = −1 also works.

questions.s: The period of f(x) = 3 tan(2x + 1) is
questions.e: tan has period π, so tan(2x + 1) has period π/2; the factor 3 and the shift 1 change neither. π is the period of tan x before the 2 inside.

questions.s: The range of f(x) = 5 sin x − 12 cos x + 3 is
questions.e: 5 sin x − 12 cos x = 13 sin(x − α) with 13 = √(25 + 144), so it ranges over [−13, 13] and adding 3 gives [−10, 16]. [−13, 13] forgets the + 3, and [−14, 20] uses 5 + 12 = 17 instead of √(5² + 12²).

questions.s: The period of f(x) = sin(x/2) + cos(x/3) is
questions.e: sin(x/2) has period 4π and cos(x/3) has period 6π. The sum repeats at their least common multiple, 12π. 24π is a common period but not the least.

questions.s: The greatest value of f(x) = 7 − 2 cos x is
questions.e: −2 cos x is greatest (= 2) when cos x = −1, so the greatest value is 7 + 2 = 9. The value 5 is the least value, at cos x = 1.

questions.s: In 0 ≤ x ≤ 2π, the graphs of y = sin x and y = cos x intersect at
questions.e: sin x = cos x means tan x = 1, so x = π/4 or π/4 + π = 5π/4 (both have equal sine and cosine, ±1/√2). At 3π/4 and 7π/4 the sine and cosine have opposite signs.

questions.s: In triangle ABC right-angled at C, the in-radius r equals
questions.e: The tangents from C to the incircle have length r because the angle at C is 90°, so a = r + x, b = r + y and c = x + y. Adding, a + b − c = 2r. c/2 is the circum-radius, and (a + b + c)/2 is s.

questions.s: A triangle ABC has area 15 cm², a = 6 cm and b = 10 cm. The value of sin C is
questions.e: Area = ½ab sin C gives 15 = ½ × 6 × 10 × sin C = 30 sin C, so sin C = ½. Forgetting the ½ in the area formula gives sin C = 1/4.

questions.s: The in-radius of a triangle with sides 7, 8 and 9 is
questions.e: s = 12 and Δ = √(12 × 5 × 4 × 3) = √720 = 12√5, so r = Δ/s = √5. Dividing by the full perimeter 24 gives √5/2, and 21√5/10 is the circum-radius abc/(4Δ) = 504/(48√5).

questions.s: In triangle ABC, a = 3, c = 8 and B = 60°. The side b equals
questions.e: b² = a² + c² − 2ac cos B = 9 + 64 − 2 × 3 × 8 × ½ = 73 − 24 = 49, so b = 7. Adding 24 instead of subtracting gives √97, and 11 = 3 + 8 ignores the angle.

questions.s: In triangle ABC, a = 10, sin A = 1/2 and sin B = 3/5. The side b equals
questions.e: By the sine rule b = a sin B/sin A = 10 × (3/5) ÷ (1/2) = 12. Inverting the ratio of sines gives 10 × (1/2)/(3/5) = 25/3.

questions.s: The radian measure of 150° is
questions.e: Multiply degrees by π/180: 150 × π/180 = 5π/6. The value 3π/4 corresponds to 135°, and 7π/6 is 210°, so neither equals 150°.

questions.s: An angle of 7π/12 radians, expressed in degrees, is
questions.e: Multiply by 180/π: (7π/12)(180/π) = 7 × 15° = 105°. The value 75° comes from 5π/12, a common slip when reading the numerator.

questions.s: One radian is approximately equal to
questions.e: 1 rad = 180°/π ≈ 180/3.1416 ≈ 57.3°. The value 0.0175 is one degree written in radians (π/180), the reverse conversion.

questions.s: An angle of 2.5 radians in standard position has its terminal side in the
questions.e: π/2 ≈ 1.57 and π ≈ 3.14, so 1.57 < 2.5 < 3.14 and the angle lies in the second quadrant. Treating 2.5 as degrees would wrongly give the first quadrant.

questions.s: The angle, in radians, through which the minute hand of a clock turns in 20 minutes is
questions.e: The minute hand turns 2π in 60 minutes, so in 20 minutes it turns (20/60)(2π) = 2π/3. The value π/3 forgets that a full turn is 2π, not π.

questions.s: The angles of a triangle are in the ratio 2 : 3 : 7. The largest angle, in radians, is
questions.e: The angles add up to π, so the largest is (7/12)π = 7π/12, which is 105°. The value 5π/12 is the sum of the two smaller parts, not the largest angle.

questions.s: The angle 22.5° in radians is
questions.e: 22.5 × π/180 = π/8, since 180/22.5 = 8. The value π/16 halves the angle a second time and equals 11.25°.

questions.s: The angle 40° 30′ expressed in radians is
questions.e: 30′ = 0.5°, so the angle is 40.5° = 40.5π/180 = 81π/360 = 9π/40. The other options are 33.75°, 42° and 44°; 7π/30 is what you get by reading 40° 30′ as 42°.

questions.s: Which of the following angles is coterminal with π/3?
questions.e: Coterminal angles differ by a multiple of 2π: π/3 + 2π = 7π/3. The angle 4π/3 differs from π/3 by π, which puts it in the opposite quadrant.

questions.s: Each interior angle of a regular hexagon, in radians, is
questions.e: Sum of interior angles = (6 − 2)π = 4π, so each angle is 4π/6 = 2π/3 (120°). The value 3π/5 (108°) is the interior angle of a regular pentagon.

questions.s: The angle between the hour hand and the minute hand of a clock at 4:20, in radians, is
questions.e: Minute hand: 20 × 6° = 120°. Hour hand: 4 × 30° + 20 × 0.5° = 130°. The angle between them is 10° = π/18. Answering 0 ignores that the hour hand moves on from the 4 during the 20 minutes.

questions.s: The sum of two angles is π/2 radians and their difference is 30°. The larger angle, in radians, is
questions.e: In degrees the angles add to 90° and differ by 30°, so the larger is (90° + 30°)/2 = 60° = π/3. The value 5π/12 (75°) comes from adding 30° to half of 90° instead of half of 30°.

questions.s: The radian measure of −225° is
questions.e: −225 × π/180 = −5π/4, since 225/45 = 5 and 180/45 = 4. The value −3π/4 is −135°, the reference-angle slip of using 225° − 90°.

questions.s: A wheel makes 360 revolutions per minute. The angle, in radians, through which it turns in one second is
questions.e: 360 rev/min = 6 rev/s, and each revolution is 2π rad, so it turns 6 × 2π = 12π rad per second. The value 6π counts each revolution as π instead of 2π.

questions.s: The angles of a quadrilateral are in arithmetic progression with common difference 10°. The smallest angle, in radians, is
questions.e: a + (a + 10) + (a + 20) + (a + 30) = 360 gives 4a = 300, a = 75° = 5π/12. The value 7π/12 (105°) is the largest angle, not the smallest.

questions.s: An angle of π/9 radians is equal to
questions.e: (π/9)(180/π) = 180/9 = 20°. The value 9° comes from dropping π and reading the denominator as the angle.

questions.s: Which of the following angles is the largest? (Take 1 rad ≈ 57.3°.)
questions.e: 1.6 rad ≈ 91.7°, 5π/9 rad = 100° and 1.8 rad ≈ 103.1°, so 1.8 rad is the largest. 5π/9 looks largest because of the π, but it is only 100°.

questions.s: The terminal side of the angle −17π/6 lies in the
questions.e: Add 4π: −17π/6 + 24π/6 = 7π/6, which lies between π and 3π/2, so the terminal side is in the third quadrant. Dropping the minus sign and reducing 17π/6 to 5π/6 wrongly gives the second quadrant.

questions.s: The length of an arc of a circle of radius 6 cm that subtends an angle of π/3 at the centre is
questions.e: l = rθ = 6 × π/3 = 2π cm. The value 3π cm uses θ = π/2 by mistake; 6π cm forgets to multiply by the angle.

questions.s: An arc of length 15 cm in a circle of radius 5 cm subtends at the centre an angle of
questions.e: θ = l/r = 15/5 = 3 rad. The value 1/3 rad inverts the ratio as r/l, and 75 rad multiplies instead of dividing.

questions.s: The area of a sector of a circle of radius 4 cm with central angle π/4 is
questions.e: A = ½r²θ = ½ × 16 × π/4 = 2π cm². The value 4π cm² leaves out the factor ½ in the formula.

questions.s: In a circle, an arc of length 22 cm subtends an angle of 60° at the centre. Taking π = 22/7, the radius of the circle is
questions.e: 60° = π/3, so r = l/θ = 22 ÷ (22/21) = 21 cm. The value 42 cm is the diameter, and 7 cm comes from using θ = π instead of π/3.

questions.s: A sector of a circle of radius 10 cm has a central angle of 1.2 radians. The perimeter of the sector is
questions.e: Arc = rθ = 10 × 1.2 = 12 cm; perimeter = 2r + arc = 20 + 12 = 32 cm. The value 22 cm adds only one radius, and 12 cm is the arc alone.

questions.s: A sector of a circle of radius 4 cm has an area of 24 cm². Its central angle is
questions.e: A = ½r²θ gives θ = 2A/r² = 48/16 = 3 rad. The value 1.5 rad comes from θ = A/r², forgetting the factor ½ in the area formula.

questions.s: Bilal's pendulum is 50 cm long and swings through an angle of 18°. The length of the arc described by its tip is
questions.e: 18° = π/10, so l = rθ = 50 × π/10 = 5π cm. The value 900 cm treats 18 as radians, and 10π cm uses θ = π/5 (36°), the full swing counted twice.

questions.s: A sector of a circle has a perimeter of 20 cm. The greatest possible area of the sector is
questions.e: With radius r the arc is 20 − 2r, so A = ½r(20 − 2r) = 10r − r². This is greatest at r = 5, giving A = 50 − 25 = 25 cm² (and θ = 2 rad). The value 50 cm² is 10r at r = 5, forgetting to subtract r².

questions.s: A sector has an arc of length 4π cm and an area of 12π cm². The radius of the circle is
questions.e: Area = ½ × r × arc, so 12π = ½ × r × 4π, giving r = 6 cm. The value 3 cm divides area by arc without the factor 2.

questions.s: If the central angle of a sector is doubled and its radius is halved, the area of the sector
questions.e: A = ½r²θ, so the new area is ½(r/2)²(2θ) = ½ × ½r²θ, half the original. Saying it stays the same treats area like arc length rθ, where the two changes do cancel.

questions.s: A car moves along a circular track of radius 200 m and covers a distance of 100π m. The angle it turns through at the centre is
questions.e: θ = l/r = 100π/200 = π/2 rad = 90°. The value 180° comes from using the diameter-like ratio 200π/200.

questions.s: Arcs of equal length in two circles subtend angles of 60° and 75° at their centres. The ratio of the radii of the circles is
questions.e: Equal arcs give r₁θ₁ = r₂θ₂, so r₁ : r₂ = θ₂ : θ₁ = 75 : 60 = 5 : 4. The ratio 4 : 5 assumes the radius grows with the angle, but a larger angle needs a smaller radius for the same arc.

questions.s: A chord of a circle of radius 6 cm subtends an angle of π/3 at the centre. The area of the minor segment cut off by the chord is
questions.e: Segment = sector − triangle = ½r²θ − ½r² sin θ = ½ × 36 × (π/3) − ½ × 36 × (√3/2) = 6π − 9√3 cm². The option 6π − 18√3 forgets the ½ in the triangle area and is even negative.

questions.s: A sector of a circle of radius 8 cm has an arc of length 5 cm. The area of the sector is
questions.e: Area = ½ × r × l = ½ × 8 × 5 = 20 cm². The value 40 cm² is r × l without the factor ½.

questions.s: Two towns lie on the same meridian and their latitudes differ by 6°. Taking the radius of the Earth as 6400 km, the distance between them along the meridian is
questions.e: 6° = π/30 rad, so the arc is 6400 × π/30 = 640π/3 km. The value 1280π/3 km uses the diameter 12800 km instead of the radius.

questions.s: A chord of length 6√2 cm is drawn in a circle of radius 6 cm. The length of the minor arc it cuts off is
questions.e: A chord is 2r sin(θ/2), so 6√2 = 12 sin(θ/2), sin(θ/2) = 1/√2 and θ = π/2. The arc is 6 × π/2 = 3π cm. Taking θ/2 = π/4 as the whole central angle gives only 1.5π cm, and 4π cm would need θ = 2π/3.

questions.s: A sector with central angle 30° has an area of 3π cm². The radius of the circle is
questions.e: 30° = π/6, so ½r²(π/6) = 3π gives r² = 36 and r = 6 cm. The value 3√2 cm drops the ½ (giving r² = 18), and 36 cm is r² rather than r.

questions.s: A wheel of radius 35 cm turns through an angle of 2 radians. The distance moved by a point on its rim is
questions.e: Distance = rθ = 35 × 2 = 70 cm. The value 140 cm uses the diameter 70 cm as the radius.

questions.s: An arc whose length equals the diameter of its circle subtends at the centre an angle of
questions.e: θ = l/r = 2r/r = 2 rad. An arc equal to the radius subtends 1 rad, and π rad is the angle for half the circumference, not the diameter.

questions.s: A sector of radius 12 cm and central angle 120° is cut from a sheet and folded so that its two straight edges meet, forming a cone. The radius of the base of the cone is
questions.e: The arc becomes the base circumference: 12 × 2π/3 = 8π = 2πR, so R = 4 cm. The value 8 cm equates the arc to πR instead of 2πR.

questions.s: The value of sin 150° is
questions.e: sin 150° = sin(180° − 30°) = sin 30° = 1/2, positive because 150° is in the second quadrant. The value √3/2 is sin 60°, from using the wrong reference angle.

questions.s: The value of cos 240° is
questions.e: cos 240° = cos(180° + 60°) = −cos 60° = −1/2, negative in the third quadrant. The value 1/2 forgets that cosine is negative there.

questions.s: The value of tan 315° is
questions.e: tan 315° = tan(360° − 45°) = −tan 45° = −1, since tangent is negative in the fourth quadrant. The value 1 drops the sign.

questions.s: The value of sin(−1170°) is
questions.e: Add 4 × 360° = 1440°: −1170° + 1440° = 270°, and sin 270° = −1. Using sin(−x) = −sin x and 1170° = 3 × 360° + 90° also gives −sin 90° = −1; the value 1 forgets the minus sign of the odd function.

questions.s: The value of cos(19π/6) is
questions.e: 19π/6 = 2π + 7π/6, and cos(7π/6) = cos(π + π/6) = −cos(π/6) = −√3/2. The value −1/2 uses sin(π/6) instead of cos(π/6).

questions.s: For every angle θ, sin(π + θ) equals
questions.e: π + θ (for acute θ) lies in the third quadrant where sine is negative, and π is a multiple of π, so the function stays sine: sin(π + θ) = −sin θ. Changing to cosine applies only to π/2 or 3π/2 offsets.

questions.s: For every angle θ, cos(3π/2 − θ) equals
questions.e: cos(3π/2 − θ) = cos(3π/2)cos θ + sin(3π/2)sin θ = 0 − sin θ = −sin θ. With 3π/2 the function changes to sine, and for acute θ the angle is in the third quadrant where cosine is negative; answering sin θ misses this sign.

questions.s: For every angle θ for which both sides are defined, tan(π/2 + θ) equals
questions.e: tan(π/2 + θ) = sin(π/2 + θ)/cos(π/2 + θ) = cos θ/(−sin θ) = −cot θ. The answer cot θ forgets that π/2 + θ lies in the second quadrant, where tangent is negative.

questions.s: The value of sec(−480°) is
questions.e: sec is even, so sec(−480°) = sec 480° = sec 120° = 1/cos 120° = 1/(−1/2) = −2. The value 2 forgets that cos 120° is negative.

questions.s: The value of sin 780° sin 480° + cos 120° sin 150° is
questions.e: sin 780° = sin 60° = √3/2 and sin 480° = sin 120° = √3/2, so the first product is 3/4. cos 120° sin 150° = (−1/2)(1/2) = −1/4. Total 3/4 − 1/4 = 1/2. Taking cos 120° as +1/2 gives 1.

questions.s: The value of cot(−855°) is
questions.e: −855° + 3 × 360° = 225°, and cot 225° = cot(180° + 45°) = cot 45° = 1. Writing cot(−855°) = −cot 855° = −cot 135° = −(−1) = 1 agrees; the value −1 drops one of the two sign changes.

questions.s: If sin θ = 3/5 and θ lies in the second quadrant, then tan(π − θ) equals
questions.e: In the second quadrant cos θ = −4/5, so tan θ = −3/4. Then tan(π − θ) = −tan θ = 3/4. The value −3/4 is tan θ itself, forgetting the sign change from π − θ.

questions.s: The value of cos 1° + cos 2° + cos 3° + … + cos 179° is
questions.e: Pair cos k° with cos(180° − k)° = −cos k°: each pair sums to 0, and the middle term cos 90° = 0. So the total is 0. The value 1 assumes the terms are all positive, but cosine is negative from 91° to 179°.

questions.s: The value of sin²5° + sin²10° + sin²15° + … + sin²85° is
questions.e: There are 17 terms. Since sin(90° − k) = cos k, the pairs (5°, 85°), (10°, 80°), …, (40°, 50°) each give sin² + cos² = 1, making 8, and the middle term sin²45° = 1/2. Total 17/2. The value 8 forgets the unpaired middle term.

questions.s: The value of tan 1° tan 2° tan 3° … tan 89° is
questions.e: tan(90° − k) = cot k, so tan k° × tan(90° − k)° = 1 for each pair, and the middle factor tan 45° = 1. The product is 1. The value 0 would need a factor tan 0°, which is not in the product.

questions.s: In which quadrant are sin θ and tan θ both negative?
questions.e: Sine is negative in the third and fourth quadrants; tangent is negative in the second and fourth. Both are negative only in the fourth quadrant. In the third quadrant tangent is positive.

questions.s: In any triangle ABC, sin(A + B) equals
questions.e: A + B = π − C, and sin(π − C) = sin C. The answer −sin C confuses this with cos(π − C) = −cos C.

questions.s: In any triangle ABC, cos((A + B)/2) equals
questions.e: (A + B)/2 = π/2 − C/2, and cos(π/2 − x) = sin x, so cos((A + B)/2) = sin(C/2). The answer cos(C/2) forgets that the offset π/2 changes cosine to sine.

questions.s: The value of sin(7π/4) cos(5π/4) is
questions.e: sin(7π/4) = −sin(π/4) = −1/√2 (fourth quadrant) and cos(5π/4) = −cos(π/4) = −1/√2 (third quadrant). The product is +1/2. The value −1/2 misses that both factors are negative.

questions.s: If cos θ = −12/13 and π < θ < 3π/2, then sin(3π/2 + θ) equals
questions.e: sin(3π/2 + θ) = sin(3π/2)cos θ + cos(3π/2)sin θ = −cos θ = 12/13. The value −5/13 is sin θ, which comes from not switching to cosine for the 3π/2 offset.

questions.s: The value of tan(−5π/3) is
questions.e: Adding 2π: −5π/3 + 2π = π/3, so tan(−5π/3) = tan(π/3) = √3. The value −√3 applies the odd-function sign but forgets that tan(5π/3) is itself negative.

questions.s: The value of cosec 300° is
questions.e: sin 300° = −sin 60° = −√3/2, so cosec 300° = −2/√3. The value −2 uses sin 30° instead of sin 60° as the reference value.

questions.s: The expression (1 − cos²θ)(1 + cot²θ), where sin θ ≠ 0, simplifies to
questions.e: 1 − cos²θ = sin²θ and 1 + cot²θ = cosec²θ, so the product is sin²θ × cosec²θ = 1. Answering sin²θ simplifies only the first bracket.

questions.s: Which of the following is an identity, true wherever both sides are defined?
questions.e: Dividing sin²θ + cos²θ = 1 by cos²θ gives tan²θ + 1 = sec²θ. Dividing by sin²θ instead gives 1 + cot²θ = cosec²θ, not sec²θ, so the first option pairs the wrong functions.

questions.s: If tan θ = 4/3 and θ lies in the third quadrant, then sin θ equals
questions.e: With tan θ = 4/3 the reference triangle has sides 3, 4, 5, so |sin θ| = 4/5; sine is negative in the third quadrant, giving −4/5. The value −3/5 is cos θ.

questions.s: If sec θ = −5/4 and sin θ > 0, then cot θ equals
questions.e: cos θ = −4/5 and sin θ > 0 places θ in the second quadrant, so sin θ = 3/5 and cot θ = cos θ/sin θ = −4/3. The value −3/4 is tan θ.

questions.s: The expression sin⁴θ − cos⁴θ is equal to
questions.e: sin⁴θ − cos⁴θ = (sin²θ − cos²θ)(sin²θ + cos²θ) = sin²θ − cos²θ = (1 − cos²θ) − cos²θ = 1 − 2cos²θ. The value 1 − 2sin²θ is cos²θ − sin²θ, the same expression with the sign reversed.

questions.s: If sin θ + cos θ = 7/5, then sin θ cos θ equals
questions.e: Squaring: 1 + 2 sin θ cos θ = 49/25, so 2 sin θ cos θ = 24/25 and sin θ cos θ = 12/25. The value 24/25 is 2 sin θ cos θ, forgetting to halve.

questions.s: If sin θ + cos θ = √2, then tan θ + cot θ equals
questions.e: Squaring gives 1 + 2 sin θ cos θ = 2, so sin θ cos θ = 1/2. Then tan θ + cot θ = (sin²θ + cos²θ)/(sin θ cos θ) = 1/(1/2) = 2. The value 1 comes from guessing θ = 45° and adding only tan θ.

questions.s: If sec θ + tan θ = 3, then sin θ equals
questions.e: Since sec²θ − tan²θ = 1, sec θ − tan θ = 1/3. Adding and subtracting: sec θ = 5/3 and tan θ = 4/3, so sin θ = tan θ/sec θ = 4/5. The value 4/3 is tan θ, not sin θ.

questions.s: If cosec θ − cot θ = 1/2, then cosec θ + cot θ equals
questions.e: cosec²θ − cot²θ = 1 factorises as (cosec θ − cot θ)(cosec θ + cot θ) = 1, so cosec θ + cot θ = 1 ÷ (1/2) = 2. The value 1/2 assumes the sum equals the difference.

questions.s: For 0 < θ < π/2, the expression √((1 − sin θ)/(1 + sin θ)) equals
questions.e: Multiply inside by (1 − sin θ)/(1 − sin θ): √((1 − sin θ)²/cos²θ) = (1 − sin θ)/cos θ = sec θ − tan θ, which is positive here. tan θ − sec θ is its negative and cannot be a square root.

questions.s: The expression sin θ cot θ sec θ, where it is defined, simplifies to
questions.e: sin θ × (cos θ/sin θ) × (1/cos θ) = 1. Stopping after sin θ cot θ = cos θ and forgetting the factor sec θ gives cos θ.

questions.s: The expression (1 + tan²θ)/(1 + cot²θ), where defined, equals
questions.e: (1 + tan²θ)/(1 + cot²θ) = sec²θ/cosec²θ = sin²θ/cos²θ = tan²θ. The value cot²θ inverts the ratio sec²θ/cosec²θ.

questions.s: The value of cos²θ(1 + tan²θ) + sin²θ(1 + cot²θ), where defined, is
questions.e: cos²θ × sec²θ = 1 and sin²θ × cosec²θ = 1, so the sum is 2. The value 1 treats the two brackets as if they shared the identity sin²θ + cos²θ = 1.

questions.s: The least value of 3 sin²θ + 5 cos²θ is
questions.e: 3 sin²θ + 5 cos²θ = 3(sin²θ + cos²θ) + 2cos²θ = 3 + 2cos²θ, which is least (3) when cos θ = 0. The value 5 is the greatest value, at cos²θ = 1.

questions.s: If cos θ = 1/3 and θ is acute, then tan θ equals
If tan θ = a/b, where a, b > 0, then (a sin θ − b cos θ)/(a sin θ + b cos θ) equals
questions.e: Divide top and bottom by cos θ: (a tan θ − b)/(a tan θ + b) = (a²/b − b)/(a²/b + b) = (a² − b²)/(a² + b²). The option (a − b)/(a + b) replaces sin θ and cos θ by a and b without dividing through.

questions.s: The expression sec⁴θ − sec²θ, where defined, is equal to
questions.e: sec⁴θ − sec²θ = sec²θ(sec²θ − 1) = (1 + tan²θ)tan²θ = tan²θ + tan⁴θ. The option tan⁴θ − tan²θ comes from writing sec²θ = tan²θ − 1, a sign error.

questions.s: The expression sin²θ/(1 + cos θ) + cos θ, where defined, simplifies to
questions.e: sin²θ = (1 − cos θ)(1 + cos θ), so the fraction is 1 − cos θ and the sum is 1 − cos θ + cos θ = 1. Writing sin²θ/(1 + cos θ) as cos θ by a wrong cancellation leads to 2 cos θ.

questions.s: If x = a cos θ and y = b sin θ, then x²/a² + y²/b² equals
questions.e: x²/a² = cos²θ and y²/b² = sin²θ, so the sum is cos²θ + sin²θ = 1. The value a² + b² is x² + y² evaluated wrongly with θ removed.

questions.s: If x = sec θ + tan θ, then x + 1/x equals
questions.e: Since (sec θ + tan θ)(sec θ − tan θ) = sec²θ − tan²θ = 1, 1/x = sec θ − tan θ. Then x + 1/x = 2 sec θ. The value 2 tan θ is x − 1/x.

questions.s: The expression (sin θ + cosec θ)² + (cos θ + sec θ)², where defined, equals
questions.e: Expanding gives sin²θ + cos²θ + 2 + 2 + cosec²θ + sec²θ = 5 + (1 + cot²θ) + (1 + tan²θ) = 7 + tan²θ + cot²θ. The option 5 + tan²θ + cot²θ forgets the 1s from cosec²θ = 1 + cot²θ and sec²θ = 1 + tan²θ.

questions.s: If cot θ = 5/12 and θ lies in the third quadrant, then cosec θ equals
questions.e: cosec²θ = 1 + cot²θ = 1 + 25/144 = 169/144, so |cosec θ| = 13/12; sine and hence cosecant are negative in the third quadrant, giving −13/12. The value −13/5 is sec θ.

questions.s: The exact value of sin 75° is
The exact value of tan 15° is
The value of cos 70° cos 10° + sin 70° sin 10° is
questions.e: cos A cos B + sin A sin B = cos(A − B) = cos 60° = 1/2. Using cos(A + B) instead gives cos 80°, which is not a standard value, and √3/2 is sin 60°.

questions.s: The value of (tan 70° − tan 25°)/(1 + tan 70° tan 25°) is
questions.e: (tan A − tan B)/(1 + tan A tan B) = tan(A − B) = tan 45° = 1. Reading it as tan(A + B) = tan 95° gives a negative value, not √3.

questions.s: If sin A = 3/5 and cos B = 5/13, where A and B are acute, then sin(A + B) equals
questions.e: cos A = 4/5 and sin B = 12/13. sin(A + B) = (3/5)(5/13) + (4/5)(12/13) = 15/65 + 48/65 = 63/65. The value 33/65 is |sin(A − B)|, from a minus sign in the formula.

questions.s: If tan A = 1/2 and tan B = 1/3, where A and B are acute, then A + B equals
questions.e: tan(A + B) = (1/2 + 1/3)/(1 − 1/6) = (5/6)/(5/6) = 1, and since 0 < A + B < π the angle is π/4. Adding the tangents directly gives 5/6, which is not tan of a standard angle.

questions.s: For tan θ ≠ 1, tan(π/4 + θ) equals
questions.e: tan(π/4 + θ) = (tan π/4 + tan θ)/(1 − tan π/4 tan θ) = (1 + tan θ)/(1 − tan θ). The option (1 − tan θ)/(1 + tan θ) is tan(π/4 − θ).

questions.s: The product sin(A + B) sin(A − B) is equal to
questions.e: (sin A cos B)² − (cos A sin B)² = sin²A(1 − sin²B) − (1 − sin²A)sin²B = sin²A − sin²B. The option cos²A − sin²B is cos(A + B)cos(A − B), the companion product.

questions.s: If A + B = 45°, then (1 + tan A)(1 + tan B) equals
questions.e: tan(A + B) = 1 gives tan A + tan B = 1 − tan A tan B, so tan A + tan B + tan A tan B = 1. Then (1 + tan A)(1 + tan B) = 1 + 1 = 2. The value 1 forgets the leading 1 in the expanded product.

questions.s: The value of sin 105° + cos 105° is
questions.e: sin x + cos x = √2 sin(x + 45°), so the value is √2 sin 150° = √2 × 1/2 = 1/√2. The value √2 is the greatest possible value of sin x + cos x, not its value at 105°.

questions.s: The greatest value of 3 sin θ + 4 cos θ is
questions.e: a sin θ + b cos θ = √(a² + b²) sin(θ + α), so its greatest value is √(9 + 16) = 5. The value 7 adds the greatest values of each term, but sin θ and cos θ cannot both equal 1 at the same θ.

questions.s: The expression √3 cos θ + sin θ is identically equal to
questions.e: 2 cos(θ − π/6) = 2(cos θ cos π/6 + sin θ sin π/6) = √3 cos θ + sin θ. The option 2 sin(θ + π/6) expands to √3 sin θ + cos θ, with the coefficients swapped.

questions.s: The value of tan 75° − tan 15° is
questions.e: tan 75° = 2 + √3 and tan 15° = 2 − √3, so the difference is 2√3. The value 4 is tan 75° + tan 15°.

questions.s: If tan(A + B) = 3 and tan A = 2, then tan B equals
questions.e: (2 + t)/(1 − 2t) = 3 gives 2 + t = 3 − 6t, so 7t = 1 and t = 1/7. Subtracting tangents directly, 3 − 2 = 1, ignores the denominator of the addition formula.

questions.s: The value of cos(45° + θ) − sin(45° − θ) is
questions.e: cos(45° + θ) = (cos θ − sin θ)/√2 and sin(45° − θ) = (cos θ − sin θ)/√2, so the difference is 0. Equivalently 45° + θ and 45° − θ are complementary. A sign slip in one expansion gives −√2 sin θ.

questions.s: In a triangle ABC, tan A = 1 and tan B = 2. Then tan C equals
questions.e: tan(A + B) = (1 + 2)/(1 − 2) = −3, and C = π − (A + B), so tan C = −tan(A + B) = 3. The value −3 is tan(A + B) itself.

questions.s: Where defined, sin(x + y)/(cos x cos y) is equal to
questions.e: (sin x cos y + cos x sin y)/(cos x cos y) = sin x/cos x + sin y/cos y = tan x + tan y. The option cot x + cot y is what you get by dividing by sin x sin y instead.

questions.s: The exact value of cos 105° is
questions.e: cos(60° + 45°) = (1/2)(1/√2) − (√3/2)(1/√2) = (1 − √3)/(2√2) = (√2 − √6)/4, negative as 105° is in the second quadrant. The value (√6 − √2)/4 is cos 75°, the positive version.

questions.s: If sin α = 4/5 with α acute, and cos β = −12/13 with β in the second quadrant, then cos(α − β) equals
questions.e: cos α = 3/5 and sin β = 5/13. cos(α − β) = cos α cos β + sin α sin β = (3/5)(−12/13) + (4/5)(5/13) = −36/65 + 20/65 = −16/65. The value −56/65 is cos(α + β), from using the minus sign of the sum formula.

questions.s: For all angles A and B, cos(A − B) equals
o: cos A cos B − sin A sin B
sin A cos B − cos A sin B
sin A cos B + cos A sin B
cos A cos B + sin A sin B
questions.e: The difference formula for cosine has a plus sign: cos(A − B) = cos A cos B + sin A sin B. With a minus sign it becomes cos(A + B); the last two options are sin(A − B) and sin(A + B).

questions.s: The value of 2 sin 15° cos 15° is
questions.e: 2 sin θ cos θ = sin 2θ, so the value is sin 30° = 1/2. The value 1/4 forgets the factor 2 and treats it as sin 15° cos 15°.

questions.s: The value of cos²22.5° − sin²22.5° is
questions.e: cos²θ − sin²θ = cos 2θ = cos 45° = 1/√2. The value 1 uses cos²θ + sin²θ instead of the difference.

questions.s: Where defined, 2 tan θ/(1 + tan²θ) is equal to
questions.e: 2 tan θ/sec²θ = 2 (sin θ/cos θ) cos²θ = 2 sin θ cos θ = sin 2θ. The expression 2 tan θ/(1 − tan²θ), with a minus sign, is tan 2θ.

questions.s: If tan θ = 1/2, then tan 2θ equals
questions.e: tan 2θ = 2 tan θ/(1 − tan²θ) = 1/(1 − 1/4) = 4/3. Doubling tan θ to get 1 ignores the denominator; using 1 + tan²θ gives 4/5, which is sin 2θ.

questions.s: If sin θ = 3/5 and θ is acute, then cos 2θ equals
questions.e: cos 2θ = 1 − 2 sin²θ = 1 − 18/25 = 7/25. The value 24/25 is sin 2θ, and 16/25 is cos²θ.

questions.s: If cos θ = −4/5 and θ lies in the third quadrant, then sin 2θ equals
questions.e: In the third quadrant sin θ = −3/5, so sin 2θ = 2(−3/5)(−4/5) = 24/25. The value −24/25 takes sin θ as positive.

questions.s: Where defined, (1 − cos 2θ)/sin 2θ is equal to
questions.e: 1 − cos 2θ = 2 sin²θ and sin 2θ = 2 sin θ cos θ, so the ratio is sin θ/cos θ = tan θ. The value cot θ comes from using 1 − cos 2θ = 2cos²θ by mistake.

questions.s: For every θ, cos 3θ is equal to
questions.e: cos 3θ = cos(2θ + θ) = (2cos²θ − 1)cos θ − 2 sin²θ cos θ = 4cos³θ − 3cos θ. The pattern 3x − 4x³ belongs to sin 3θ, not cos 3θ.

questions.s: If sin θ = 1/3, then sin 3θ equals
questions.e: sin 3θ = 3 sin θ − 4 sin³θ = 1 − 4/27 = 23/27. The value 1 is 3 sin θ alone, ignoring the cubic term.

questions.s: The exact value of sin 22.5° is
questions.e: sin²22.5° = (1 − cos 45°)/2 = (1 − 1/√2)/2 = (2 − √2)/4, and taking the positive root gives √(2 − √2)/2. The value √(2 + √2)/2 is cos 22.5°.

questions.s: The exact value of tan 22.5° is
questions.e: tan(θ/2) = (1 − cos θ)/sin θ with θ = 45°: (1 − 1/√2)/(1/√2) = √2 − 1. The value √2 + 1 is tan 67.5°, and 2 − √3 is tan 15°.

questions.s: If cos θ = 1/8 and θ is acute, then cos(θ/2) equals
questions.e: cos²(θ/2) = (1 + cos θ)/2 = (9/8)/2 = 9/16, and θ/2 is acute, so cos(θ/2) = 3/4. The value √7/4 is sin(θ/2), from using 1 − cos θ.

questions.s: If cos θ = −7/25 and π < θ < 3π/2, then tan(θ/2) equals
questions.e: tan²(θ/2) = (1 − cos θ)/(1 + cos θ) = (32/25)/(18/25) = 16/9. Since π/2 < θ/2 < 3π/4, θ/2 is in the second quadrant where tangent is negative, so tan(θ/2) = −4/3. The value 4/3 misses the quadrant of θ/2.

questions.s: For every θ, cos⁴θ − sin⁴θ equals
questions.e: cos⁴θ − sin⁴θ = (cos²θ − sin²θ)(cos²θ + sin²θ) = cos²θ − sin²θ = cos 2θ. The value 1 comes from factorising and keeping only the bracket cos²θ + sin²θ.

questions.s: The value of cos 20° cos 40° cos 80° is
questions.e: Multiply by 8 sin 20°: 8 sin 20° cos 20° cos 40° cos 80° = 4 sin 40° cos 40° cos 80° = 2 sin 80° cos 80° = sin 160° = sin 20°. So the product is sin 20°/(8 sin 20°) = 1/8. The value 1/16 uses one doubling too many.

questions.s: The exact value of sin 18° is
questions.e: With θ = 18°, 2θ = 90° − 3θ, so sin 2θ = cos 3θ; dividing by cos θ gives 4 sin²θ + 2 sin θ − 1 = 0 and the positive root is sin 18° = (√5 − 1)/4. The value (√5 + 1)/4 is cos 36°.

questions.s: If tan(θ/2) = t, then cos θ equals
questions.e: cos θ = (cos²(θ/2) − sin²(θ/2))/(cos²(θ/2) + sin²(θ/2)); dividing by cos²(θ/2) gives (1 − t²)/(1 + t²). The expression 2t/(1 + t²) is sin θ and 2t/(1 − t²) is tan θ.

questions.s: The value of 1 − 2 sin²75° is
questions.e: 1 − 2 sin²θ = cos 2θ = cos 150° = −√3/2. The value √3/2 forgets that 150° lies in the second quadrant where cosine is negative.

questions.s: For every θ, (cos θ − sin θ)² equals
questions.e: (cos θ − sin θ)² = cos²θ + sin²θ − 2 sin θ cos θ = 1 − sin 2θ. The option cos 2θ is (cos θ − sin θ)(cos θ + sin θ), not the square.

questions.s: If sin θ + cos θ = 1/2, then sin 2θ equals
questions.e: Squaring: 1 + sin 2θ = 1/4, so sin 2θ = −3/4. The value 1/4 is just (1/2)², forgetting to subtract the 1.

questions.s: The greatest value of sin θ cos θ is
questions.e: sin θ cos θ = ½ sin 2θ, whose greatest value is ½ (at θ = 45°). The value 1 assumes both sin θ and cos θ can equal 1 together.

questions.s: Where defined, cot θ − tan θ equals
questions.e: cot θ − tan θ = (cos²θ − sin²θ)/(sin θ cos θ) = cos 2θ/(½ sin 2θ) = 2 cot 2θ. The value 2 cosec 2θ is cot θ + tan θ.

questions.s: The value of sin 75° + sin 15° is
questions.e: sin A + sin B = 2 sin((A + B)/2) cos((A − B)/2) = 2 sin 45° cos 30° = 2 (√2/2)(√3/2) = √6/2. The value √6 forgets that the factor 2 cancels with the halves.

questions.s: The value of cos 75° − cos 15° is
questions.e: cos A − cos B = −2 sin((A + B)/2) sin((A − B)/2) = −2 sin 45° sin 30° = −2 (√2/2)(1/2) = −√2/2. The value √2/2 drops the minus sign; cos 75° is smaller than cos 15°, so the difference must be negative.

questions.s: For all angles A and B, sin A + sin B equals
questions.e: sin A + sin B = 2 sin((A + B)/2) cos((A − B)/2); check with A = B: 2 sin A cos 0 = 2 sin A. The second option is sin A − sin B, the third is cos A + cos B and the fourth is cos A − cos B.

questions.s: The product 2 sin 3θ cos θ, written as a sum, is
questions.e: 2 sin A cos B = sin(A + B) + sin(A − B), so 2 sin 3θ cos θ = sin 4θ + sin 2θ. The option cos 2θ − cos 4θ equals 2 sin 3θ sin θ, the product with sine in both places.

questions.s: The product 2 cos 5θ sin 2θ, written as a sum or difference, is
questions.e: 2 cos A sin B = sin(A + B) − sin(A − B) = sin 7θ − sin 3θ. The option sin 7θ + sin 3θ is 2 sin 5θ cos 2θ, where the sine and cosine are the other way round.

questions.s: Where defined, (sin 5x + sin 3x)/(cos 5x + cos 3x) equals
questions.e: Numerator = 2 sin 4x cos x and denominator = 2 cos 4x cos x, so the ratio is tan 4x. The value tan x would come from the half-difference angle, which cancels here.

questions.s: Where defined, (cos 2x − cos 4x)/(sin 4x − sin 2x) equals
questions.e: cos 2x − cos 4x = −2 sin 3x sin(−x) = 2 sin 3x sin x, and sin 4x − sin 2x = 2 cos 3x sin x. The ratio is tan 3x. Missing the sign from sin(−x) gives −tan 3x.

questions.s: The value of sin 20° + sin 40° − sin 80° is
questions.e: sin 20° + sin 40° = 2 sin 30° cos 10° = cos 10° = sin 80°, so the expression is 0. Adding the angles to treat sin 20° + sin 40° as sin 60° is the usual slip.

questions.s: The value of 2 sin 52.5° sin 7.5° is
questions.e: 2 sin A sin B = cos(A − B) − cos(A + B) = cos 45° − cos 60° = √2/2 − 1/2 = (√2 − 1)/2. Reversing the order to cos(A + B) − cos(A − B) gives a negative value, and (√2 + 1)/2 adds the two cosines.

questions.s: The value of cos 75° cos 15° is
questions.e: 2 cos A cos B = cos(A + B) + cos(A − B) = cos 90° + cos 60° = 1/2, so cos 75° cos 15° = 1/4. The value 1/2 forgets to divide by 2.

questions.s: The value of sin 105° cos 15° is
questions.e: 2 sin A cos B = sin(A + B) + sin(A − B) = sin 120° + sin 90° = √3/2 + 1, so the product is (2 + √3)/4. The value (2 − √3)/4 uses sin(A − B) with a minus sign.

questions.s: The sum cos 7x + cos 3x, written as a product, is
questions.e: cos A + cos B = 2 cos((A + B)/2) cos((A − B)/2) = 2 cos 5x cos 2x. The option 2 cos 10x cos 4x forgets to halve the sum and difference of the angles.

questions.s: Where defined, (sin θ + sin 3θ + sin 5θ)/(cos θ + cos 3θ + cos 5θ) equals
questions.e: sin 5θ + sin θ = 2 sin 3θ cos 2θ and cos 5θ + cos θ = 2 cos 3θ cos 2θ. So the ratio is sin 3θ(1 + 2 cos 2θ)/(cos 3θ(1 + 2 cos 2θ)) = tan 3θ. Adding the angles to get tan 9θ treats sine as if it were additive.

questions.s: The value of 4 sin 15° cos 75° is
questions.e: 2 sin A cos B = sin(A + B) + sin(A − B) = sin 90° + sin(−60°) = 1 − √3/2, so 4 sin 15° cos 75° = 2 − √3. The value 1 − √3/2 is only 2 sin 15° cos 75°.

questions.s: If cos A + cos B = 1/2 and sin A + sin B = 1/4, then cos(A + B) equals
questions.e: Dividing the sum-to-product forms: 2 sin((A + B)/2) cos((A − B)/2) ÷ 2 cos((A + B)/2) cos((A − B)/2) = tan((A + B)/2) = 1/2. Then cos(A + B) = (1 − t²)/(1 + t²) = (3/4)/(5/4) = 3/5. The value 4/5 is sin(A + B) = 2t/(1 + t²).

questions.s: The difference sin 3θ − sin θ, written as a product, is
questions.e: sin A − sin B = 2 cos((A + B)/2) sin((A − B)/2) = 2 cos 2θ sin θ. The option 2 sin 2θ cos θ is sin 3θ + sin θ.

questions.s: The radian measure of 135° is
questions.e: Multiply by π/180: 135 × π/180 = 3π/4. 2π/3 is 120° and 5π/6 is 150°.

questions.s: An arc of a circle of radius 6 cm subtends an angle of π/3 radians at the centre. The length of the arc is
questions.e: Arc length s = rθ = 6 × π/3 = 2π cm. The formula needs θ in radians; 6π cm would be the length for θ = π.

questions.s: The area of a sector of a circle of radius 10 cm with central angle 72° is
questions.e: 72° = 72π/180 = 2π/5 rad, so area = ½r²θ = ½ × 100 × 2π/5 = 20π cm². Leaving out the ½ gives 40π cm²; 4π cm is the arc length.

questions.s: The minute hand of a clock is 7 cm long. The distance moved by its tip in 20 minutes is
questions.e: In 20 minutes the hand turns one-third of a revolution, 2π/3 rad, so s = rθ = 7 × 2π/3 = 14π/3 cm. Using π/3 for a third of a turn gives 7π/3 cm.

questions.s: The value of sin 210° is
questions.e: 210° = 180° + 30° lies in the third quadrant, where sine is negative, so sin 210° = −sin 30° = −½. −√3/2 would use sin 60° as the reference value.

questions.s: The value of cos(−300°) is
questions.e: Cosine is even, so cos(−300°) = cos 300° = cos(360° − 60°) = cos 60° = ½. Treating cosine as odd gives −½.

questions.s: tan(3π/2 − θ) equals
questions.e: An odd multiple of π/2 changes tan to cot, and for small θ the angle 3π/2 − θ is in the third quadrant, where tangent is positive. So tan(3π/2 − θ) = cot θ; −cot θ is the value of tan(3π/2 + θ).

questions.s: The value of sin 150° + cos 240° is
questions.e: sin 150° = sin 30° = ½ and cos 240° = −cos 60° = −½, so the sum is 0. Forgetting that cosine is negative in the third quadrant gives 1.

questions.s: For every θ where both are defined, sec²θ − tan²θ equals
questions.e: Dividing sin²θ + cos²θ = 1 by cos²θ gives tan²θ + 1 = sec²θ, so sec²θ − tan²θ = 1. −1 is tan²θ − sec²θ.

questions.s: The expression (1 − cos²θ)(1 + cot²θ) simplifies to
questions.e: 1 − cos²θ = sin²θ and 1 + cot²θ = cosec²θ, so the product is sin²θ × cosec²θ = 1. Stopping after the first factor gives sin²θ.

questions.s: If sin θ = 3/5 and θ lies in the second quadrant, then tan θ equals
questions.e: cos θ = −√(1 − 9/25) = −4/5 in the second quadrant, so tan θ = (3/5)/(−4/5) = −3/4. −4/3 is cot θ.

questions.s: If sin θ + cos θ = 7/5, then sin θ cos θ equals
questions.e: Squaring, 1 + 2 sin θ cos θ = 49/25, so 2 sin θ cos θ = 24/25 and sin θ cos θ = 12/25. 24/25 is the value of sin 2θ, before halving.

questions.s: The exact value of tan 75° is
If sin A = 3/5 and cos B = 5/13, where A and B are acute, then cos(A + B) equals
questions.e: cos A = 4/5 and sin B = 12/13, so cos(A + B) = cos A cos B − sin A sin B = 20/65 − 36/65 = −16/65. Adding the products gives cos(A − B) = 56/65.

questions.s: The value of cos²15° − sin²15° is
questions.e: cos²θ − sin²θ = cos 2θ, so the value is cos 30° = √3/2. Confusing it with cos²θ + sin²θ gives 1.

questions.s: If tan θ = 1/3, then tan 2θ equals
questions.e: tan 2θ = 2 tan θ/(1 − tan²θ) = (2/3)/(8/9) = 3/4. Just doubling 1/3 gives 2/3, and 3/5 is sin 2θ.

questions.s: If cos θ = 1/8 and θ is acute, then cos(θ/2) equals
questions.e: cos²(θ/2) = (1 + cos θ)/2 = (9/8)/2 = 9/16, so cos(θ/2) = 3/4 (positive, since θ/2 is acute). √7/4 is sin(θ/2), and 9/16 forgets the square root.

questions.s: The value of cos 20° cos 40° cos 60° cos 80° is
questions.e: cos 20° cos 40° cos 80° = 1/8 (multiply and divide by 2 sin 20° and use 2 sin θ cos θ = sin 2θ three times: the product becomes sin 160°/(8 sin 20°) = 1/8). Then cos 60° = 1/2 gives 1/8 × 1/2 = 1/16. Choosing 1/8 forgets the extra factor cos 60°.

questions.s: The value of 3 sin 10° − 4 sin³10° is
questions.e: sin 3θ = 3 sin θ − 4 sin³θ, so the expression is sin 30° = ½. √3/2 would be cos 30°, from mixing up the triple-angle formulas.

questions.s: The value of sin 75° + sin 15° is
questions.e: sin P + sin Q = 2 sin((P + Q)/2) cos((P − Q)/2) = 2 sin 45° cos 30° = 2 × (1/√2) × (√3/2) = √6/2. Leaving out the factor 2 gives √6/4.

questions.s: The expression (sin 5x + sin 3x)/(cos 5x + cos 3x) simplifies to
questions.e: The numerator is 2 sin 4x cos x and the denominator is 2 cos 4x cos x, so the ratio is tan 4x. tan 8x adds the angles instead of averaging them, and tan x uses the half-difference.

questions.s: For all angles A and B, 2 sin A cos B equals
questions.e: Adding sin(A + B) = sin A cos B + cos A sin B and sin(A − B) = sin A cos B − cos A sin B gives 2 sin A cos B. The difference sin(A + B) − sin(A − B) is 2 cos A sin B.

questions.s: The period of f(x) = cos 4x is
questions.e: The period of cos(bx) is 2π/b = 2π/4 = π/2. 8π multiplies by 4 instead of dividing.

questions.s: The least value of f(x) = 3 + 2 sin x is
questions.e: sin x ≥ −1, so 3 + 2 sin x ≥ 3 − 2 = 1, reached at x = 3π/2. 5 is the greatest value and −1 is the least value of sin x alone.

questions.s: The least value of 9 sec²x + 4 cos²x is
questions.e: Let t = cos²x, 0 < t ≤ 1, and f = 9/t + 4t. AM-GM suggests 12, but equality needs t = 3/2, which is impossible. f′ = −9/t² + 4 < 0 for t ≤ 1, so f decreases and its least value is at t = 1: 9 + 4 = 13.

questions.s: In triangle ABC, a = 6, A = 30° and B = 45°. The side b equals
questions.e: By the sine rule b = a sin B/sin A = 6 × (1/√2) ÷ ½ = 12/√2 = 6√2. Multiplying by sin A instead of dividing gives 3√2.

questions.s: The area of an equilateral triangle of side 4 cm is
questions.e: Area = ½ab sin C = ½ × 4 × 4 × sin 60° = 8 × √3/2 = 4√3 cm². Forgetting the ½ gives 8√3 cm².

questions.s: In triangle ABC, a = 4, b = 5 and c = 6. Which relation between its angles is true?
questions.e: cos A = (25 + 36 − 16)/60 = 3/4 and cos C = (16 + 25 − 36)/40 = 1/8. Then cos 2A = 2(9/16) − 1 = 1/8 = cos C, and both angles lie between 0° and 180°, so C = 2A. Since C is acute (cos C > 0), A + B = 180° − C cannot be 90°.

questions.s: In triangle ABC, A = 60° and a = 3√3 cm. The circum-radius is
questions.e: 2R = a/sin A = 3√3 ÷ (√3/2) = 6, so R = 3 cm. The value 6 cm is the diameter 2R.

questions.s: The value of tan⁻¹(1) + cos⁻¹(0) is
questions.e: tan⁻¹1 = π/4 and cos⁻¹0 = π/2, so the sum is 3π/4. Taking cos⁻¹0 = 0 (confusing it with sin⁻¹0) gives π/4.

questions.s: The value of cos(sin⁻¹(−12/13)) is
questions.e: θ = sin⁻¹(−12/13) lies in [−π/2, 0), where cosine is positive, so cos θ = +√(1 − 144/169) = 5/13. Giving cosine the sign of the sine leads to −5/13.

questions.s: If sin⁻¹x + sin⁻¹y = 2π/3, then cos⁻¹x + cos⁻¹y equals
questions.e: cos⁻¹x = π/2 − sin⁻¹x and cos⁻¹y = π/2 − sin⁻¹y, so the sum is π − 2π/3 = π/3. Assuming the two sums are equal gives 2π/3.

questions.s: The solution of cos x = −1 in 0 ≤ x < 2π is
questions.e: On the unit circle cos x = −1 only at the point (−1, 0), i.e. x = π. At x = 0 the cosine is +1, and at π/2 and 3π/2 it is 0.

questions.s: The solutions of cos 2x = sin x in 0 ≤ x < 2π are
questions.e: cos 2x = 1 − 2 sin²x gives 2 sin²x + sin x − 1 = (2 sin x − 1)(sin x + 1) = 0. sin x = ½ gives π/6, 5π/6 and sin x = −1 gives 3π/2. A sign slip, (2 sin x + 1)(sin x − 1), leads to the last option.

questions.s: The value of cos 20° + cos 100° + cos 140° is
questions.e: cos 100° + cos 20° = 2 cos 60° cos 40° = cos 40°, and cos 140° = −cos 40°, so the total is 0. Treating each term as a positive acute cosine leads to a non-zero answer.

questions.s: The domain of f(x) = √(x − 3) is
questions.e: A square root is real only when its argument is non-negative, so x − 3 ≥ 0 gives x ≥ 3. The value x = 3 is allowed because √0 = 0, so x > 3 wrongly drops the end point.

questions.s: The domain of f(x) = 1/(x² − 4) is
questions.e: The function is undefined where the denominator is zero: x² − 4 = 0 gives x = 2 or x = −2. Removing only 2 forgets the negative root of x² = 4.

questions.s: The domain of f(x) = √(9 − x²) is
questions.e: We need 9 − x² ≥ 0, i.e. x² ≤ 9, so −3 ≤ x ≤ 3. The end points are included since √0 is defined; the set (−∞, −3] ∪ [3, ∞) is the solution of x² ≥ 9, the reverse inequality.

questions.s: The domain of f(x) = 1/√(x² − 5x + 6) is
questions.e: The root must be real and non-zero, so x² − 5x + 6 = (x − 2)(x − 3) > 0, which holds for x < 2 or x > 3. The end points 2 and 3 make the denominator zero, so (−∞, 2] ∪ [3, ∞) is wrong.

questions.s: The range of f(x) = x² + 3, x ∈ ℝ, is
questions.e: Since x² ≥ 0, x² + 3 ≥ 3, and the value 3 is reached at x = 0. So the range is [3, ∞); [0, ∞) is the range of x² alone.

questions.s: The range of f(x) = 5 − 2 sin x is
questions.e: As −1 ≤ sin x ≤ 1, we get −2 ≤ −2 sin x ≤ 2, so 3 ≤ 5 − 2 sin x ≤ 7. The interval [−2, 2] is only the range of −2 sin x before adding 5.

questions.s: The range of f(x) = (2x + 1)/(x − 3), x ≠ 3, is
questions.e: Solve y = (2x + 1)/(x − 3) for x: x = (3y + 1)/(y − 2), which exists for every y except y = 2. The excluded value 3 belongs to the domain, not the range.

questions.s: If f(x) = 3x² − 2x + 1, then f(−2) is
questions.e: f(−2) = 3(4) − 2(−2) + 1 = 12 + 4 + 1 = 17. Getting 9 comes from treating −2x as −4 instead of +4.

questions.s: The domain of f(x) = ln(x² − 1) is
questions.e: A logarithm needs a positive argument: x² − 1 > 0 gives x² > 1, so x < −1 or x > 1. The answer (1, ∞) forgets the negative values, and ℝ − {−1, 1} wrongly keeps the interval (−1, 1) where x² − 1 < 0.

questions.s: The domain of f(x) = √((x − 1)/(x + 2)) is
questions.e: We need (x − 1)/(x + 2) ≥ 0 with x ≠ −2. The quotient is ≥ 0 when x ≥ 1 or x < −2. The point x = −2 must be excluded because the denominator vanishes, so (−∞, −2] is wrong.

questions.s: Which of the following sets of ordered pairs is a function?
questions.e: A function gives exactly one image to each first element. In {(1, 2), (2, 2), (3, 2)} each of 1, 2, 3 appears once; different inputs may share the same output. The other sets repeat a first element with two different images.

questions.s: The range of f(x) = |x − 2| + 1 is
questions.e: |x − 2| ≥ 0 with equality at x = 2, so f(x) ≥ 1 and the value 1 is attained. The set (1, ∞) wrongly excludes f(2) = 1.

questions.s: The range of f(x) = x² − 4x + 7 is
questions.e: Complete the square: x² − 4x + 7 = (x − 2)² + 3 ≥ 3, with minimum 3 at x = 2. The value 7 is only f(0), not the least value.

questions.s: If f(x) = (x + 1)/(x − 1), then f(3) + f(−3) equals
questions.e: f(3) = 4/2 = 2 and f(−3) = (−2)/(−4) = 1/2, so the sum is 5/2. Assuming f is odd and writing 0 is a mistake, since f(−3) ≠ −f(3).

questions.s: The range of f(x) = x/(x² + 1), x ∈ ℝ, is
questions.e: Setting y = x/(x² + 1) gives yx² − x + y = 0; real x needs 1 − 4y² ≥ 0, so −1/2 ≤ y ≤ 1/2. The end values are reached at x = 1 and x = −1, so the open interval is wrong.

questions.s: The domain of f(x) = 1/(|x| − 3) is
questions.e: The denominator is zero when |x| = 3, i.e. x = 3 or x = −3, and f is defined for every other real x. Removing only 3 forgets that |−3| = 3 as well.

questions.s: The range of f(x) = 2ˣ, x ∈ ℝ, is
questions.e: An exponential with positive base is always positive and takes every positive value, but never 0. So the range is (0, ∞); [0, ∞) wrongly includes 0.

questions.s: The domain of f(x) = √(x − 2) + √(6 − x) is
questions.e: Both roots must be real: x − 2 ≥ 0 gives x ≥ 2 and 6 − x ≥ 0 gives x ≤ 6. The intersection is [2, 6]; [2, ∞) satisfies only the first condition.

questions.s: If f(x) = x² − 3x and f(a) = 10, then the possible values of a are
questions.e: a² − 3a − 10 = 0 factorises as (a − 5)(a + 2) = 0, so a = 5 or a = −2. Check: 25 − 15 = 10 and 4 + 6 = 10. The pair −5, 2 comes from a sign slip in the factors.

questions.s: The range of f(x) = 3 cos 2x + 1 is
questions.e: −1 ≤ cos 2x ≤ 1, so −3 ≤ 3 cos 2x ≤ 3 and adding 1 gives −2 ≤ f(x) ≤ 4. The factor 2 inside cos changes the period, not the range.

questions.s: If f(x) = 2x + 1 and g(x) = x², then (f∘g)(x) is
questions.e: (f∘g)(x) = f(g(x)) = f(x²) = 2x² + 1. The option (2x + 1)² is (g∘f)(x), the composition taken in the wrong order.

questions.s: If f(x) = x − 3 and g(x) = x² + 1, then g(f(4)) is
questions.e: First f(4) = 1, then g(1) = 1 + 1 = 2. The value 14 is f(g(4)) = 17 − 3, which applies the functions in the wrong order.

questions.s: The inverse of f(x) = (x + 2)/3 is
questions.e: Write y = (x + 2)/3, so 3y = x + 2 and x = 3y − 2; hence f⁻¹(x) = 3x − 2. Check: f(3x − 2) = 3x/3 = x. The option 3/(x + 2) is the reciprocal, not the inverse.

questions.s: If f(x) = (2x − 1)/(x + 3), x ≠ −3, then f⁻¹(x) is
questions.e: From y(x + 3) = 2x − 1 we get xy − 2x = −1 − 3y, so x(y − 2) = −(3y + 1) and x = (3y + 1)/(2 − y). Hence f⁻¹(x) = (3x + 1)/(2 − x). The option (x + 3)/(2x − 1) is 1/f(x), not the inverse.

questions.s: If f(x) = x³, then f⁻¹(8) is
questions.e: f⁻¹(8) is the number whose cube is 8, which is 2. The value 512 is f(8) and 1/8 is the reciprocal, neither of which is the inverse value.

questions.s: If f(x) = x² + 1 and g(x) = √(x − 1) for x ≥ 1, then (g∘f)(x) for real x equals
questions.e: g(f(x)) = √(x² + 1 − 1) = √(x²) = |x|, because a square root is never negative. Writing x is wrong for negative x, e.g. x = −2 gives √4 = 2, not −2.

questions.s: If f(x) = 3x − 4, then f(f(x)) is
