questions.s: The slope of the line 3x − 4y + 12 = 0 is
questions.e: For ax + by + c = 0 the slope is −a/b = −3/(−4) = 3/4; equivalently y = (3/4)x + 3. Writing −3/4 forgets that b is negative, and 4/3 inverts the ratio.

questions.s: The line through (2, −3) and (4, a) is parallel to the line through (−1, 0) and (1, 6). The value of a is
questions.e: The second line has slope 6/2 = 3. Parallel lines have equal slopes, so (a + 3)/2 = 3 and a = 3. The value 9 comes from writing (a − 3)/2 by a sign slip, and −11/3 is the answer for perpendicular lines.

questions.s: The line through (k, 3) and (2, −1) is perpendicular to a line of slope 2. Then k equals
questions.e: The required slope is −1/2, so 4/(k − 2) = −1/2, giving k − 2 = −8 and k = −6. Setting the slope equal to 2 gives k = 4, which is the condition for parallel lines, not perpendicular ones.

questions.s: The orthocentre of the triangle with vertices A(0, 0), B(4, 0) and C(1, 3) is
questions.e: AB lies on the x-axis, so the altitude from C is x = 1. BC has slope 3/(1 − 4) = −1, so the altitude from A has slope 1 and is y = x. They meet at (1, 1). (5/3, 1) is the centroid and (2, 1) is the circumcentre; note H = 3G − 2O checks: (5 − 4, 3 − 2) = (1, 1).

questions.s: The equation of the line with slope −2 and y-intercept 5 is
questions.e: y = mx + c gives y = −2x + 5, that is 2x + y − 5 = 0. The equation 2x + y + 5 = 0 has the right slope but y-intercept −5, and 2x − y + 5 = 0 has slope +2.

questions.s: The equation of the line through (3, −2) with slope 4 is
questions.e: Point-slope form: y + 2 = 4(x − 3), so y = 4x − 14, i.e. 4x − y − 14 = 0. The option 4x − y − 10 = 0 comes from writing y − 2 instead of y + 2; the other two pass through (3, −2) but have slopes −4 and 1/4.

questions.s: The equation of the line through (−1, 3) and (2, −3) is
questions.e: Slope = (−3 − 3)/(2 + 1) = −2, so y − 3 = −2(x + 1), giving y = −2x + 1, i.e. 2x + y − 1 = 0. Check: (2, −3) gives 4 − 3 − 1 = 0. The line x + 2y − 5 = 0 passes through (−1, 3) only, with slope −1/2.

questions.s: The line whose x-intercept is 3 and y-intercept is −4 has the equation
questions.e: Intercept form x/a + y/b = 1 gives x/3 + y/(−4) = 1; multiplying by 12 gives 4x − 3y = 12. 3x − 4y = 12 swaps the roles of the intercepts (it cuts the axes at 4 and −3).

questions.s: The x-intercept and y-intercept of the line 5x − 2y + 20 = 0 are respectively
questions.e: Put y = 0: 5x = −20, so x = −4. Put x = 0: −2y = −20, so y = 10. Writing 5x − 2y = −20 as x/(−4) + y/10 = 1 confirms −4 and 10; the option 4 and −10 has both signs reversed.

questions.s: The perpendicular from the origin to a line has length 4 and makes an angle of 30° with the positive x-axis. The equation of the line is
questions.e: Normal form: x cos 30° + y sin 30° = 4, i.e. (√3/2)x + (1/2)y = 4, so √3x + y = 8. x + √3y = 8 uses α = 60° (cos and sin swapped), and √3x + y = 4 forgets to clear the halves on the right-hand side.

questions.s: When the line 3x − 4y + 15 = 0 is written in the normal form x cos α + y sin α = p, the value of p is
questions.e: Move the constant: −3x + 4y = 15, then divide by √(3² + 4²) = 5 to get (−3/5)x + (4/5)y = 3, so p = 3. In normal form p is the length of the perpendicular and must be positive, so −3 is wrong; 15 forgets to divide by 5.

questions.s: The equation of the line through (4, −7) parallel to the x-axis is
questions.e: A line parallel to the x-axis has constant y, and here y = −7 at the given point, so the line is y = −7. x = 4 is the line through the point parallel to the y-axis.

questions.s: The line through (2, 3) that makes equal non-zero intercepts on the coordinate axes is
questions.e: Equal intercepts a give x/a + y/a = 1, i.e. x + y = a. Substituting (2, 3) gives a = 5, so x + y = 5. 3x − 2y = 0 also passes through (2, 3) but goes through the origin, so both its intercepts are zero.

questions.s: A line through (4, 3) cuts intercepts on the axes whose sum is −1. One such line is
questions.e: Take x/a + y/b = 1 with b = −1 − a. Substituting (4, 3): 4/a − 3/(1 + a) = 1, which simplifies to a² = 4, so a = 2, b = −3 (or a = −2, b = 1). With a = 2: x/2 − y/3 = 1, i.e. 3x − 2y = 6. The other options pass through (4, 3) but their intercept sums are 0, 15 and −1/6.

questions.s: The equation of the line through (1, −2) parallel to 3x + 2y − 7 = 0 is
questions.e: A parallel line has the form 3x + 2y + k = 0. Substituting (1, −2): 3 − 4 + k = 0, so k = 1, giving 3x + 2y + 1 = 0. 2x − 3y − 8 = 0 passes through the point but is perpendicular to the given line.

questions.s: The equation of the line through (−2, 5) perpendicular to x − 3y + 4 = 0 is
questions.e: The given slope is 1/3, so the perpendicular slope is −3 and the line is 3x + y + k = 0. Substituting (−2, 5): −6 + 5 + k = 0, so k = 1. 3x − y + 11 = 0 has slope +3 (the negative reciprocal sign was dropped), and x − 3y + 17 = 0 is the parallel line.

questions.s: Two non-vertical lines with slopes m₁ and m₂ are perpendicular if and only if
questions.e: Perpendicular slopes are negative reciprocals, m₂ = −1/m₁, so m₁m₂ = −1. m₁ = m₂ is the condition for parallel lines, and m₁ + m₂ = 0 only says the lines are equally inclined to the x-axis on opposite sides (for example slopes 2 and −2, whose product is −4).

questions.s: The lines 2x + ky − 5 = 0 and 6x − 4y + 1 = 0 are perpendicular when k equals
questions.e: For a₁x + b₁y + c₁ = 0 and a₂x + b₂y + c₂ = 0 to be perpendicular, a₁a₂ + b₁b₂ = 0: 12 − 4k = 0, so k = 3. The value −4/3 makes the lines parallel (2/6 = k/(−4)), not perpendicular.

questions.s: The acute angle between the lines 2x − y + 3 = 0 and 3x + y − 7 = 0 is
questions.e: The slopes are 2 and −3. tan θ = |(m₁ − m₂)/(1 + m₁m₂)| = |(2 + 3)/(1 − 6)| = |5/(−5)| = 1, so θ = 45°. The lines are not perpendicular because m₁m₂ = −6, not −1.

questions.s: The acute angle between the lines √3x − y + 1 = 0 and x − √3y + 2 = 0 is
questions.e: The slopes are √3 and 1/√3, so the inclinations are 60° and 30°, and the angle between the lines is 60° − 30° = 30°. 60° is just the inclination of the first line; the lines are not perpendicular since the product of slopes is 1, not −1.

questions.s: The slopes of the two lines through the origin that make an angle of 45° with the line 3x − y = 0 are
questions.e: The given slope is 3, so |(m − 3)/(1 + 3m)| = 1. Case m − 3 = 1 + 3m gives m = −2; case m − 3 = −(1 + 3m) gives 4m = 2, m = 1/2. Check m = 1/2: (1/2 − 3)/(1 + 3/2) = −1. The pair −1/2 and 2 has both signs reversed.

questions.s: Which of the following lines is parallel to 4x − 6y + 5 = 0?
questions.e: The given slope is −4/(−6) = 2/3. Only 2x − 3y + 7 = 0 has slope 2/3 (its coefficients are half of 4 and −6). 3x − 2y + 1 = 0 and 6x − 4y = 0 have slope 3/2, the reciprocal, and 2x + 3y − 4 = 0 has slope −2/3.

questions.s: The perpendicular bisector of the segment joining A(1, 4) and B(5, −2) is
questions.e: The midpoint is (3, 1) and the slope of AB is −6/4 = −3/2, so the bisector has slope 2/3: y − 1 = (2/3)(x − 3), giving 2x − 3y − 3 = 0. 3x + 2y − 11 = 0 is the line AB itself, since A and B each satisfy it.

questions.s: The foot of the perpendicular from the point P(1, 2) to the line x + y − 7 = 0 is
questions.e: The perpendicular through P has direction (1, 1), so the foot is (1 + t, 2 + t). Substituting: 3 + 2t − 7 = 0 gives t = 2, so the foot is (3, 4). (5, 6) uses t = 4 and is the reflection of P in the line; (4, 3) and (2, 5) lie on the line but PQ is not perpendicular to it.

questions.s: The image (reflection) of the point (3, −1) in the line x − 2y + 5 = 0 is
questions.e: Image: (x − 3)/1 = (y + 1)/(−2) = −2(3 + 2 + 5)/(1 + 4) = −4, so x = −1 and y = 7. Check: the midpoint (1, 3) lies on the line and the segment has slope −2, perpendicular to slope 1/2. (1, 3) is only the foot of the perpendicular, and (7, −9) comes from a sign error.

questions.s: The y-intercept of the line passing through (2, 7) and (−1, −2) is
questions.e: Slope = (7 + 2)/(2 + 1) = 3, so y − 7 = 3(x − 2), i.e. y = 3x + 1, and the y-intercept is 1. −1/3 is the x-intercept (put y = 0), and 3 is the slope.

questions.s: The line 2x + 3y = 12 meets the x-axis at A and the y-axis at B. The midpoint of AB is
questions.e: A = (6, 0) and B = (0, 4), so the midpoint is (3, 2). (2, 3) reverses the coordinates, and (6, 4) lists the intercepts without halving.

questions.s: The area of the triangle formed by the line 3x + 4y = 24 and the coordinate axes is
questions.e: The intercepts are 24/3 = 8 and 24/4 = 6, so the area is ½ × 8 × 6 = 24 sq. units. 48 forgets the factor ½.

questions.s: The equation of the y-axis is
questions.e: Every point on the y-axis has x-coordinate zero, so its equation is x = 0. y = 0 is the x-axis, and x = y is the line bisecting the first and third quadrants.

questions.s: A line meets the coordinate axes at A and B so that the point (3, 4) is the midpoint of AB. The equation of the line is
questions.e: If (3, 4) is the midpoint, A = (6, 0) and B = (0, 8), so x/6 + y/8 = 1, i.e. 4x + 3y = 24. 3x + 4y = 24 swaps the intercepts, and 3x + 4y = 25 passes through (3, 4) but its intercepts are 25/3 and 25/4.

questions.s: A line through P(2, 1) meets the x-axis at A and the y-axis at B so that AP : PB = 1 : 2. The equation of the line is
questions.e: Let A = (a, 0), B = (0, b). P divides AB in 1 : 2, so P = ((2a + 0)/3, (0 + b)/3) = (2a/3, b/3) = (2, 1), giving a = 3 and b = 3. The line is x/3 + y/3 = 1, i.e. x + y = 3. x + 4y = 6 results from using the ratio 2 : 1.

questions.s: The acute angle between the line x = 5 and the line x − √3y + 1 = 0 is
questions.e: x = 5 is vertical (inclination 90°). The second line has slope 1/√3, so its inclination is 30°. The angle between them is 90° − 30° = 60°. Answering 30° gives the angle with the x-axis, not with the vertical line.

questions.s: If the lines 3x + ky + 4 = 0 and 6x − 2y + 1 = 0 are parallel, then k equals
questions.e: Parallel lines need a₁/a₂ = b₁/b₂: 3/6 = k/(−2), so k = −1. Then the first line is 3x − y + 4 = 0 with slope 3, matching 6x − 2y + 1 = 0. k = 9 satisfies a₁a₂ + b₁b₂ = 0, the perpendicular condition.

questions.s: The perpendicular distance of the point (2, 3) from the line 3x + 4y − 8 = 0 is
questions.e: d = |3(2) + 4(3) − 8|/√(3² + 4²) = |6 + 12 − 8|/5 = 10/5 = 2. The value 10 forgets to divide by √(a² + b²) = 5, and 26/5 uses +8 instead of −8.

questions.s: The distance between the parallel lines 3x − 4y + 7 = 0 and 6x − 8y − 1 = 0 is
questions.e: First make the coefficients equal: the second line is 3x − 4y − 1/2 = 0. Then d = |7 − (−1/2)|/√(9 + 16) = (15/2)/5 = 3/2. Using |7 − (−1)|/5 = 8/5 without rescaling is the common mistake.

questions.s: The length of the perpendicular from the origin to the line 5x − 12y + 39 = 0 is
questions.e: From the origin, d = |c|/√(a² + b²) = 39/√(25 + 144) = 39/13 = 3. 39/17 divides by a + b with signs ignored (5 + 12), and 39/7 divides by |a + b|.

questions.s: If the distance of the point (1, k) from the line 4x + 3y − 1 = 0 is 3 units, then k is
questions.e: |4 + 3k − 1|/5 = 3 gives |3 + 3k| = 15, so 3 + 3k = 15 (k = 4) or 3 + 3k = −15 (k = −6). The pair −4 or 6 has the signs swapped, from solving |3k − 3| = 15 instead.

questions.s: The lines parallel to 3x − 4y + 2 = 0 at a distance of 2 units from it are
questions.e: A parallel line is 3x − 4y + c = 0 with |c − 2|/5 = 2, so c − 2 = ±10 and c = 12 or −8. The pair with ±10 forgets that the given line has its own constant 2, and the pair with c = 4 and 0 forgets to multiply the distance by 5.

questions.s: Which of the following points lies on the same side of the line 2x − 3y + 6 = 0 as the origin?
questions.e: At the origin 2x − 3y + 6 = 6 > 0. At (1, 2): 2 − 6 + 6 = 2 > 0, so it is on the same side. (−4, 1) gives −5 and (0, 3) gives −3, both on the other side, while (−3, 0) gives 0 and lies on the line itself.

questions.s: The lines x + y = 5 and x − y = 1 intersect at
questions.e: Adding the equations gives 2x = 6, so x = 3 and then y = 5 − 3 = 2. (2, 3) satisfies x + y = 5 but gives x − y = −1, and (4, 1) satisfies only the first equation.

questions.s: The lines 2x − y + 1 = 0, x + y − 4 = 0 and kx + 2y − 9 = 0 are concurrent. The value of k is
questions.e: Adding the first two equations gives 3x − 3 = 0, so x = 1 and y = 3. The third line must pass through (1, 3): k + 6 − 9 = 0, so k = 3. The value 9 comes from forgetting the term 2y = 6.

questions.s: The lines ax + y + 1 = 0, x + ay + 1 = 0 and x + y + a = 0, where a ≠ 1, are concurrent when a equals
questions.e: Concurrency requires the determinant of coefficients |a 1 1; 1 a 1; 1 1 a| = a³ − 3a + 2 = (a − 1)²(a + 2) to be zero. Since a ≠ 1 (then all three lines coincide), a = −2. Check: −2x + y + 1 = 0 and x − 2y + 1 = 0 meet at (1, 1), which satisfies x + y − 2 = 0.

questions.s: The lines x + 2y − 5 = 0, 2x − y = 0 and 3x + ky − 11 = 0 are concurrent. The value of k is
questions.e: From 2x − y = 0, y = 2x; then x + 4x = 5 gives x = 1, y = 2. Substituting (1, 2) in the third line: 3 + 2k − 11 = 0, so k = 4. The value −4 comes from a sign slip with the constant −11.

questions.s: The area of the triangle with vertices (1, 2), (4, 2) and (1, 7) is
questions.e: The side from (1, 2) to (4, 2) is horizontal with length 3, and the side from (1, 2) to (1, 7) is vertical with length 5, so the angle at (1, 2) is right. Area = ½ × 3 × 5 = 15/2 sq. units. 15 forgets the ½.

questions.s: The area of the triangle with vertices (2, 1), (6, 3) and (−1, 4) is
questions.e: Area = ½|x₁(y₂ − y₃) + x₂(y₃ − y₁) + x₃(y₁ − y₂)| = ½|2(3 − 4) + 6(4 − 1) + (−1)(1 − 3)| = ½|−2 + 18 + 2| = 9 sq. units. 18 is the value of the bracket before halving.

questions.s: The area of the triangle with vertices (k, 0), (4, 0) and (0, 2) is 4 square units. Then k is
questions.e: The base lies on the x-axis with length |4 − k| and the height is 2, so ½ × |4 − k| × 2 = 4 gives |4 − k| = 4. Hence k = 0 or k = 8. The option 2 or 6 forgets the factor ½ (it solves |4 − k| = 2).

questions.s: The area of the quadrilateral whose vertices, taken in order, are (1, 1), (5, 2), (6, 6) and (2, 5) is
questions.e: Shoelace: (1·2 − 5·1) + (5·6 − 6·2) + (6·5 − 2·6) + (2·1 − 1·5) = −3 + 18 + 18 − 3 = 30, and the area is ½ × 30 = 15 sq. units. 30 forgets the ½; the figure is in fact a rhombus with diagonals √50 and √18, and ½√50·√18 = ½ × 30 = 15 confirms it.

questions.s: The area of the triangle bounded by the lines y = x, y = −x and y = 4 is
questions.e: The vertices are (0, 0), (4, 4) and (−4, 4). The base on y = 4 has length 8 and the height from the origin is 4, so the area is ½ × 8 × 4 = 16 sq. units. 8 uses only one half of the base, from (0, 4) to (4, 4).

questions.s: The area of the triangle bounded by the lines x + y = 6, x − y = 2 and the x-axis is
questions.e: x + y = 6 and x − y = 2 meet at (4, 2); they cut the x-axis at (6, 0) and (2, 0). Base = 4, height = 2, so area = ½ × 4 × 2 = 4 sq. units. 8 forgets the factor ½.

questions.s: Three distinct points A, B and C are collinear if and only if
o: the area of triangle ABC is zero
the distances AB and BC are equal
the slopes of AB and BC multiply to −1
the midpoint of AC lies on the y-axis
questions.e: Collinear points form a degenerate triangle, so the area formula ½|x₁(y₂ − y₃) + x₂(y₃ − y₁) + x₃(y₁ − y₂)| gives zero, and conversely. AB = BC alone only puts B on the perpendicular bisector of AC, and slopes with product −1 mean AB ⊥ BC.

questions.s: The length of the perpendicular from the point (−2, 3) to the line 5x − 12y = 6 is
questions.e: Write the line as 5x − 12y − 6 = 0. Then d = |5(−2) − 12(3) − 6|/√(25 + 144) = |−10 − 36 − 6|/13 = 52/13 = 4. 40/13 comes from taking the constant as +6, and 52 forgets to divide by 13.

questions.s: The distance between the parallel lines y = 2x + 3 and y = 2x − 7 is
questions.e: Write them as 2x − y + 3 = 0 and 2x − y − 7 = 0. Then d = |3 − (−7)|/√(4 + 1) = 10/√5 = 2√5. The value 10 is only the vertical gap between the lines, and 4/√5 subtracts the constants with the wrong sign.

questions.s: In triangle ABC with A(0, 0), B(3, 4) and C(4, 3), the length of the altitude from C to AB is
questions.e: Line AB is y = (4/3)x, i.e. 4x − 3y = 0. The altitude from C is its distance from this line: |16 − 9|/5 = 7/5. Check with area: ½ × AB × h = ½ × 5 × 7/5 = 7/2, which matches ½|3·3 − 4·4| = 7/2. √2 is the length of BC, not the altitude.

questions.s: The points on the line x + y = 4 that are at a distance of 1 unit from the line 4x + 3y = 10 are
questions.e: A point on x + y = 4 is (t, 4 − t). Its distance from 4x + 3y − 10 = 0 is |4t + 12 − 3t − 10|/5 = |t + 2|/5 = 1, so t + 2 = ±5 and t = 3 or −7, giving (3, 1) and (−7, 11). (1, 3) and (11, −7) swap the coordinates and do not satisfy the distance condition.

questions.s: The point of intersection of the lines 2x + 3y = 7 and 3x − y = 5 is
questions.e: From 3x − y = 5, y = 3x − 5. Then 2x + 9x − 15 = 7, so 11x = 22, x = 2 and y = 1. (1, 2) gives 2 + 6 = 8 ≠ 7, so it is not on the first line, and (2, −1) gives 4 − 3 = 1 ≠ 7.

questions.s: The line through the point of intersection of x + y = 3 and 2x − y = 0, parallel to 3x + y = 1, is
questions.e: Adding x + y = 3 and 2x − y = 0 gives x = 1, y = 2. A parallel line is 3x + y = k with k = 3 + 2 = 5. 3x + y = 7 uses the point (2, 1) by mistake, and x − 3y + 5 = 0 is the perpendicular line through (1, 2).

questions.s: For every real k, the line (2 + k)x + (1 − k)y + k − 4 = 0 passes through a fixed point. That point is
questions.e: Regroup: (2x + y − 4) + k(x − y + 1) = 0. This holds for all k when 2x + y − 4 = 0 and x − y + 1 = 0, which give 3x = 3, x = 1 and y = 2. Check (2, 1): the left side becomes 1 + 2k, which is not zero for all k.

questions.s: Which of the following points satisfies the inequality 3x + 2y < 6?
questions.e: Substitute each point: (1, 1) gives 3 + 2 = 5 < 6. (0, 3) gives exactly 6, which lies on the boundary and fails the strict inequality; (2, 1) gives 8 and (3, −1) gives 7.

questions.s: The graph of the inequality x ≥ 0 in the xy-plane is
o: the y-axis and the half-plane to its right
the x-axis and the half-plane above it
the y-axis and the half-plane to its left
the half-plane right of the y-axis, with the axis excluded
questions.e: x ≥ 0 holds for every point with a non-negative x-coordinate: the line x = 0 (the y-axis) and all points to its right. The axis is included because of the equality sign, so the open half-plane is wrong; the x-axis option describes y ≥ 0.

questions.s: When the inequality 2x − 5y ≥ 10 is graphed, its boundary line is drawn as
o: a solid line, since equality is included
a broken line, since equality is excluded
a solid line, since equality is excluded
a broken line, since equality is included
questions.e: The sign ≥ includes the points where 2x − 5y = 10, so the boundary is part of the solution set and is drawn solid. A broken (dashed) line is used only for strict inequalities such as > or <.

questions.s: Which statement about the solution region of 3x − 4y > 12 is correct?
questions.e: Test each point in 3x − 4y: (4, −1) gives 12 + 4 = 16 > 12, so it is in the region. The origin gives 0, (0, −2) gives 8 and (5, 1) gives 15 − 4 = 11, all less than 12.

questions.s: The closed half-plane lying below the line x + 2y = 8 (the line included) is represented by
questions.e: Below the line means y ≤ (8 − x)/2, i.e. x + 2y ≤ 8; the origin (0 ≤ 8) lies below the line, which agrees. The strict sign < would leave out the line, and x + 2y ≥ 8 is the region above it.

questions.s: A region is the open half-plane on the same side as the origin of the line through (4, 0) and (0, −3). The region is
questions.e: The line is x/4 + y/(−3) = 1, i.e. 3x − 4y = 12. The origin gives 0 < 12, so its side is 3x − 4y < 12; 'open' excludes the line, so ≤ is wrong. 4x − 3y = 12 would cut the axes at 3 and −4 instead.

questions.s: Which point lies in the solution region of the system x + y ≤ 5, x − y ≥ 1, y ≥ 0?
questions.e: (3, 1): x + y = 4 ≤ 5, x − y = 2 ≥ 1 and y = 1 ≥ 0, so all three hold. (2, 2) gives x − y = 0 < 1, (1, 3) gives x − y = −2, and (5, 2) gives x + y = 7 > 5.

questions.s: The solution region of x ≥ 0, y ≥ 0, 2x + y ≤ 6 is a triangle whose vertices are
questions.e: The line 2x + y = 6 meets the x-axis where 2x = 6, at (3, 0), and the y-axis at (0, 6); with the origin these bound the region. (6, 0) and (0, 3) swap the intercepts, as if the line were x + 2y = 6.

questions.s: Which of the following is NOT a corner point of the feasible region x ≥ 0, y ≥ 0, x + y ≤ 6, x + 3y ≤ 12?
questions.e: x + y = 6 and x + 3y = 12 meet where 2y = 6, at (3, 3). The corners are (0, 0), (6, 0), (3, 3) and (0, 4). (0, 6) is the y-intercept of x + y = 6, but it violates x + 3y ≤ 12 because 18 > 12.

questions.s: The area of the feasible region x ≥ 0, y ≥ 0, x + 2y ≤ 8, 3x + 2y ≤ 12 is
questions.e: Subtracting x + 2y = 8 from 3x + 2y = 12 gives x = 2, y = 3. The corners in order are (0, 0), (4, 0), (2, 3), (0, 4). Shoelace: ½|4·3 − 2·0 + 2·4 − 0·3| = ½ × 20 = 10 sq. units. 20 forgets the ½.

questions.s: Which of the following is a vertex of the region given by y ≥ 2x, y ≤ 3, x ≥ 0?
questions.e: The region is the triangle bounded by x = 0, y = 3 and y = 2x, with vertices (0, 0), (0, 3) and the meeting point of y = 2x and y = 3, which is (3/2, 3). (1, 3) lies on the edge y = 3 but is not a corner; (3, 3) fails y ≥ 2x and (3, 6) fails y ≤ 3.

questions.s: The system of inequalities x ≥ 0, y ≤ 0 represents
o: the first quadrant with its bounding axes
the second quadrant with its bounding axes
the third quadrant with its bounding axes
the fourth quadrant with its bounding axes
questions.e: Points with x ≥ 0 and y ≤ 0 are to the right of (or on) the y-axis and below (or on) the x-axis, which is the fourth quadrant. The first quadrant needs y ≥ 0 as well.

questions.s: The system of inequalities x + y ≥ 6 and x + y ≤ 2 has
questions.e: No number x + y can be at least 6 and at most 2 at the same time, so the two half-planes, bounded by parallel lines, do not overlap and the solution set is empty. A strip would arise only for a system such as 2 ≤ x + y ≤ 6.

questions.s: The point (a, 2) lies in the solution region of 3x − y > 4 exactly when
questions.e: Substitute: 3a − 2 > 4 gives 3a > 6, so a > 2. a ≥ 2 includes a = 2, which gives 3a − 2 = 4 and fails the strict inequality; a > 2/3 forgets to move the −2.

questions.s: The closed triangular region with vertices (1, 1), (5, 1) and (1, 4) is described by
questions.e: The sides are x = 1, y = 1 and the line through (5, 1) and (1, 4), which has slope −3/4: 3x + 4y = 19. An inside point such as (2, 2) gives x ≥ 1, y ≥ 1 and 6 + 8 = 14 ≤ 19. 4x + 3y = 19 passes through (4, 1) and (1, 5), not the given vertices.

questions.s: In a linear programming problem, the optimal value of the objective function, if it exists, occurs at
o: the centroid of the feasible region
a corner point of the feasible region
any interior point of the feasible region
questions.e: A linear objective function takes its maximum and minimum over a convex polygonal feasible region at a vertex (corner point), which is why we test the corner points. An interior point can always be moved to improve a non-constant linear function, and the origin is often not optimal or not even feasible.

questions.s: In a linear programming problem, the conditions x ≥ 0 and y ≥ 0 are called
questions.e: x ≥ 0 and y ≥ 0 are the non-negative constraints: the quantities being decided cannot be negative. x and y themselves are the decision variables, and the function being maximised or minimised is the objective function.

questions.s: The maximum value of f = 3x + 2y subject to x ≥ 0, y ≥ 0, x + y ≤ 4, x ≤ 3 is
questions.e: The corners are (0, 0), (3, 0), (3, 1) and (0, 4), where f = 0, 9, 11 and 8. The maximum is 11 at (3, 1). 12 would come from (4, 0), which violates x ≤ 3.

questions.s: The minimum value of f = 2x + 5y subject to x + y ≥ 4, x ≤ 3, y ≤ 3 is
questions.e: The feasible region is the triangle with corners (1, 3), (3, 1) and (3, 3), where f = 17, 11 and 21. The minimum is 11 at (3, 1). 8 comes from (4, 0), which violates x ≤ 3.

questions.s: The maximum value of z = 5x + 4y subject to x ≥ 0, y ≥ 0, x + 2y ≤ 8, 3x + 2y ≤ 12 is
questions.e: x + 2y = 8 and 3x + 2y = 12 meet at (2, 3). The corners are (0, 0), (4, 0), (2, 3), (0, 4), giving z = 0, 20, 22, 16, so the maximum is 22 at (2, 3). 20 is the value at (4, 0), a corner but not the best one.

questions.s: The corner points of a feasible region are (0, 2), (3, 0), (6, 0), (6, 8) and (0, 5). The minimum of z = 4x + 6y occurs at
o: all points on the segment from (0, 2) to (3, 0)
questions.e: At the corners z = 12, 12, 24, 72 and 30. The minimum 12 is reached at both (0, 2) and (3, 0), and the edge joining them is 2x + 3y = 6, on which 4x + 6y = 12 everywhere, so every point of that edge is optimal. (0, 0) is not a corner of the region.

questions.s: The corner points of a feasible region are (0, 0), (5, 0), (4, 3) and (0, 6). The maximum value of z = 2x + 3y on this region is
questions.e: At the corners z = 0, 10, 8 + 9 = 17 and 18. The maximum is 18 at (0, 6). 17 is the value at (4, 3), which is tempting because it looks like the 'middle' corner, and 15 comes from swapping the coefficients at (5, 0).

questions.s: A shopkeeper in Lahore stocks x fans and y lamps. He has space for at most 20 items; a fan costs Rs 2000, a lamp Rs 1000, and he can spend at most Rs 30 000. His profit is Rs 300 per fan and Rs 200 per lamp. His maximum profit is
questions.e: Constraints: x + y ≤ 20 and 2x + y ≤ 30 with x, y ≥ 0. The lines meet at (10, 10). Corners: (0, 0), (15, 0), (10, 10), (0, 20), where P = 300x + 200y = 0, 4500, 5000, 4000. The maximum is Rs 5000. Rs 6000 assumes 20 fans, which would cost Rs 40 000.

questions.s: The minimum value of z = 3x + 2y subject to x + y ≥ 5, x ≥ 1, y ≥ 1 is
questions.e: The feasible region is unbounded with corners (1, 4) and (4, 1), where z = 3 + 8 = 11 and 12 + 2 = 14. Since both coefficients are positive, z only grows along the unbounded edges, so the minimum is 11 at (1, 4). 10 comes from (0, 5), which violates x ≥ 1.

questions.s: The distance of the point (−5, 12) from the origin is
questions.e: d = √((−5)² + 12²) = √(25 + 144) = √169 = 13. The value 7 adds −5 and 12 directly, 17 adds their sizes, and √119 subtracts the squares instead of adding them.

questions.s: The points (0, −1), (2, 1), (0, 3) and (−2, 1), taken in order, are the vertices of
o: a rhombus that is not a square
a rectangle that is not a square
a trapezium that is not a parallelogram
questions.e: Each side has length √(4 + 4) = 2√2, so the figure is a rhombus. The diagonals, from (0, −1) to (0, 3) and from (2, 1) to (−2, 1), both have length 4, and a rhombus with equal diagonals is a square.

questions.s: The point that divides the segment from A(−4, 6) to B(8, −6) internally in the ratio 3 : 1 is
questions.e: x = (3·8 + 1·(−4))/4 = 20/4 = 5 and y = (3·(−6) + 1·6)/4 = −12/4 = −3, giving (5, −3). (−1, 3) uses the ratio 1 : 3, (2, 0) is the midpoint, and (14, −12) is the external division point.

questions.s: The line 2x + y = 6 divides the segment joining (1, 1) and (5, 5) in the ratio
questions.e: Put each end point into 2x + y − 6: (1, 1) gives −3 and (5, 5) gives 9. The ratio is −(−3)/9 = 1/3, and it is positive, so the division is 1 : 3 internally. Check: the point (1·5 + 3·1)/4 = 2, (1·5 + 3·1)/4 = 2 gives 2(2) + 2 = 6. Writing 3 : 1 reverses the order of the end points.

questions.s: The triangle with vertices A(2, 1), B(5, 3) and C(k, 4) is right-angled at A. Then k equals
questions.e: Slope AB = 2/3, so AC must have slope −3/2: 3/(k − 2) = −3/2 gives k − 2 = −2 and k = 0. k = 4 gives AC the slope 3/2, the reciprocal of 2/3 rather than its negative reciprocal, and −2 is the value of k − 2, not k.

questions.s: If θ is the angle measured from the line with slope m₁ to the line with slope m₂ (m₁m₂ ≠ −1), then tan θ equals
questions.e: With m₁ = tan α₁ and m₂ = tan α₂, θ = α₂ − α₁, and tan(α₂ − α₁) = (tan α₂ − tan α₁)/(1 + tan α₁ tan α₂) = (m₂ − m₁)/(1 + m₁m₂). The form with (1 − m₁m₂) in the denominator belongs to tan(α₁ + α₂).

questions.s: The lines through (1, 2) that make an angle of 45° with the line x + y = 0 are
questions.e: x + y = 0 has inclination 135°. Lines at 45° to it have inclination 135° ± 45°, that is 90° or 180°: a vertical line and a horizontal line. Through (1, 2) these are x = 1 and y = 2. The pair y = x + 1 and y = 3 − x makes angles of 90° and 0° with the given line.

questions.s: A line through (−3, 4) has its y-intercept equal to twice its x-intercept (both non-zero). Its equation is
questions.e: Take x/a + y/(2a) = 1, i.e. 2x + y = 2a. Substituting (−3, 4): −6 + 4 = 2a, so a = −1 and the line is 2x + y + 2 = 0, with intercepts −1 and −2. x + 2y − 5 = 0 passes through (−3, 4) but its x-intercept (5) is twice its y-intercept (5/2), the reverse.

questions.s: In slope-intercept form, the line 4x + 2y − 6 = 0 is
questions.e: Solve for y: 2y = −4x + 6, so y = −2x + 3, with slope −2 and y-intercept 3. y = −x/2 + 3/2 comes from dividing by 4 (the x-coefficient) instead of 2.

questions.s: The perpendicular distance of the origin from the line x/2 − y/3 = 1 is
questions.e: Clear fractions: 3x − 2y − 6 = 0. Then d = |−6|/√(9 + 4) = 6/√13. 6/5 divides by 3 + 2 instead of √(3² + 2²), and √13/6 is the reciprocal.

questions.s: In triangle ABC with A(3, 4), B(−1, 1) and C(5, −7), the length of the altitude from A to BC is
The lines 3x + y − 2 = 0, px + 2y − 3 = 0 and 2x − y − 3 = 0 are concurrent. The value of p is
questions.e: Adding the first and third equations gives 5x − 5 = 0, so x = 1 and y = −1. Substituting (1, −1) in the second line: p − 2 − 3 = 0, so p = 5. The value 1 comes from taking y = +1.

questions.s: The point on the line 2x − 3y + 6 = 0 whose x-coordinate is 3 is
questions.e: Put x = 3: 6 − 3y + 6 = 0, so 3y = 12 and y = 4. (3, −4) comes from a sign slip when moving 12 across, and (3, 0) is not on the line because 6 + 6 ≠ 0.

questions.s: The maximum value of z = x + y subject to x ≥ 0, y ≥ 0, x + 2y ≤ 10, 2x + y ≤ 14 is
questions.e: The lines x + 2y = 10 and 2x + y = 14 meet at (6, 2). The corners are (0, 0), (7, 0), (6, 2) and (0, 5), where z = 0, 7, 8 and 5. The maximum is 8. 10 would need (10, 0), which violates 2x + y ≤ 14.

questions.s: Zainab bakes x cakes and y batches of biscuits. A cake needs 2 hours of oven time and 1 kg of flour; a batch needs 1 hour and 1 kg. She has 12 oven hours and 8 kg of flour. Profit is Rs 500 per cake and Rs 300 per batch. Her profit is greatest when she makes
o: 8 batches of biscuits and no cakes
questions.e: Constraints: 2x + y ≤ 12, x + y ≤ 8, x, y ≥ 0; the lines meet at (4, 4). Corners: (6, 0), (4, 4), (0, 8) give profits Rs 3000, Rs 3200, Rs 2400, so (4, 4) is best. (5, 2) is feasible but gives only Rs 3100 and is not a corner.

questions.s: The region between the lines y = 1 and y = 4, both lines included, is described by
questions.e: The lines y = 1 and y = 4 are horizontal, so the strip between them is 1 ≤ y ≤ 4, with ≤ because the lines are included. 1 < y < 4 leaves out the lines, and 1 ≤ x ≤ 4 is a vertical strip.

questions.s: The area of the region x ≥ 0, y ≥ 0, x + y ≥ 2, x + y ≤ 5 is
questions.e: The region is the triangle cut off by x + y ≤ 5 (area ½ × 5 × 5 = 25/2) minus the triangle with x + y < 2 (area ½ × 2 × 2 = 2), so the area is 25/2 − 2 = 21/2. 29/2 adds the small triangle instead of removing it.

questions.s: The number of points with integer coordinates in the region x ≥ 0, y ≥ 0, y ≥ x, x + y ≤ 4 is
questions.e: The region is the triangle with corners (0, 0), (2, 2) and (0, 4). Count by columns: x = 0 gives y = 0 to 4 (5 points), x = 1 gives y = 1 to 3 (3 points), x = 2 gives y = 2 (1 point), total 9. 15 counts all lattice points with x + y ≤ 4 in the first quadrant, ignoring y ≥ x.

questions.s: The points (2, −1) and (a, 3) lie on opposite sides of the line 3x − 2y + 1 = 0 exactly when
questions.e: At (2, −1), 3x − 2y + 1 = 6 + 2 + 1 = 9 > 0. For (a, 3) to be on the other side, 3a − 6 + 1 < 0, so 3a < 5 and a < 5/3. a > 5/3 would put both points on the same side.

questions.s: When x + √3y = 6 is written in normal form x cos α + y sin α = p, the values of α and p are
questions.e: Divide by √(1 + 3) = 2: (1/2)x + (√3/2)y = 3. Then cos α = 1/2 and sin α = √3/2, so α = 60°, and p = 3. α = 30° swaps cos and sin, and p = 6 forgets to divide the constant by 2.

questions.s: The distance between the points (1, −3) and (1, 4) is
questions.e: Both points have x = 1, so the segment is vertical and its length is |4 − (−3)| = 7. The value 1 comes from 4 + (−3), and √50 wrongly adds a horizontal difference of 1.

questions.s: M(2, 3) is the midpoint of AB, where A is (−1, 5). The point B is
questions.e: B = 2M − A = (4 + 1, 6 − 5) = (5, 1). Check: the midpoint of (−1, 5) and (5, 1) is (2, 3). (1/2, 4) is the midpoint of A and M, and (3, −2) is only M − A.

questions.s: In triangle ABC with A(1, 1), B(4, 2) and C(3, 5), the interior angle at A is
questions.e: Slope AB = 1/3 and slope AC = 4/2 = 2, so tan A = (2 − 1/3)/(1 + 2/3) = (5/3)/(5/3) = 1 and A = 45°. The right angle is at B, since slope BA × slope BC = (1/3)(−3) = −1, which makes 90° tempting for the wrong vertex.

questions.s: The line joining the origin to the point of intersection of 2x + y = 5 and x − 3y = −1 is
questions.e: From x = 3y − 1, 2(3y − 1) + y = 5 gives y = 1 and x = 2. The line through (0, 0) and (2, 1) is y = x/2, i.e. x − 2y = 0. 2x − y = 0 joins the origin to (1, 2), with the coordinates swapped.

questions.s: The distance between the points (−3, 5) and (4, −19) is
questions.e: Δx = 7 and Δy = −24, so d = √(49 + 576) = √625 = 25. 31 adds 7 and 24 directly, 17 subtracts them, and √527 subtracts the squares.

questions.s: The midpoint of the segment joining (−6, 4) and (2, 10) is
questions.e: Midpoint = ((−6 + 2)/2, (4 + 10)/2) = (−4/2, 14/2) = (−2, 7). (−4, 14) adds the coordinates without halving, and (−4, 3) halves the differences instead of the sums.

questions.s: The centroid of a triangle is (1, 2) and two of its vertices are (3, −1) and (−2, 4). The third vertex is
questions.e: The coordinates of the three vertices add up to 3 × centroid = (3, 6). So the third vertex is (3 − 3 + 2, 6 + 1 − 4) = (2, 3). (3, 6) is 3G itself, before subtracting the two known vertices, and (1/2, 3/2) is just the midpoint of the given vertices.

questions.s: The inclination of the line 3x + √3y − 7 = 0 is
questions.e: Slope = −3/√3 = −√3, and tan α = −√3 with 0° ≤ α < 180° gives α = 120°. Choosing 60° ignores the negative sign, and 150° corresponds to slope −1/√3.

questions.s: The equation of the line with inclination 45° and y-intercept −3 is
questions.e: Slope = tan 45° = 1, so y = x − 3, i.e. x − y − 3 = 0. x − y + 3 = 0 has y-intercept +3, and x + y + 3 = 0 has slope −1 (inclination 135°).

questions.s: The equation of the line through (4, −1) perpendicular to 2x + 5y = 3 is
questions.e: Swap the coefficients and change one sign: 5x − 2y + k = 0. Substituting (4, −1): 20 + 2 + k = 0, so k = −22. 2x + 5y − 3 = 0 passes through (4, −1) but is parallel to the given line, and 5x + 2y − 18 = 0 has slope −5/2.

questions.s: The acute angle between the lines x − y = 0 and √3x − y = 0 is
questions.e: The slopes are 1 and √3, so the inclinations are 45° and 60°, and the angle between the lines is 60° − 45° = 15°. 45° is only the inclination of the first line, and 75° is not the difference of the inclinations.

questions.s: A(2, 0) and B(0, 4) are two points. The perpendicular from the origin to AB meets AB at
questions.e: AB is x/2 + y/4 = 1, i.e. 2x + y = 4, with slope −2. The perpendicular through O has slope 1/2: x = 2y. Then 4y + y = 4 gives y = 4/5, x = 8/5. (1, 2) is the midpoint of AB, which is the foot only for an isosceles right triangle, and (4/5, 8/5) does not lie on AB.

questions.s: The perpendicular distance of the point (−1, 1) from the line 6x + 8y + 8 = 0 is
questions.e: d = |6(−1) + 8(1) + 8|/√(36 + 64) = |−6 + 8 + 8|/10 = 10/10 = 1. 10 forgets to divide by √(a² + b²), 5/7 divides by 6 + 8, and 3/5 comes from taking the constant as −8.

questions.s: The distance between the parallel lines x + 2y = 3 and 2x + 4y + 9 = 0 is
questions.e: Write both with the same coefficients: x + 2y − 3 = 0 and x + 2y + 9/2 = 0. Then d = |9/2 + 3|/√5 = (15/2)/√5 = 15/(2√5) = 3√5/2. 12/√5 uses |9 + 3| without halving the 9 first.

questions.s: The lines x + y = 1, 2x − y = 5 and 4x + ky = 7 are concurrent. The value of k is
questions.e: Adding the first two equations gives 3x = 6, so x = 2 and y = −1. Substituting (2, −1) in the third: 8 − k = 7, so k = 1. The value −1 comes from writing 8 + k = 7, forgetting that y is negative.

questions.s: The area of the triangle with vertices (0, 0), (5, 0) and (2, 6) is
questions.e: The base from (0, 0) to (5, 0) has length 5 and the height is the y-coordinate of (2, 6), which is 6. Area = ½ × 5 × 6 = 15 sq. units. 6 wrongly uses the x-coordinate 2 as the base, and 15/2 applies the factor ½ twice.

questions.s: The area of the triangle bounded by the lines y = 2x, x = 2y and x + y = 6 is
questions.e: The vertices are the origin, (2, 4) from y = 2x with x + y = 6, and (4, 2) from x = 2y with x + y = 6. With one vertex at the origin, area = ½|x₁y₂ − x₂y₁| = ½|2·2 − 4·4| = ½ × 12 = 6 sq. units. 12 forgets the ½.

questions.s: Which of the following points lies in the solution region of x − 2y ≥ 4?
questions.e: (6, 1) gives 6 − 2 = 4, and 4 ≥ 4 holds because the boundary is included. (5, 1) gives 3, (2, 0) gives 2 and (0, −1) gives 2, all less than 4.

questions.s: The open half-plane lying above the line through (0, 2) with slope 1 is given by
questions.e: The line is y = x + 2. Points above it have larger y for the same x, so the region is y > x + 2; 'open' means the line itself is excluded, so ≥ is wrong. y > x − 2 is the region above a different line, with y-intercept −2.

questions.s: Which of the following is a corner point of the feasible region x ≥ 0, y ≥ 0, x + y ≤ 7, x − y ≤ 1?
questions.e: x + y = 7 and x − y = 1 meet where 2x = 8, at (4, 3). The corners are (0, 0), (1, 0), (4, 3) and (0, 7). (7, 0) violates x − y ≤ 1, (3, 4) lies on an edge but is not a corner, and (1, 7) violates x + y ≤ 7.

questions.s: The maximum value of z = 4x + 3y subject to x ≥ 0, y ≥ 0, x + y ≤ 7, x − y ≤ 1 is
questions.e: The corners are (0, 0), (1, 0), (4, 3) and (0, 7), where z = 0, 4, 16 + 9 = 25 and 21. The maximum is 25 at (4, 3). 28 would come from (7, 0), which is outside the region because 7 − 0 > 1.

questions.s: Usman mixes two feeds. Each kg of feed A gives 2 units of protein and 1 unit of vitamins and costs Rs 60; each kg of feed B gives 1 unit of protein and 2 units of vitamins and costs Rs 40. He needs at least 8 units of protein and 7 units of vitamins. The minimum cost is
questions.e: With x kg of A and y kg of B: 2x + y ≥ 8, x + 2y ≥ 7, x, y ≥ 0. The lines meet at (3, 2). Corners: (0, 8), (3, 2), (7, 0) cost Rs 320, Rs 260 and Rs 420, so the minimum is Rs 260. Rs 240 comes from (2, 3), which gives only 7 units of protein.

questions.s: In linear programming, the set of all points that satisfy every constraint is called
questions.e: The points satisfying all the constraints together form the feasible region (feasible solution set). The objective function is the expression being maximised or minimised, and the optimal point is the particular feasible point where it is best.

questions.s: The image (reflection) of the point (4, 1) in the line y = x + 1 is
questions.e: Write the line as x − y + 1 = 0; at (4, 1) it gives 4. Image: (x − 4)/1 = (y − 1)/(−1) = −2(4)/(1 + 1) = −4, so x = 0, y = 5. Check: the midpoint (2, 3) lies on the line. (2, 3) is only the foot of the perpendicular, and (−4, 9) forgets to divide by a² + b² = 2.

questions.s: The centre and radius of the circle (x − 3)² + (y + 4)² = 49 are
questions.e: Comparing with (x − h)² + (y − k)² = r² gives h = 3, k = −4 and r² = 49, so r = 7. The centre takes the opposite signs of the numbers inside the brackets, so (−3, 4) is a sign slip, and 49 is r², not r.

questions.s: The radius of the circle x² + y² + 4x − 10y − 7 = 0 is
questions.e: Here g = 2, f = −5 and c = −7, so r = √(g² + f² − c) = √(4 + 25 + 7) = √36 = 6. Using +c instead of −c gives √22, ignoring c gives √29, and 36 is r² without the square root.

questions.s: The equation of the circle with centre (−1, 2) and radius 3 is
questions.e: (x + 1)² + (y − 2)² = 9 expands to x² + 2x + 1 + y² − 4y + 4 = 9, that is x² + y² + 2x − 4y − 4 = 0. The option with −2x + 4y uses the centre (1, −2), and +4 comes from subtracting 9 − 5 the wrong way round.

questions.s: The equation of the circle whose diameter has end points (2, −3) and (−4, 5) is
questions.e: The centre is the midpoint (−1, 1). The diameter is √(6² + 8²) = 10, so the radius is 5 and the equation is (x + 1)² + (y − 1)² = 25. Writing 100 uses the diameter as the radius, and (−3, 4) is half the difference of the end points, not the midpoint.

questions.s: Which of the following points lies inside the circle x² + y² = 25?
questions.e: A point is inside when x² + y² < 25. For (−2, 4): 4 + 16 = 20 < 25, so it is inside. (3, 4) gives exactly 25, so it lies on the circle, while (5, 1) gives 26 and (−4, −4) gives 32, both outside.

questions.s: The point (1, k) lies inside the circle x² + y² − 2x − 4y − 4 = 0 if and only if
questions.e: Inside means S₁ < 0: 1 + k² − 2 − 4k − 4 < 0, so k² − 4k − 5 < 0, i.e. (k − 5)(k + 1) < 0, giving −1 < k < 5. The condition k < −1 or k > 5 is the outside region, and −5 < k < 1 comes from a sign slip in the factors.

questions.s: The equation of the tangent to the circle x² + y² = 25 at the point (3, −4) is
questions.e: For x² + y² = a² the tangent at (x₁, y₁) is xx₁ + yy₁ = a², so it is 3x − 4y = 25. Writing 3x + 4y = 25 drops the sign of y₁, and 3x − 4y = 5 uses a instead of a² on the right.

questions.s: The length of the tangent from the point (5, 3) to the circle x² + y² − 4x + 2y − 4 = 0 is
questions.e: The tangent length is √S₁ with S₁ = 25 + 9 − 20 + 6 − 4 = 16, so the length is 4. The value 16 is S₁ itself without the square root, and 2√6 comes from taking the constant as +4.

questions.s: The line y = 2x + c touches the circle x² + y² = 5 if c equals
questions.e: y = mx + c touches x² + y² = a² when c² = a²(1 + m²) = 5(1 + 4) = 25, so c = ±5. Taking c² = a² gives ±√5, and ±25 forgets to take the square root of c².

questions.s: The length of the chord cut off by the line x = 3 on the circle x² + y² = 25 is
questions.e: Putting x = 3 gives y² = 16, so y = ±4 and the chord joins (3, 4) and (3, −4), of length 8. The value 4 is only half the chord, and 10 is the diameter.

questions.s: The equation of the circle with centre (2, −3) that touches the x-axis is
questions.e: A circle touching the x-axis has radius equal to |y-coordinate of the centre| = 3, so (x − 2)² + (y + 3)² = 9, i.e. x² + y² − 4x + 6y + 4 = 0. The constant +9 gives radius 2, which is the circle touching the y-axis; the equation with no constant passes through the origin.

questions.s: The area enclosed by the circle x² + y² − 6x + 2y + 6 = 0 is
questions.e: g = −3, f = 1, c = 6, so r² = 9 + 1 − 6 = 4 and the area is πr² = 4π. 10π ignores c, 16π uses −c with the wrong sign, and 2π is πr without squaring.

questions.s: If the circle x² + y² + 4x − 6y + k = 0 has radius 5, then k is
questions.e: r² = g² + f² − c = 4 + 9 − k = 25, so k = −12. Writing 4 + 9 + k = 25 gives 12, a sign error in the radius formula.

questions.s: The equation x² + y² + 2gx + 2fy + c = 0 represents a real circle with non-zero radius when
questions.e: Completing squares gives (x + g)² + (y + f)² = g² + f² − c, and this is a real circle of positive radius only when g² + f² − c > 0. If it equals 0 the circle shrinks to a point, and if it is negative no real point satisfies the equation.

questions.s: Which of the following equations represents a circle?
questions.e: A circle needs equal coefficients of x² and y² and no xy term. Dividing 2x² + 2y² − 4x + 8y + 1 = 0 by 2 gives r² = 1 + 4 − ½ = 9/2 > 0, a real circle. Unequal coefficients (3 and 2) give an ellipse, opposite signs give a hyperbola, and an xy term rules out a circle.

questions.s: The equation of the circle with centre (3, −4) that passes through the origin is
questions.e: The radius is the distance from (3, −4) to (0, 0), which is 5. Then (x − 3)² + (y + 4)² = 25 gives x² + y² − 6x + 8y + 25 − 25 = 0, so the constant term vanishes. The option with −25 forgets that 9 + 16 cancels the 25.

questions.s: The circle x² + y² − 6x − 8y = 0 meets the x-axis at the origin and at the point
questions.e: On the x-axis y = 0, so x² − 6x = 0 and x = 0 or 6. The other point is (6, 0); (3, 0) is only the x-coordinate of the centre, and (8, 0) uses the y-coefficient.

questions.s: The radius of the circle passing through the points (0, 0), (4, 0) and (0, 6) is
questions.e: Through the origin, c = 0; (4, 0) gives 16 + 8g = 0, so g = −2, and (0, 6) gives 36 + 12f = 0, so f = −3. The centre is (2, 3) and r = √(4 + 9) = √13. 2√13 is the diameter, the hypotenuse joining (4, 0) and (0, 6).

questions.s: The circles x² + y² = 9 and x² + y² − 8x + 6y + 21 = 0
questions.e: The first has centre (0, 0), radius 3; the second has centre (4, −3) and radius √(16 + 9 − 21) = 2. The distance between centres is 5 = 3 + 2, so they touch externally. Internal touching would need the distance to equal 3 − 2 = 1.

questions.s: The length of the chord cut off by the line 3x + 4y = 10 on the circle x² + y² = 25 is
questions.e: The distance from the centre (0, 0) to the line is 10/5 = 2. Half the chord is √(25 − 4) = √21, so the chord is 2√21. √21 is only the half chord, and 2√29 adds 4 to 25 instead of subtracting.

questions.s: The line 3x − 4y + k = 0 touches the circle x² + y² − 2x − 4y − 4 = 0. The values of k are
questions.e: The centre is (1, 2) and r = √(1 + 4 + 4) = 3. Tangency needs |3 − 8 + k|/5 = 3, so |k − 5| = 15 and k = 20 or −10. ±15 treats the centre as the origin, and 10 or 0 comes from r = 1, taking the constant as +4.

questions.s: The equation of the normal to the circle x² + y² − 4x + 6y − 12 = 0 at the point (5, 1) is
questions.e: The normal passes through the centre (2, −3), so its slope is (1 + 3)/(5 − 2) = 4/3 and y − 1 = (4/3)(x − 5), i.e. 4x − 3y − 17 = 0. The line 3x + 4y − 19 = 0 has slope −3/4: it is the tangent at (5, 1), not the normal.

questions.s: The curve x = 3 + 5 cos θ, y = −2 + 5 sin θ is a circle with
questions.e: (x − 3)² + (y + 2)² = 25(cos²θ + sin²θ) = 25, so the centre is (3, −2) and the radius is 5. The parametric constants give the centre directly with their own signs, and 25 is r², not r.

questions.s: The circle concentric with x² + y² − 4x + 2y + 1 = 0 and passing through (5, 3) is
questions.e: Concentric circles share the centre (2, −1). The radius² is (5 − 2)² + (3 + 1)² = 25, so (x − 2)² + (y + 1)² = 25, i.e. x² + y² − 4x + 2y + 5 − 25 = 0, giving −20. The constant −25 forgets the 4 + 1 from expanding the brackets.

questions.s: The tangents to the circle x² + y² = 4 that are parallel to the line 3x + 4y = 1 are
questions.e: A parallel line is 3x + 4y = k, and tangency needs |k|/5 = 2, so k = ±10. ±20 uses r² = 4 instead of r = 2, and 4x − 3y = ±10 is perpendicular, not parallel, to the given line.

questions.s: The length of the common chord of the circles x² + y² = 25 and x² + y² − 6x − 8y + 15 = 0 is
questions.e: Subtracting the equations gives the common chord 6x + 8y − 40 = 0, i.e. 3x + 4y = 20. Its distance from the origin is 20/5 = 4, so the half chord is √(25 − 16) = 3 and the chord is 6. The value 3 is only half the chord, and 4 is the distance from the centre.

questions.s: A circle of radius 3 touches both coordinate axes and has its centre in the second quadrant. Its equation is
questions.e: In the second quadrant the centre is (−3, 3), so (x + 3)² + (y − 3)² = 9, which expands to x² + y² + 6x − 6y + 9 = 0. The equation with −6x + 6y has its centre (3, −3) in the fourth quadrant, and +18 forgets to subtract r² = 9.

questions.s: The number of tangents that can be drawn from the point (1, 1) to the circle x² + y² = 4 is
questions.e: S₁ = 1 + 1 − 4 = −2 < 0, so (1, 1) lies inside the circle and no tangent can be drawn from it. Two tangents exist only from an outside point, and exactly one from a point on the circle.

questions.s: The line y = x + c meets the circle x² + y² = 8 at two distinct points if and only if
questions.e: Two points need the distance from the centre to the line x − y + c = 0 to be less than the radius: |c|/√2 < 2√2, so |c| < 4. The range −2√2 < c < 2√2 forgets the √2 in the distance formula, and c < −4 or c > 4 is the case where the line misses the circle.

questions.s: The greatest distance of the origin from a point on the circle x² + y² − 2x + 4y − 20 = 0 is
questions.e: The centre is (1, −2) and r = √(1 + 4 + 20) = 5. The origin is inside (S₁ = −20 < 0), at distance √5 from the centre, so the farthest point is at 5 + √5. The value 5 − √5 is the least distance, and 10 is the diameter.

questions.s: The radius of the circle 3x² + 3y² − 12x + 18y − 9 = 0 is
questions.e: Divide by 3 first: x² + y² − 4x + 6y − 3 = 0, so g = −2, f = 3, c = −3 and r = √(4 + 9 + 3) = 4. √10 uses +c in place of −c, and 16 is r².

questions.s: The equation of the tangent to the circle x² + y² − 6x + 4y − 12 = 0 at the point (−1, 1) is
questions.e: The centre is (3, −2), so the radius to (−1, 1) has slope 3/(−4) = −3/4 and the tangent has slope 4/3. Then y − 1 = (4/3)(x + 1) gives 4x − 3y + 7 = 0. The line 3x + 4y − 1 = 0 has slope −3/4 and is the normal at that point.

questions.s: A circle has its centre on the line y = x and passes through the points (2, 0) and (0, 4). Its equation is
questions.e: Let the centre be (h, h). Equal distances give (h − 2)² + h² = h² + (h − 4)², so −4h + 4 = −8h + 16 and h = 3. Then r² = 1 + 9 = 10 and (x − 3)² + (y − 3)² = 10 gives x² + y² − 6x − 6y + 8 = 0. The circle x² + y² − 4x − 4y = 0 passes through (0, 4) but not through (2, 0).

questions.s: If the point (3, k) lies on the circle x² + y² = 25, then k equals
questions.e: 9 + k² = 25 gives k² = 16, so k = ±4. ±16 stops at k² without the square root, and ±5 is the radius.

questions.s: The shortest distance from the point (9, 7) to the circle x² + y² − 2x − 2y − 7 = 0 is
questions.e: The centre is (1, 1) and r = √(1 + 1 + 7) = 3. The point is √(8² + 6²) = 10 from the centre, so the nearest point of the circle is 10 − 3 = 7 away. 10 is the distance to the centre and 13 is the greatest distance.

questions.s: The circle x² + y² + 2x − 4y + k = 0 touches the y-axis when k equals
questions.e: The centre is (−1, 2), so touching the y-axis needs r = 1: 1 + 4 − k = 1, giving k = 4. Check: on x = 0, y² − 4y + 4 = 0 has the double root y = 2. Taking k = 1 makes the radius 2, which is the condition for touching the x-axis.

questions.s: A point P moves so that its distance from (0, 0) is always twice its distance from (3, 0). The locus of P is a circle with
questions.e: x² + y² = 4[(x − 3)² + y²] gives 3x² + 3y² − 24x + 36 = 0, i.e. x² + y² − 8x + 12 = 0. The centre is (4, 0) and r = √(16 − 12) = 2. Radius 4 ignores the constant term 12.

questions.s: The centre of the circle x² + y² − 10x = 0 is
questions.e: Here 2g = −10, so g = −5 and f = 0, and the centre (−g, −f) is (5, 0). The point (−5, 0) forgets to change the sign of g, and (10, 0) forgets to halve the coefficient.

questions.s: The focus of the parabola y² = 12x is
questions.e: Comparing with y² = 4ax gives 4a = 12, so a = 3 and the focus is (a, 0) = (3, 0). (12, 0) uses 4a as a, and (0, 3) belongs to x² = 12y.

questions.s: The directrix of the parabola x² = −8y is
questions.e: x² = −4ay with 4a = 8 gives a = 2; the parabola opens downwards with focus (0, −2), so the directrix is y = 2. The line y = −2 passes through the focus, which is on the other side of the vertex from the directrix.

questions.s: The length of the latus rectum of the parabola y² = −20x is
questions.e: The latus rectum of y² = ±4ax has length 4a, and here 4a = 20. The sign only shows that the parabola opens to the left; lengths are positive. 5 is a itself, and 10 is 2a, the semi latus rectum.

questions.s: The parabola with focus (0, 3) and directrix y = −3 is
questions.e: The vertex is midway between the focus and directrix, at the origin, with a = 3 and the axis along the y-axis, opening upwards. So x² = 4ay = 12y. x² = 6y uses 2a instead of 4a, and x² = −12y opens downwards, towards the directrix.

questions.s: The focus of the parabola y² − 4y − 8x + 20 = 0 is
questions.e: Complete the square: (y − 2)² = 8x − 16 = 8(x − 2). The vertex is (2, 2), 4a = 8 gives a = 2, and the parabola opens to the right, so the focus is (2 + 2, 2) = (4, 2). (2, 2) is the vertex, and (0, 2) lies on the directrix x = 0.

questions.s: A point P on the parabola y² = 8x is at distance 10 from the focus. The x-coordinate of P is
questions.e: For y² = 4ax the focal distance of (x, y) is x + a, because it equals the distance to the directrix x = −a. Here a = 2, so x + 2 = 10 and x = 8 (then y = ±8). 12 adds a instead of subtracting it, and 6 subtracts 2a instead of a.

questions.s: The axis of the parabola (x − 1)² = 4(y + 3) is
questions.e: The vertex is (1, −3) and the squared term is in x, so the parabola opens upwards and its axis is the vertical line through the vertex, x = 1. y = −3 is the tangent at the vertex, and x = −1 has the wrong sign.

questions.s: The parabola with vertex at the origin and axis along the x-axis that passes through (2, −4) is
questions.e: Take y² = 4ax: 16 = 4a(2) gives a = 2, so y² = 8x. x² = −y also passes through (2, −4) but its axis is the y-axis, and y² = 16x would need 16 = 32.

questions.s: The tangent of slope 2 to the parabola y² = 16x is
questions.e: y = mx + c touches y² = 4ax when c = a/m. Here a = 4 and m = 2, so c = 2 and the tangent is y = 2x + 2. y = 2x + 8 uses c = am, and y = 2x + 4 uses c = a.

questions.s: The end points of the latus rectum of the parabola x² = 16y are
questions.e: 4a = 16 gives a = 4, so the latus rectum lies on y = 4 and x² = 64 there, giving x = ±8. The end points are (±8, 4), and the length is 16 = 4a. (4, ±8) belongs to y² = 16x, with the axes swapped.

questions.s: The equation of the parabola with focus (2, 3) and directrix x = −4 is
questions.e: Distance to the focus equals distance to the directrix: (x − 2)² + (y − 3)² = (x + 4)², so (y − 3)² = 12x + 12 = 12(x + 1). The vertex (−1, 3) is midway and a = 3. Using 24 treats the focus-to-directrix distance 6 as a, when it is 2a.

questions.s: For every value of t, the point (3t², 6t) lies on the parabola
questions.e: y² = 36t² = 12(3t²) = 12x. This is the parametric form (at², 2at) of y² = 4ax with a = 3. y² = 3x takes the coefficient of t² as 4a.

questions.s: The directrix of the parabola x² + 4x − 8y + 12 = 0 is
questions.e: Complete the square: (x + 2)² = 8y − 8 = 8(y − 1). The vertex is (−2, 1), 4a = 8 gives a = 2, and the parabola opens upwards, so the directrix is y = 1 − 2 = −1. y = 3 is the level of the focus, and y = 1 is the tangent at the vertex.

questions.s: The eccentricity of every parabola is
questions.e: A parabola is the locus of points whose distance from the focus equals their distance from the directrix, so the ratio e is exactly 1. An ellipse has 0 < e < 1 (a circle e = 0), and a hyperbola has e > 1.

questions.s: If the parabola y² = 4ax passes through the point (3, 6), the length of its latus rectum is
questions.e: 36 = 4a(3) gives 4a = 12, which is the latus rectum length (a = 3). In fact (3, 6) is an end of the latus rectum, since x = a there. The value 3 is a, and 6 is only the semi latus rectum 2a.

questions.s: The parabola with vertex (1, 2) and focus (1, 5) is
questions.e: The focus is directly above the vertex at distance a = 3, so the parabola opens upwards: (x − 1)² = 4a(y − 2) = 12(y − 2). The form (y − 2)² = 12(x − 1) has a horizontal axis, and 20 uses the focus's y-coordinate 5 as a.

questions.s: The parabolas y² = 4x and x² = 4y meet at the origin and at a point P. The distance OP is
questions.e: From x² = 4y, y = x²/4; then x⁴/16 = 4x gives x³ = 64, so x = 4 and y = 4. P = (4, 4) and OP = √(16 + 16) = 4√2. The value 4 is only one coordinate of P.

questions.s: The line y = x + 1 and the parabola y² = 4x
questions.e: Substituting gives (x + 1)² = 4x, i.e. (x − 1)² = 0, a double root x = 1, so the line touches the parabola at (1, 2). This agrees with c = a/m = 1/1 = 1. The point (2, 1) has its coordinates swapped and does not lie on y² = 4x.

questions.s: The focus of the parabola y = x² − 4x + 7 is
questions.e: y = (x − 2)² + 3, so (x − 2)² = y − 3 = 4a(y − 3) with 4a = 1, a = 1/4. The vertex is (2, 3) and the parabola opens upwards, so the focus is (2, 3 + 1/4) = (2, 13/4). (2, 4) takes a = 1, and (2, 11/4) goes the wrong way from the vertex.

questions.s: Which of the following parabolas opens to the left?
questions.e: For y² = −6x, x = −y²/6 is never positive, so the curve lies to the left of the y-axis and opens left. x² = −6y opens downwards, and y² = 6x opens to the right.

questions.s: The foci of the ellipse x²/25 + y²/9 = 1 are
questions.e: a² = 25 and b² = 9 with the major axis along the x-axis, so c² = a² − b² = 16 and the foci are (±4, 0). (±√34, 0) adds a² and b², which is the rule for a hyperbola, and (±5, 0) are the vertices.

questions.s: The eccentricity of the ellipse x²/25 + y²/16 = 1 is
questions.e: c² = 25 − 16 = 9, so c = 3 and e = c/a = 3/5. 3/4 divides by b instead of a, and 5/3 is greater than 1, which is impossible for an ellipse.

questions.s: The length of the major axis of the ellipse 4x² + 9y² = 36 is
questions.e: Dividing by 36 gives x²/9 + y²/4 = 1, so a = 3 and the major axis is 2a = 6. The value 4 is the minor axis 2b, and 3 is only the semi-major axis.

questions.s: The length of the latus rectum of the ellipse x²/16 + y²/9 = 1 is
questions.e: For x²/a² + y²/b² = 1 with a > b the latus rectum is 2b²/a = 2(9)/4 = 9/2. 9/4 is b²/a, only half of it, and 32/3 swaps a and b.

questions.s: The ellipse with foci (±3, 0) and major axis of length 10 is
questions.e: 2a = 10 gives a = 5, c = 3, so b² = a² − c² = 16 and the ellipse is x²/25 + y²/16 = 1. x²/25 + y²/9 = 1 puts c² in place of b², and x²/100 + y²/91 = 1 uses the full major axis as a.

questions.s: The foci of the ellipse x²/9 + y²/25 = 1 are
questions.e: The larger denominator 25 is under y², so the major axis is the y-axis with a = 5, b = 3. c² = 25 − 9 = 16 and the foci are (0, ±4). (±4, 0) puts them on the minor axis.

questions.s: The directrices of the ellipse x²/36 + y²/20 = 1 are
questions.e: c² = 36 − 20 = 16, so c = 4 and e = 4/6 = 2/3. The directrices are x = ±a/e = ±6 ÷ (2/3) = ±9. x = ±4 passes through the foci and x = ±6 through the vertices.

questions.s: For any point P on the ellipse x²/49 + y²/24 = 1, the sum of the distances of P from the two foci is
questions.e: The focal distances of any point on an ellipse add up to the major axis 2a = 2(7) = 14. The value 10 is the distance 2c between the foci (c² = 49 − 24 = 25), and 4√6 is the minor axis 2b.

questions.s: An ellipse with centre at the origin and major axis along the x-axis has eccentricity 1/2 and latus rectum of length 6. Its equation is
questions.e: b² = a²(1 − e²) = 3a²/4, and 2b²/a = 6 gives 2(3a²/4)/a = 3a/2 = 6, so a = 4 and b² = 12. The ellipse is x²/16 + y²/12 = 1. x²/12 + y²/16 = 1 has its major axis along the y-axis, and x²/64 + y²/48 = 1 has latus rectum 12.

questions.s: The foci of the ellipse (x − 2)²/16 + (y + 1)²/9 = 1 are
questions.e: The centre is (2, −1) and the major axis is horizontal with a² = 16, b² = 9, so c = √7. The foci are c units either side of the centre: (2 ± √7, −1). (±√7, 0) forgets the shift of the centre, and 2 ± 5 uses √(a² + b²).

questions.s: The ellipse 9x² + 4y² − 18x + 16y − 11 = 0 has centre and length of major axis
questions.e: 9(x − 1)² − 9 + 4(y + 2)² − 16 = 11 gives 9(x − 1)² + 4(y + 2)² = 36, i.e. (x − 1)²/4 + (y + 2)²/9 = 1. The centre is (1, −2), and the major axis is vertical with a = 3, so its length is 6. The length 4 is the minor axis 2b.

questions.s: For the ellipse x²/a² + y²/b² = 1 with a > b and eccentricity e, which relation is correct?
questions.e: c = ae and c² = a² − b², so b² = a² − a²e² = a²(1 − e²). The form b² = a²(e² − 1) is the hyperbola relation, and a² = b²(1 − e²) would make a smaller than b.

questions.s: The minor axis of an ellipse is half as long as its major axis. Its eccentricity is
questions.e: b = a/2, so e² = 1 − b²/a² = 1 − 1/4 = 3/4 and e = √3/2. 3/4 is e² without the square root, and 1/2 is the ratio b/a, not e.

questions.s: The distance between the foci of an ellipse equals the length of its minor axis. The eccentricity of the ellipse is
questions.e: 2c = 2b gives c = b, so a² = b² + c² = 2c² and a = c√2. Then e = c/a = 1/√2. √3/2 would need b = a/2, which is a different condition.

questions.s: The point (2, 1) with respect to the ellipse x²/8 + y²/4 = 1 lies
questions.e: 4/8 + 1/4 = 3/4 < 1, so the point is inside. The foci are at (±2, 0), since c² = 8 − 4 = 4, so (2, 1) is not a focus; a value of exactly 1 would put it on the curve.

questions.s: The ellipse x²/a² + y²/9 = 1 passes through the point (4, 9/5). The value of a² is
questions.e: 16/a² + (81/25)/9 = 1 gives 16/a² + 9/25 = 1, so 16/a² = 16/25 and a² = 25. Taking a² = 16 forgets the y-term, which makes the left side larger than 1.

questions.s: The vertices of the ellipse x²/16 + y²/49 = 1 are
questions.e: 49 > 16 and 49 is under y², so the major axis is the y-axis with a = 7, and the vertices are (0, ±7). (±4, 0) are the ends of the minor axis, and (±7, 0) puts a on the wrong axis.

questions.s: The foci of the hyperbola x²/16 − y²/9 = 1 are
questions.e: For a hyperbola c² = a² + b² = 16 + 9 = 25, so c = 5 and the foci lie on the transverse (x) axis at (±5, 0). (±√7, 0) uses the ellipse rule a² − b², and (±4, 0) are the vertices.

questions.s: The asymptotes of the hyperbola x²/9 − y²/4 = 1 are
questions.e: The asymptotes of x²/a² − y²/b² = 1 are y = ±(b/a)x. Here a = 3 and b = 2, so y = ±(2/3)x. The slope 3/2 inverts the ratio, and 4/9 uses b²/a² instead of b/a.

questions.s: The eccentricity of the hyperbola x²/9 − y²/16 = 1 is
questions.e: c² = 9 + 16 = 25, so c = 5 and e = c/a = 5/3. 5/4 divides by b instead of a, and 3/5 is less than 1, which is impossible for a hyperbola.

questions.s: The length of the transverse axis of the hyperbola 9x² − 16y² = 144 is
questions.e: Dividing by 144 gives x²/16 − y²/9 = 1, so a = 4 and the transverse axis 2a = 8. The value 6 is the conjugate axis 2b, and 10 is the distance 2c between the foci.

questions.s: The length of the latus rectum of the hyperbola x²/4 − y²/12 = 1 is
questions.e: The latus rectum of x²/a² − y²/b² = 1 is 2b²/a = 2(12)/2 = 12. 6 is b²/a, only the semi latus rectum, and 24 forgets to divide by a.

questions.s: The eccentricity of the rectangular hyperbola x² − y² = 16 is
questions.e: Here a² = b² = 16, so c² = 32 and e = c/a = √32/4 = √2. Every rectangular hyperbola (a = b) has e = √2. The value 1 is the eccentricity of a parabola.

questions.s: The hyperbola with foci (±5, 0) and vertices (±3, 0) is
questions.e: a = 3 and c = 5, so b² = c² − a² = 16 and the hyperbola is x²/9 − y²/16 = 1. x²/16 − y²/9 = 1 swaps a² and b² and has vertices (±4, 0), and 34 adds c² and a².

questions.s: The foci of the hyperbola y²/16 − x²/9 = 1 are
questions.e: The positive term is in y, so the transverse axis is the y-axis. c² = 16 + 9 = 25, so the foci are (0, ±5). (±5, 0) puts them on the wrong axis, and (0, ±4) are the vertices.

questions.s: A hyperbola with centre at the origin and foci on the x-axis has eccentricity 2, and the distance between its foci is 16. Its equation is
questions.e: 2c = 16 gives c = 8, and e = c/a = 2 gives a = 4. Then b² = c² − a² = 64 − 16 = 48, so x²/16 − y²/48 = 1. x²/64 − y²/192 = 1 takes c = 16, and x²/16 − y²/64 = 1 uses c² as b².

questions.s: For any point P on the hyperbola x²/25 − y²/11 = 1, the difference of the distances of P from the two foci is
questions.e: For a hyperbola |PF₁ − PF₂| = 2a, the transverse axis, and a = 5 gives 10. The value 12 is 2c, the distance between the foci (c² = 25 + 11 = 36), and 2√11 is the conjugate axis.

questions.s: The directrices of the hyperbola x²/16 − y²/20 = 1 are
questions.e: c² = 16 + 20 = 36, so c = 6 and e = 6/4 = 3/2. The directrices are x = ±a/e = ±4 ÷ (3/2) = ±8/3, between the centre and the vertices. x = ±6 passes through the foci and x = ±4 through the vertices.

questions.s: A hyperbola with centre at the origin and transverse axis along the x-axis has asymptotes y = ±2x and passes through (3, 4). Its equation is
questions.e: b/a = 2 means b² = 4a², so the hyperbola is 4x² − y² = 4a². The point gives 36 − 16 = 20, so 4x² − y² = 20 (a² = 5, b² = 20). 2x² − y² = 2 passes through (3, 4) but has asymptotes y = ±√2 x, and 52 adds 36 and 16.

questions.s: The foci of the hyperbola (x − 1)²/9 − (y + 2)²/16 = 1 are
questions.e: The centre is (1, −2), the transverse axis is horizontal and c² = 9 + 16 = 25. The foci are 5 units either side of the centre: (6, −2) and (−4, −2). (4, −2) and (−2, −2) are the vertices, 3 units from the centre, and (±5, 0) ignores the shift.

questions.s: The equation x²/(9 − k) + y²/(5 − k) = 1 represents a hyperbola when
questions.e: A hyperbola needs the two denominators to have opposite signs: 9 − k > 0 and 5 − k < 0, so 5 < k < 9. For k < 5 both are positive (an ellipse), and for k > 9 both are negative, so no real point satisfies it.

questions.s: Which of the following equations represents a hyperbola?
questions.e: x² − 4y² = 4 is x²/4 − y²/1 = 1, with x² and y² terms of opposite signs, which is a hyperbola. x² + 4y² = 4 is an ellipse, and x² − 4y = 4 has only one squared term, so it is a parabola.

questions.s: A conic section has eccentricity 3/2. The conic is
questions.e: The eccentricity decides the type: e = 0 circle, 0 < e < 1 ellipse, e = 1 parabola, e > 1 hyperbola. Since 3/2 > 1, the conic is a hyperbola.

questions.s: The curve 4x² − 9y² − 8x − 36y − 68 = 0 is
questions.e: 4(x − 1)² − 4 − 9(y + 2)² + 36 − 68 = 0 gives 4(x − 1)² − 9(y + 2)² = 36, i.e. (x − 1)²/9 − (y + 2)²/4 = 1. Opposite signs make it a hyperbola, centred at (1, −2). The centre (−1, 2) takes the signs from the equation without changing them.

questions.s: If the point (k, 4) lies on the hyperbola x²/9 − y²/16 = 1, then k equals
questions.e: k²/9 − 16/16 = 1 gives k²/9 = 2, so k² = 18 and k = ±3√2. ±√2 forgets to multiply by 9, and ±3 comes from k²/9 − 1 = 0, dropping the right side.

questions.s: The acute angle between the asymptotes of the hyperbola x² − 3y² = 3 is
questions.e: x²/3 − y²/1 = 1 has asymptotes y = ±x/√3, which make angles of 30° and −30° with the x-axis. The angle between them is 60°. The answer 30° is the angle of one asymptote with the axis, not between the two lines.

questions.s: The curve x = 3 sec θ, y = 4 tan θ is
questions.e: sec θ = x/3 and tan θ = y/4, and sec²θ − tan²θ = 1 gives x²/9 − y²/16 = 1. The plus sign would come from cos θ and sin θ, which give an ellipse, and y²/16 − x²/9 = 1 has the signs reversed.

questions.s: The curve x = 2 cos θ, y = 4 sin θ is an ellipse whose foci are
questions.e: Eliminating θ gives x²/4 + y²/16 = 1, with the major axis along the y-axis (a = 4, b = 2). c² = 16 − 4 = 12, so the foci are (0, ±2√3). (0, ±4) are the vertices, and (0, ±2√5) adds 16 and 4.

questions.s: The tangents of slope 1 to the ellipse x²/9 + y²/4 = 1 are
questions.e: y = mx + c touches x²/a² + y²/b² = 1 when c² = a²m² + b² = 9 + 4 = 13, so c = ±√13. y = x ± √5 uses a²m² − b², which is the hyperbola condition, and ±13 forgets the square root.

questions.s: The tangents of slope 1 to the hyperbola x²/16 − y²/9 = 1 are
questions.e: y = mx + c touches x²/a² − y²/b² = 1 when c² = a²m² − b² = 16 − 9 = 7, so c = ±√7. y = x ± 5 uses the ellipse condition a²m² + b² = 25, and ±7 forgets the square root.

questions.s: The tangent to the ellipse x²/8 + y²/2 = 1 at the point (2, 1) is
questions.e: The tangent at (x₁, y₁) is xx₁/a² + yy₁/b² = 1, so 2x/8 + y/2 = 1, i.e. x + 2y = 4. Check: (2, 1) gives 2 + 2 = 4. The line 2x + y = 4 swaps the coefficients and does not have the right slope −1/2.

questions.s: The tangent to the parabola y² = 12x at the point (3, 6) is
questions.e: The tangent to y² = 4ax at (x₁, y₁) is yy₁ = 2a(x + x₁). With a = 3: 6y = 6(x + 3), so y = x + 3. The line x + y = 9 has slope −1 and is the normal at (3, 6), and y = 2x joins the point to the origin.

questions.s: A circle touches the x-axis at (3, 0) and passes through the point (1, 2). Its equation is
questions.e: Touching the x-axis at (3, 0) puts the centre at (3, k) with radius |k|. Then (1 − 3)² + (2 − k)² = k² gives 8 − 4k = 0, so k = 2 and (x − 3)² + (y − 2)² = 4, i.e. x² + y² − 6x − 4y + 9 = 0. The version with +4y has its centre below the axis and misses (1, 2).

questions.s: The angle between the two tangents drawn from the point (6, 8) to the circle x² + y² = 25 is
questions.e: The point is 10 from the centre and the radius is 5. Each tangent makes an angle α with the line to the centre, where sin α = 5/10 = 1/2, so α = 30° and the angle between the tangents is 2α = 60°. 30° is only half the angle.

questions.s: The line y = 4 and the circle x² + y² = 16
questions.e: Putting y = 4 gives x² = 0, a double root x = 0, so the line touches the circle at (0, 4). Equivalently, the distance of the line from the centre is 4, equal to the radius. (4, 0) is where the vertical tangent x = 4 touches.

questions.s: The circle with centre (1, 1) that touches the line 3x + 4y + 3 = 0 is
questions.e: The radius is the distance from the centre to the line: |3 + 4 + 3|/5 = 2. So (x − 1)² + (y − 1)² = 4, i.e. x² + y² − 2x − 2y − 2 = 0. The constant −98 comes from forgetting to divide by 5, giving r = 10.

questions.s: The circles x² + y² = 1 and x² + y² − 6x − 8y + k = 0 touch each other externally. The value of k is
questions.e: The second circle has centre (3, 4), at distance 5 from the origin, and radius √(25 − k). External touching needs 1 + √(25 − k) = 5, so 25 − k = 16 and k = 9. k = −11 gives radius 6, which is internal touching (6 − 1 = 5).

questions.s: The focus of the parabola y² = 8(x − 3) is
questions.e: The vertex is (3, 0) and 4a = 8 gives a = 2, opening to the right, so the focus is (3 + 2, 0) = (5, 0). (2, 0) ignores the shift of the vertex, and (11, 0) adds 4a instead of a.

questions.s: The area of the triangle formed by the vertex and the two end points of the latus rectum of the parabola y² = 8x is
questions.e: a = 2, so the latus rectum joins (2, 4) and (2, −4), a base of length 8 at distance 2 from the vertex (0, 0). The area is ½ × 8 × 2 = 8. 16 forgets the factor ½.

questions.s: The ellipse with foci (1, 2) and (7, 2) and major axis of length 10 is
questions.e: The centre is the midpoint (4, 2), c = 3 and a = 5, so b² = 25 − 9 = 16. The major axis is horizontal, giving (x − 4)²/25 + (y − 2)²/16 = 1. Putting 9 under (y − 2)² uses c² as b², and (x + 4), (y + 2) put the centre at (−4, −2).

questions.s: The hyperbola with vertices (±2, 0) and eccentricity 3/2 is
questions.e: a = 2 and c = ae = 3, so b² = c² − a² = 9 − 4 = 5 and the hyperbola is x²/4 − y²/5 = 1. Writing 9 for b² uses c² directly, and the plus sign gives an ellipse, which cannot have e > 1.

questions.s: The latus rectum of a hyperbola is half as long as its conjugate axis. The eccentricity of the hyperbola is
questions.e: 2b²/a = ½(2b) = b gives a = 2b. Then e² = 1 + b²/a² = 1 + 1/4 = 5/4, so e = √5/2. 5/4 is e² without the root, and √3/2 is less than 1, which is impossible for a hyperbola.

questions.s: P is a point on the ellipse x²/25 + y²/16 = 1 with x-coordinate 10/3. The distance of P from the focus (3, 0) is
questions.e: Here e = 3/5, and the focal distance from the focus (ae, 0) is a − ex = 5 − (3/5)(10/3) = 5 − 2 = 3. The distance from the other focus is a + ex = 7, and the two add to 2a = 10.

questions.s: Which of the following points lies on the circle x² + y² + 6x − 8y = 0?
questions.e: The constant term is 0, so (0, 0) satisfies the equation and the circle passes through the origin. (−3, 4) is the centre, not a point of the circle, and (3, −4) gives 9 + 16 + 18 + 32 = 75 ≠ 0.

questions.s: For the ellipse x²/a² + y²/b² = 1 with a > b, the length of the minor axis is
questions.e: The minor axis joins (0, b) and (0, −b), so its length is 2b. 2a is the major axis, and b is only the semi-minor axis.

questions.s: The asymptotes of the hyperbola x² − 4y² = 16 are
questions.e: Dividing by 16 gives x²/16 − y²/4 = 1, so a = 4, b = 2 and the asymptotes are y = ±(b/a)x = ±x/2. Equivalently, x² − 4y² = 0 factorises as (x − 2y)(x + 2y) = 0. y = ±2x inverts the ratio.

questions.s: An end of the latus rectum of the parabola x² = 4ay is the point (4, 2). The equation of the parabola is
questions.e: The latus rectum of x² = 4ay has ends (±2a, a), so a = 2 and 2a = 4 agree with (4, 2). Then 4a = 8 and the parabola is x² = 8y; check 16 = 8 × 2. x² = 16y takes a = 4 from the x-coordinate.

questions.s: The circle whose centre is the focus of the parabola y² = 8x and which passes through the vertex of the parabola is
questions.e: The focus is (2, 0) and the vertex is (0, 0), so r = 2 and (x − 2)² + y² = 4 gives x² + y² − 4x = 0. x² + y² − 8x = 0 has centre (4, 0), using 4a as a, and +4x puts the centre at (−2, 0).

questions.s: The length of the intercept made by the circle x² + y² − 10x + 4y + 9 = 0 on the x-axis is
questions.e: On y = 0, x² − 10x + 9 = 0 gives x = 1 or 9, so the intercept is 9 − 1 = 8. In general it is 2√(g² − c) = 2√(25 − 9) = 8. The value 4 is only √(g² − c), half the intercept.

questions.s: The latus rectum of an ellipse is one third of its major axis. The eccentricity of the ellipse is
questions.e: 2b²/a = (1/3)(2a) gives b² = a²/3. Then e² = 1 − b²/a² = 1 − 1/3 = 2/3, so e = √(2/3) = √6/3. 2/3 is e², and √3/3 = √(1/3) is b/a, not e.

questions.s: A point P moves so that |PF₁ − PF₂| = 4, where F₁ = (−4, 0) and F₂ = (4, 0). The locus of P is
questions.e: A constant difference of focal distances gives a hyperbola with 2a = 4, so a = 2, and c = 4. Then b² = c² − a² = 12, giving x²/4 − y²/12 = 1. The plus sign is an ellipse, which needs a constant sum, and 20 adds c² and a².

questions.s: Regarded as a conic section, a circle has eccentricity
questions.e: For an ellipse e = c/a with c² = a² − b²; a circle has a = b, so c = 0 and e = 0. An eccentricity of 1 belongs to a parabola, and √2 to a rectangular hyperbola.

questions.s: The centre of the circle x² + y² + 8x − 2y + 1 = 0 is
questions.e: 2g = 8 and 2f = −2 give g = 4, f = −1, and the centre is (−g, −f) = (−4, 1). (4, −1) forgets to change the signs, and (−8, 2) forgets to halve the coefficients.

questions.s: The focus of the parabola x² = 20y is
questions.e: x² = 4ay with 4a = 20 gives a = 5; the parabola opens upwards, so the focus is (0, 5). (5, 0) belongs to y² = 20x, and (0, −5) lies on the directrix y = −5.

questions.s: The eccentricity of the ellipse 9x² + 25y² = 225 is
questions.e: Dividing by 225 gives x²/25 + y²/9 = 1, so a = 5, b = 3 and c = √(25 − 9) = 4. Then e = c/a = 4/5. 3/5 is b/a, and 5/4 is greater than 1, impossible for an ellipse.

questions.s: The asymptotes of the hyperbola x²/25 − y²/16 = 1 are
questions.e: For x²/a² − y²/b² = 1 the asymptotes are y = ±(b/a)x, and here b/a = 4/5. 5/4 inverts the ratio and 16/25 uses b²/a².

questions.s: The tangent to the circle x² + y² = 13 at the point (2, −3) is
questions.e: The tangent to x² + y² = a² at (x₁, y₁) is xx₁ + yy₁ = a², giving 2x − 3y = 13. Check: 4 + 9 = 13. Using √13 on the right confuses a² with a, and 2x + 3y = 13 loses the sign of y₁.

questions.s: The circle on the segment joining (1, 2) and (5, 6) as diameter is
questions.e: Use (x − x₁)(x − x₂) + (y − y₁)(y − y₂) = 0: (x − 1)(x − 5) + (y − 2)(y − 6) = x² − 6x + 5 + y² − 8y + 12, so x² + y² − 6x − 8y + 17 = 0. The centre (3, 4) and r² = 25 − 17 = 8 agree with half the diameter, 2√2. The constant +25 would make the radius zero.

questions.s: The length of the tangent from the point (3, 4) to the circle x² + y² = 9 is
questions.e: The tangent length is √S₁ = √(9 + 16 − 9) = √16 = 4. The value 5 is the distance to the centre, and √34 adds the 9 instead of subtracting it.

questions.s: The length of the latus rectum of the ellipse x²/9 + y²/36 = 1 is
questions.e: The major axis is along the y-axis with a = 6 and b = 3, so the latus rectum is 2b²/a = 2(9)/6 = 3. 24 comes from 2a²/b, swapping the roles of a and b.

questions.s: The directrix of the parabola y² = 16x is
questions.e: 4a = 16 gives a = 4. The focus is (4, 0) and the directrix is the line x = −a = −4 on the other side of the vertex. x = 4 is the line through the focus, which contains the latus rectum.

questions.s: The foci of the hyperbola x²/7 − y²/9 = 1 are
questions.e: c² = a² + b² = 7 + 9 = 16, so c = 4, and the foci lie on the transverse (x) axis at (±4, 0). (±√2, 0) uses b² − a², and (±16, 0) forgets the square root.

questions.s: The parabola with vertex at the origin and focus (−3, 0) is
questions.e: The focus is on the negative x-axis with a = 3, so the parabola opens to the left: y² = −4ax = −12x. y² = −3x uses a in place of 4a, and x² = −12y has its focus on the y-axis.

questions.s: The line x + y = k touches the circle x² + y² = 8 when k equals
questions.e: Tangency needs the distance from the centre to equal the radius: |k|/√2 = 2√2, so |k| = 4. ±2√2 forgets the √2 in the denominator, and ±8 uses r² instead of r.

questions.s: Which of the following equations represents an ellipse?
questions.e: x²/4 + y²/9 = 1 has both squared terms positive with unequal denominators, so it is an ellipse (major axis along y). A minus sign between the squares gives a hyperbola, and y² = 4x is a parabola.

questions.s: The point (3, 2) with respect to the circle x² + y² − 4x + 2y − 11 = 0 lies
questions.e: S₁ = 9 + 4 − 12 + 4 − 11 = −6 < 0, so the point is inside. The centre is (2, −1), not (3, 2), and S₁ = 0 would be needed for the point to lie on the circle.

questions.s: An ellipse with centre at the origin has foci (±3, 0) and passes through the point (3, 16/5). Its equation is
questions.e: The point has x = c = 3, so it is an end of a latus rectum and b²/a = 16/5. With b² = a² − 9 this gives 5a² − 16a − 45 = 0, so a = 5 and b² = 16. The ellipse is x²/25 + y²/16 = 1. x²/25 + y²/9 = 1 has foci (±4, 0), not (±3, 0).

questions.s: The hyperbola with foci (0, ±6) and eccentricity 3/2 is
questions.e: The foci are on the y-axis, so the y² term is positive. c = 6 and e = c/a = 3/2 give a = 4, and b² = c² − a² = 36 − 16 = 20, so y²/16 − x²/20 = 1. x²/16 − y²/20 = 1 has its foci on the x-axis, and 36 under x² uses c² as b².

questions.s: The radius of the circle x² + y² − 2x + 6y + 1 = 0 is
questions.e: g = −1, f = 3, c = 1, so r = √(1 + 9 − 1) = √9 = 3. √10 ignores c, √11 adds c instead of subtracting, and 9 is r².

questions.s: The normal to the circle x² + y² = 25 at the point (4, 3) is
questions.e: Every normal of a circle passes through its centre, so the normal at (4, 3) is the line through (0, 0) and (4, 3): y = (3/4)x, i.e. 3x − 4y = 0. 4x + 3y = 25 is the tangent at (4, 3), and 4x − 3y = 0 does not pass through (4, 3).

questions.s: The line 2x − y + k = 0 touches the parabola y² = 8x. The value of k is
questions.e: Write the line as y = 2x + k, so m = 2. For y² = 4ax with a = 2, tangency needs k = a/m = 1. Check: (2x + 1)² = 8x gives 4x² − 4x + 1 = (2x − 1)² = 0, a double root. k = 4 uses am instead of a/m.

questions.s: The foci of an ellipse divide its major axis into three equal parts. The eccentricity of the ellipse is
